en: The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Volume One. The name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost; it is now appended to the Qin Records. Chapter One: Turning the Wheel of Dharma. **Chapter One: Turning the Wheel of Dharma** [The Buddha] addressed the assembly: "In the past, immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless eons ago, there was a world-system named *Vimalaprabhā* (Stainless Light). In that world-system, there was a buddha-land called *Ratnavibhūṣita* (Adorned with Jewels), which was vast, expansive, and exceedingly beautiful. Therein dwelt a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, named *Dīpaṅkara* (Lamp-Maker). At that time, there was a king named *Mahāprabha* (Great Radiance) who ruled over four continents. He possessed great power, wealth, and majesty, and his dominion extended over all the lands. The king had a son named *Sudarśana* (Good Appearance), who was endowed with a handsome countenance and virtuous qualities. He was skilled in various arts and crafts, and his wisdom was profound and far-reaching. At that time, the King Mahāprabha, having heard that the Tathāgata Dīpaṅkara had appeared in the world and was turning the wheel of the unsurpassed Dharma, felt great joy and resolved to go forth to meet him. Accompanied by his ministers, retinue, and the fourfold army, he set out from his capital.

Upon arriving at the presence of the Buddha, he prostrated himself at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times, and withdrew to sit to one side. The King then addressed the Buddha: 'World-Honored One, I have long desired to see you. May the World-Honored One, out of compassion for me, accept my humble invitation to reside in my palace. The Buddha accepted his request by remaining silent. Then, the Prince Sudarśana, seeing his father the king prostrate before the Buddha, felt a surge of faith. He approached the Buddha, prostrated himself at his feet, and said: 'World-Honored One, I too wish to renounce the world and follow the Buddha to cultivate the path. May the World-Honored One grant me permission to leave the household life. The Buddha said to the prince: 'Excellent, excellent! You have made a rare and difficult-to-find aspiration. If you can practice the Dharma with diligence, you shall surely attain the fruit of liberation. [The prince then] requested the precepts, received the full ordination, and diligently practiced meditation and wisdom. After many years, he attained the stage of a Śrāvaka Arhat. Subsequently, he returned to his father the king and preached the Dharma for him. The king, hearing this teaching, also developed a heart of renunciation and sought to leave the household life. However, his ministers and subjects obstructed him, saying: 'Your Majesty, the kingdom depends upon you. How can you abandon us to become a monk? The king replied: 'I have already entrusted the affairs of state to my son. You need not worry about me. With these words, the king went forth to follow the Buddha. At that time, the Tathāgata Dīpaṅkara, knowing the roots of merit of the King Mahāprabha and his son, turned the wheel of the Dharma for them. Through this turning of the wheel, they both attained the realization of the Dharma and were established in the stage of non-retrogression. Thus ends the first chapter of the *Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, titled "Turning the Wheel of Dharma."
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of sixty-two thousand bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats—whose outflows were exhausted, who had destroyed all fetters of existence, and had attained mastery; whose minds were well-liberated and whose wisdom was well-liberated; who were like tamed elephant kings; who had done what was to be done, laid down the heavy burden, achieved their own benefit, brought an end to the cycle of coming and going, and having attained right knowledge, had gained mastery over their minds and reached the further shore—with the sole exception of the elder Ānanda.

There were eight million four hundred thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas present, with Maitreya at their head; they had all attained dhāraṇīs, the patience of non-arising, and samādhi, and they delighted in dwelling in emptiness and stillness, all being non-retrogressive.
The Brahmā who is the Lord of the Sahā World was accompanied by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Brahmās;

the Son of Heaven of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin realm was accompanied by eighty hundred thousand Sons of Heaven of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin realm; the Son of Heaven of the Nirmāṇarati realm was accompanied by seventy hundred thousand Sons of Heaven of the Nirmāṇarati realm;
and the Son of Heaven of the Tuṣita realm was accompanied by sixty hundred thousand [Sons of Heaven] of the Tuṣita realm.
The Son of Heaven was accompanied by them: the Suyāma deva-putra was accompanied by seventy-two hundred thousand Suyāma deva-putras;
Śakra-devendra was accompanied by eight hundred thousand gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven;
Vaiśravaṇa, King of the Gods, was accompanied by his retinue of one hundred thousand yakṣas; and Virūḍhaka was accompanied by his retinue.
A thousand kumbhāṇḍas were together with him; Virūpākṣa was together with his retinue of a thousand nāgas;
and Dhṛtarāṣṭra was each accompanied by his own retinue of a thousand nāga kings.
At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by such leaders as these—all of whom sought the Mahāyāna and practiced the six pāramitās.

Having abandoned the four inverted views, his bright wisdom shone forth as he preached the Dharma based on the Four Noble Truths, causing all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas to attain various samādhis. By means of these samādhis, they transcended the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; by means of these samādhis, they attained firm and unshakable anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Vision, the Bodhisattva Varuṇadeva, the Bodhisattva Siṃhamati, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Illumination, and ten thousand other such Bodhisattvas, all rose from their seats, adjusted their robes, and turned toward the southeast. With their right knees touching the ground, they joined their palms in reverence, gazed with eyes full of joyful exultation, and spoke these words:

“Homage, homage to the Lotus-Supreme Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha! Not long after attaining Buddhahood, you have manifested great supernormal powers, inspiring countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to bring their roots of goodness to fulfillment and attain non-retrogression in Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jewel Radiance rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

For what reason did the Bodhisattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Vision, the Bodhisattva Varuṇa, the Bodhisattva Lion-Mind, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Illumination, and these ten thousand Bodhisattvas, all abandon the Dharma taught by the World-Honored One, rise from their seats, adjust their robes, face southeast, kneel with their right knees on the ground, join their palms in reverence, and with eyes gazing with joyful exultation, speak these words:

"Homage, homage to the Lotus-Supreme Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha! It is most rare that, not long after attaining Buddhahood, you have manifested great supernormal powers and auspicious responses to encourage and develop the roots of goodness in countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings."
"How far away from here is the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara?
And how much time has passed since he attained anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi?"
What is the name of the world of the Tathāgata Padmottara?
How is that land adorned, and by what means is it embellished?
By what means does the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara manifest great supernormal powers?

By what causes and conditions do some bodhisattvas see the present Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the countless other worlds of the ten directions, and furthermore see the supernatural powers manifested by those Buddhas, while we do not see them?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Jewel-Light Illumination, saying:
"Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!"
Your eloquence is most excellent, and what you have asked is wise and skillful.

You, son of good family, have questioned the Tathāgata on such a matter for the sake of bringing to fruition the roots of goodness of immeasurable billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings; you have thus inquired about the supernatural powers manifested by the Tathāgata Padmottara and the adornments of his buddha-field.
"You, son of good family!
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well!"
"I shall speak for your sake. "Indeed,
World-Honored One!"
“Bodhisattva Ratnaprabhāsa, listen to what the Buddha has said.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnaprabhāsa, saying: “Good son!
To the southeast, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of buddha-fields from this buddha-land, there is a world named Lotus.

It is adorned with various exquisite ornaments and strewn with many kinds of famous flowers; diverse wonderful fragrances fill the world. Adorned with jewel trees and many precious mountains, its ground is made of lapis lazuli, and it is filled with bodhisattvas whose sounds of the Dharma never cease.

That lapis lazuli ground is soft and exquisite, like celestial garments; when one treads upon it with the foot, it sinks down four inches, and when the foot is lifted, it returns to its original state;
it is filled with many lotus flowers.
The rows of trees made of the seven treasures were seven yojanas high, and from these jeweled trees hung various celestial garments.
The devas played music that was soft, exquisite, and wonderful.
Upon the trees, flocks of birds produced the sounds of the teachings on the faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, and the path.
The leaves of the various jewel trees rub against one another, producing sounds that surpass the five kinds of celestial music.
The exquisite fragrance emitted by each individual jewel tree pervades a thousand yojanas.

From the various jewel trees hung celestial necklaces; between each tree stood a terrace made of the seven treasures, five hundred yojanas high and one hundred yojanas wide, with windows on all four sides surrounding the terrace.

The natural pond water is eighty yojanas long and fifty yojanas wide; on all four sides of the pond are stairways made of the seven treasures, and water lilies and blue lotuses completely cover the surface of the water, each individual lotus being one yojana in width.

Upon the various flower pedestals, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are born; at the time of the first watch of the night, they are born upon the flower pedestals and sit cross-legged, experiencing the bliss of liberation and rejoicing throughout the night.

When dawn approaches, gentle, fragrant, and pleasant breezes blow from the four directions, causing the flowers to bloom. Those bodhisattvas arise from samādhi, relinquish their bliss of liberation, descend from the flower pedestals, and ascend to the various jeweled terraces. There, they sit cross-legged upon seats made of the seven precious substances to listen to and receive the Dharma.

On all four sides of the jeweled terraces surrounding the various trees stood Mounts of Purple-Golden Jewels, twenty yojanas high and three yojanas wide. Upon these mountains were countless hundreds of thousands of sun-crystals, moon-crystals, king-sapphire, great-sapphire, and bright-moon-jewels; everywhere they manifested the radiance of the Buddha Padmottara, and the mountain jewels and the Buddha’s light shone universally throughout the Lotus World.

The wondrous light is constant and pervasive, without distinction between day and night; though there is no sun or moon, one does not perceive the arrival of night. When the lotus flowers close and the cries of the birds cease, it is by these signs that night is known.

Upon those mountains are pavilions made of deep-blue lapis lazuli, sixty yojanas high and twenty yojanas wide. The pavilions are surrounded by windows made of the seven precious gems. Within these pavilions are thrones made of the seven precious gems, upon which Bodhisattvas bound for their final birth sit to listen to the Dharma.
“Good son! In the Lotus World, the Bodhi tree is named Indra; it is three thousand five hundred yojanas high, with branches and leaves spreading five thousand yojanas.

Beneath that Bodhi tree is a lotus flower five hundred yojanas high, with a stem of lapis lazuli and petals of gold. There are hundreds of thousands of millions of them, each five hundred yojanas long, with pedestals made of the seven jewels and filaments of agate, ten yojanas high and seven yojanas wide.”
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara attained anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi upon that lotus last night.
Around his seat of enlightenment, there were flower seats upon which all bodhisattvas were seated, observing the Tathāgata Padmottara manifesting great supernormal powers.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ratnaprabhāsa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"How does the Tathāgata Padmottara manifest such great supernormal powers?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnāvabhāsa, saying:

"The Tathāgata Padmottara attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi during the final watch of last night. That very night, as dawn approached, he manifested these supernormal powers, manifesting transformation bodies that reached as far as the Brahma heavens. From the *uṣṇīṣa* on his crown, he emitted sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of rays of light, which illuminated the regions above, passing through as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in a Buddha-world."

At that time, the bodhisattvas from the upper direction looked down upon the lower direction and saw that the Great Iron Ring Mountains, the Small Iron Ring Mountains, and the Black Mountains could not obstruct them.

Among the great bodhisattvas in all the worlds who have received the prediction of enlightenment, some have attained samādhi, some have attained dhāraṇī, some have attained kṣānti, some have transcended the stages, and some have reached the stage of being born only once more before attaining buddhahood.

All the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas beheld the radiance; with hands joined in reverent salutation, they gazed upon the body of the Tathāgata atop the lotus flower, seeing the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor characteristics with which he was adorned.
They also saw the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the adornments of the buddha-field of the Lotus World.
Having seen this, they were filled with joy and all gave rise to wholesome minds.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, each left their own lands and, by means of their supernormal powers, arrived at the Lotus World to make offerings to, revere, and attend upon the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara.

“Good son! The Tathāgata Padmottara, seeing the great assembly gathered, manifested the mark of the broad and long tongue, which completely covered the assembly and the four continents, as he walked, stood, sat, and remained upon this seat.”
The bodhisattvas all arose from their samādhis and made offerings to the Tathāgata Padmottara.
"O son of good family!

The Tathāgata Padmottara withdrew his supernatural manifestation of the tongue, and again emitted from each and every pore of his body sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of rays of light, which universally illuminated as many lands in each of the ten directions as there are atoms in a buddha-world."
Among the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in all those lands, there were those who had received predictions of enlightenment and those who had attained samādhi; these are described briefly.

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each departed from their own buddha-fields and, by means of their supernormal powers, arrived at the Lotus World to make offerings, pay respect to, and attend upon the Tathāgata Padmottara.

“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Padmottara withdrew his supernormal powers and, for the sake of the great assembly of all bodhisattvas, turned the wheel of the true Dharma of non-retrogression, bringing benefit to many. Out of compassion for the world, he acted for the benefit, peace, and happiness of gods and humans, so as to bring the Mahāyāna to fulfillment.”

Chapter 2: Entering the Gate of Dhāraṇīs. From the *Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, Chapter Two: Entering the Gate of Dhāraṇīs. At that time, the Bodhisattva Ratnāvabhāsa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
How is day and night distinguished in the Lotus World?
What sounds are heard there?
And what are the physical characteristics of those sentient beings?
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnāvabhāsa, saying: "Good son!
In that Lotus World, the lotuses close and the cries of the various birds cease;
When the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas sport in samādhi and experience the joy and bliss of liberation, this constitutes their night.

When the wind blows and flowers bloom, when the various birds sing in harmony, when a rain of diverse named flowers falls, and when soft breezes from the four directions touch them with most wondrous sounds, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas arise from samādhi; then the Buddha Padmottara expounds for the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the Dharma-treasury that transcends that of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas—this constitutes their day.

“Good son! Among them, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas constantly hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṅgha, the sound of cessation, the sound of the unconditioned, the sound of the pāramitās, the sound of the powers, the sound of the fearlessnesses, the sound of the superknowledges, the sound of non-action, the sound of non-arising, the sound of non-extinction, the sound of tranquility, the sound of stillness, the sound of detachment, the sound of great loving-kindness, the sound of great compassion, the sound of non-arising, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of receiving empowerment, and the sound of pure bodhisattvas.”
Those bodhisattvas hear such sounds as these, which never cease.
Furthermore, son of good family!

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the Lotus World, whether already born or yet to be born there, all possess the thirty-two marks and emit light for one yojana; furthermore, until they attain buddhahood, they do not fall into the evil realms.

All those Bodhisattvas possess a mind moistened by loving-kindness, an unclouded mind, a disciplined mind, a tranquil mind, a patient mind, a concentrated mind, a pure mind, an unobstructed mind, a clean mind, a dustless mind, a virtuous mind, a mind of Dharma-joy, a mind that eliminates the fetters of all sentient beings, a mind like the earth, a mind that does not delight in worldly speech, a mind that delights in supramundane speech, a mind that seeks all wholesome dharmas, a mind of cessation, a mind that removes old age, sickness, and death, a true mind, a mind that burns away all fetters, a mind that extinguishes all sensations, and a mind that does not disparage any dharma.

The power of intention; the power of action; the power of causes and conditions; the power of aspiration; the power of karmic conduct; the power of severance; the power of roots of goodness; the power of vows; the power of hearing; the power of precepts; the power of giving; the power of patience; the power of diligence; the power of concentration; the power of wisdom; the power of tranquility; the power of insight; the power of supernormal faculties; the power of mindfulness; the power of bodhi; the power of destroying all Māras; the power of subduing all external disputants through the same Dharma; and the power of destroying all fetters.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of that Lotus World—those who have been born there and those yet to be born—have all already approached and served immeasurable hundreds of thousands of buddhas, planting various roots of goodness.

Furthermore, the bodhisattvas born or yet to be born in the Lotus World take the joy of meditation as their food, as well as the food of Dharma and the food of fragrance; they are like the Brahmā gods, for whom there is no solid food.
Within that world, there is not even the name of any unwholesome thing, nor are there any women, nor is there even the sound of them.
There is no sound of any suffering, nor of love or hatred; even the sounds of fetters and afflictions are absent, as are the sounds of conditioned phenomena.
There is no darkness, no foul odors or impurities, and neither body nor mind experiences fatigue.
There are no sounds of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, or animals, nor are there even provisional names for them.
It is free from thorns, brambles, pits, and gravel;
it has no lamps, nor sun, moon, or stars;
it has no great ocean, nor Mount Sumeru, the Cakravāḍa Mountains, the Mahācakravāḍa Mountains, the barrier mountains, the Black Mountains, or any other terrestrial mountains.
There is no sound of clouds or rain, no sound of violent winds, no sounds of any of the evil realms, and no sounds of calamities.
In that Lotus World, the light of the Buddha, the light of the bodhisattvas, the light of mani jewels, the light of precious gems, and wondrous lights shine everywhere throughout it.
“There is a bird named Sahakāra, each of which utters the soft and gentle sounds of the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, and the path.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ratnaprabhāsa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
What are the dimensions of that Lotus World?
Since the Tathāgata Padmottara attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* last night, how long will he remain in the world to preach the Dharma and transform sentient beings?
After his parinirvāṇa, for how long will the True Dharma remain in the world?
For how long will those bodhisattvas who have already been born or are yet to be born in that Lotus World remain in the world?
And for what purpose do those bodhisattvas behold the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and make offerings to the Saṅgha?
"Will this not be for long?
What was the previous name of the Lotus World?
How much time has elapsed since the previous Buddha passed into parinirvāṇa, before the Tathāgata Padmottara subsequently attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
"For what reason, while some see the supernatural transformations manifested by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in other worlds throughout the ten directions,
others do not? The Buddha said, "Good son!

Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, is sixty-eight thousand yojanas high and eighty-four thousand yojanas broad. Suppose there were a person of heroic and powerful strength who, by the power of samādhi, could crush Mount Sumeru into pieces as small as mustard seeds such that no one could count them—except for the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā).

Taking each mustard seed to represent a set of four continents (cāturdvīpaka), and exhausting all these mustard seeds to constitute a Lotus World (Padmāvatī-lokadhātu), such worlds would be filled with Bodhisattvas, just as the Land of Peace and Bliss (Sukhāvatī) is completely filled with Bodhisattvas.
“Good son! The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara has a lifespan of thirty minor kalpas, during which he dwells in the world, preaching the Dharma to teach and transform sentient beings.”

“Good son! After the Tathāgata Padmottara has entered parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for ten minor kalpas. In that Lotus World, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have been born or will be born shall have a lifespan of forty minor kalpas.”
“Good son! The Lotus World was formerly named Candana; its land was adorned and its sentient beings were pure, yet none were as [excellent] as they are now. Good son!”

At that time, in the world-system Candana, there was a Buddha named Candrottara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, up to Buddha, Bhagavān. That Buddha also remained in the world for thirty intermediate kalpas teaching the Dharma. When he was about to enter parinirvāṇa, a bodhisattva departed for another buddha-field due to his original vow; the others each thought to themselves:
"In the middle watch of this very night, Candrottara Tathāgata shall enter nirvāṇa."
After the Blessed One has entered parinirvāṇa, we shall uphold the True Dharma for ten intermediate kalpas.
Who will, after the extinction of the True Dharma, next attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?

At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Gaganamudrā. Because of his original vow, the Tathāgata Candrottara immediately bestowed upon him the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, saying:
"O sons of good family!..."

After my parinirvāṇa, during the ten intermediate kalpas that the True Dharma remains in the world, the True Dharma will be extinguished at the first watch of the night; immediately thereafter, in the final watch of the night, this bodhisattva shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, named Padmottara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, up to Buddha, Bhagavat.

At that time, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas went to the place where the Tathāgata Candrottara was. All those bodhisattvas, through the power of their vows and various bodhisattva supernormal powers, made offerings to the Tathāgata Candrottara with sincere hearts; they circumambulated the Buddha three times and then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
“We wish to enter the samādhi of the mind’s cessation and non-contention for ten minor kalpas. “Good son!
At that time, the Tathāgata Candrottara addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā, saying these words:”
“You, son of good family!
Receive this Dharani-door of Entering All Compassion.
It was taught by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past for the sake of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who have been invested as Dharma-Prince Heirs.”

The Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in all worlds throughout the ten directions, who now abide in the world preaching the Dharma and transforming sentient beings—they too have preached this for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who have received their office as Dharma-Princes.

Furthermore, the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones of the future shall also preach this "Entrance into All Compassion Dhāraṇī Gate" for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who receive their office as Dharma-Princes.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
"Cālinī Mahācālinī"
Kṣi kṣi re re kṣi tri-pada mahā-tripada-tīkṣṇa-āditya-cchinda kṣi.
Tā-lè-luó-jià tā-chì ā-sì-mó-jia-sì shī-lí-mí.
Lide li luoqi mahaloqi shami du luo shami shayemoti yu ti she lu lou nieqie tuo ni amou lei moulu bolichen ni.
Māra-sthita-vijitaraśmi-nirmite-tat-pariśuddhe.
Abhitiṣaye mucāne brahmayoghe.
"Raṇe danda viḍhe viḍhe vārudame ni garaha badhina dharmabadhina saṃgha rahe rakṣa dharmabadhina. "This is the liberation phrase of the four foundations of mindfulness (catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni)."
“*Buddhaparākāśe amamaime ma-ma-acchi aṭṭhe aṭṭha-niṭṭhi-loka-ṇiṭṭhimuṇate dhamma-parivane.* This is the liberation phrase of the four noble lineages.”

“*Vasa-ti-vaṇe-dāre-dhāra-pati-nyāyate-mu-be-mu-va-para-be-mite-le | Su-ma-pate | Kṣante-kṣite | Garu-naye-udī-cakre-pi-le-te-u-kaṃ-taṃ | Saṃpaṇe | A-lekhi-va-ra-li-kha-gi-kha-ri-a-mule-mu-la-śu-te.*” “These are the phrases of liberation for the four fearlessnesses.”

“*Tatphara āgara phara ani phara nila phara trimukta amukta nemukta | Abhi lio abhimati bane bilaphara āyana te abhichi te abhichi | Ullunda cūla dūlana ākṣe samaye ti ta bhapate bhadate bhasabha lokaku adaka le akale | Prida abusa le cheda mate visaga rava te apalaka phara.*” “These are the four protective phrases of liberation.”

“*Jalita aniśe rāpavata pūṅge itaṃ phaleṇiye māphalaṃ samudatana ya vibhuśe | paśi sumārṇa anumatu akumatu citthabhati medatrattha dhaśaparavibharavatha | iśacitta sunikhamati na madeti ākhu ga adhi | dauṣṇaṃ sate madeti parāñca budha | phulubha parāhale.*” “This is the liberation-phrase of the four right efforts (*catvāri samyakprahāṇāni*)."

"Anirmale malmale manite mamane jvale jvāle tiṣṭha me śame śamita-bhiṣaṇite mudite uttara-tṛṣṇe saṃtṛṣṇe saṃmasaṃtṛṣṇe kṣaye akṣaye akṣaya-nirghoṣe śame siddhe dhāraṇi-aloka-vaśe harada-nava-rade haraṣmi-vade jana-vade nilu-vade milu-vade kṣayani arisa niluka-parāti-paṇidari-saṇi. "These are the phrases for the four analytical knowledges and liberation."

“*Cacau akhāśne arīṣaṇe jana-khu-ga-du-du-parāva-sate sādya-dri-riya-bu-mate kālante sa-sa-pava pama-sape parata-phakha-ni-gale guka-da-vadane loka-anudari-śana-vi-bhu.*” “These are the liberation-words of the four bases of psychic power (*catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ*)."

“*Acchale budhi dādhapacale bane khillanasiddhikamgaviḍini ci sapicchi parika siri sumiñcadhiṣṭhācācā acācale apale vicivale pule parācācale parāvale anaya abhyasike kagārami parāvavidhe | kārami nicake gālakārami nadyute.*” “This is the phrase for the manifestation of the faculties and powers (*indriya-bala*).”

“*Pūṣe pūṣe, duṣpārihāre, apabhāṣye, lūzile, cikaralekṣe, asama-siddhite, dite, male, male, ghuṭa-śiṣle, lokasā-vijñāne, nayaje, kili-nidhe, tsa-yaṇte, sa-śrī-dhana.*” “These are the phrases for liberation concerning the seven factors of enlightenment.”

“Cakrāvaśivati ca, śre, cakrādare dare ca średare mudre he re he re dare, aluṣpadi hūhūre yatha vitaga-pi vare yatha gani yatha palinca ti-ti-riśayatha vaya-huli-riśa. “The sound of truth, the sound of darkness, the sound of diligence, the sound of concentration, the sound of morality, the sound of meditative absorption, the sound of wisdom, the sound of liberation, the sound of the knowledge and vision of liberation, the sound of the constellations, the sound of the moon, and the sound of the sun.”
Such phrases as these were spoken by the Tathāgata:
Aṇḍa, Mīla, Buda, Sambuddha, Abuda.
Dandimaka vandati vandate vandani vande gamani arapathārapathānta le.
Mandāravatāraṇa-druma-mukhara-nirmocani-saparā.
Muciṭiṅga nepaccha gagaṇe nūnam nilapabbate naṭṭhe naṭṭhapade cicciṭi cicciṭi.
Te-te-tou-mo-yu-po-yi-ju-qie-cheng-qi-mo-po-lei-mo-lei-he-duo-ning-po-jin-lu-pi-di-pin-lei.
Pinlei yusha lei shaluo niduoluo ning boluopo.
Devāraṇa-caye-vithūthuma-bharaku-mabharahama-cariṇa-indrā-paṇiti-titira-senima-heśi-paralāra-ṇivama-carmie-arani.
Mīyika mūlaka ruru śicā nicca rāpha jiṃba āraśūle sarva śūraṇa aparāṇa.

Anāgatiṃ ca pratyutpannām atītāṃ ca gatiṃ jñāsyati | yāvat saṃvartakalpam api vivartakalpam api saṃvartavivartakalpam api anekān api saṃvartavivartakalpān anusmarati | amuṣminn ātmabhāve evaṃnāmaivaṃjātya evaṃgotra evamāhāra evaṃsukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī evaṃdīrghāyur evaṃcirasthitika evamāyuṣparyantaḥ | so ’haṃ tasmāt sthānāc cyutaḥ amutropapannaḥ | tasmād api cyutaḥ amutropapannaḥ | tasmād api cyutaḥ ihopapanna iti | sākāraṃ soddeśam anekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsam anusmarati || He shall know the future, the present, and the past course [of beings]. He recollects even a kalpa of dissolution, a kalpa of evolution, a kalpa of both dissolution and evolution, and even many kalpas of dissolution and evolution: "In that state of existence, I had such a name, such a birth, such a clan, such food, such experiences of pleasure and pain, such a long life, such a duration, and such a limit to my lifespan. Passing away from that place, I was reborn there; passing away from there as well, I was reborn there; and passing away from there, I was reborn here. Thus he recollects his manifold former abodes with their modes and details.
*Kamade buddhe śikhite dhāraṇīmukhe.* "This is the liberation-phrase of the Ten Powers. Chapter Three:

The Dhāraṇī for Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge (*Sarvākārajñatācaryāpraveśa-dhāraṇī*) At that time, when the World-Honored One was about to proclaim these phrases of the gateway to the dhāraṇī for entering the practice of all-knowledge, the great earth of this trichiliocosm shook in six ways, trembling violently and emitting a great sound; it surged and subsided, manifesting such radiance that its wondrous light pervaded worlds beyond number as many as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions.

At that time, Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, and the Great Iron Ring Mountains did not obstruct his vision; the countless worlds of the ten directions appeared as level as the palm of a hand, and he dwelt within those countless worlds of the ten directions.

There were bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had attained samādhi, dhāraṇī, and patience; riding upon the power of the Tathāgata, they suddenly vanished from their respective lands and came to this Sahā world. Arriving at Vulture Peak Mountain, they went to where the World-Honored One was, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, and honored the World-Honored One with various and immeasurable bodhisattva supernormal powers. Each sat to one side to listen to this "Dhāraṇī Door of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge."

Countless devas from the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm came to where the Buddha was in order to hear this dharani gate of entering the practice of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).
Countless nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, and piśācas went to Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain and approached the World-Honored One in order to hear this dhāraṇī gate of entering the practice of all-knowledge.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas gathered here see everywhere the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara in the world Padmāvatī, surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One began to preach this Dharani Gate of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge.

Seventy-two Ganges-sands of Bodhisattva-Mahasattvas attained this dharani; they beheld the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in countless worlds throughout the ten directions, as well as the magnificent adornments of those Buddha-worlds, attaining what they had never experienced before.
Having made offerings to the Buddha through the power of the Bodhisattva’s vows and supernormal knowledges, the Buddha said: “Good son!

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates this dharani-door of the practice for entering all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), they will attain eighty-four thousand dharani-doors, seventy-two thousand samādhi-doors, and sixty thousand dharma-doors.”
Once the Bodhisattva has attained this dhāraṇī, he attains great loving-kindness and great compassion.

Having attained this dhāraṇī, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva awakens to the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment, attains all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), and therein fully encompasses all Buddha-dharmas.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have truly awakened to this dhāraṇī and preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, rather than entering nirvāṇa prematurely. "Good son!

You should know that it is through the majestic power of this 'Dhāraṇī Door of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge' that the great earth trembles and wondrous light shines forth, pervading immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-worlds."

By means of this wondrous light, immeasurable and boundless Buddha-worlds were illuminated, causing immeasurable and boundless Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas to come to this land in order to hear this Dharani-door of entering the practice of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).

In this entire Sahā world—with its immeasurable and boundless realms of desire, form, and formlessness—the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, humans, and non-humans gathered to hear this Dharma-door of the dhāraṇī for entering the practice of all-knowledge.
As soon as a bodhisattva hears this Dharani-door of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge, they attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Furthermore, those who transcribe it will constantly behold the Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and make offerings to the Sangha, until their unsurpassed Parinirvana.

If a bodhisattva reads and recites this "Dhāraṇī Door for Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge," all grave offenses will be extinguished without remainder, and upon rebirth, they shall attain the first stage (bhūmi).

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates this "Dhāraṇī Door for Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge," if that bodhisattva previously committed the five sins of immediate retribution, they shall all be completely eliminated, and upon rebirth, they shall likewise attain the first stage;
if there were no sins of immediate retribution, the remaining offenses of the present life shall all be extinguished, and they shall immediately attain the first stage.

Even if one is unable to practice, unable to recite, or does not hear the Dharma, if one makes offerings to the Dharma Master with flower garlands of silk and brocade, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, will praise them, saying, "Excellent! Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will also bestow upon them the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Because this Bodhisattva has given silk and brocade, they shall before long attain the rank of a Dharma Prince in the position of one-life-to-enlightenment (ekajāti-pratibaddha), and achieve Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Likewise, through such offerings of incense, they shall before long obtain the fragrance of the unsurpassed samādhi.
By making offerings of flowers, one shall before long obtain the flower of unsurpassed wisdom;
those who make offerings of jewels to the Dharma Master shall before long obtain the thirty-seven jewels that assist toward enlightenment.
“Good son! This Dharani-door of entering the practice of all-aspect wisdom provides such benefits for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Why is this?

Because this exclusively expounds the Dharma-treasury of the Bodhisattvas, by means of this, they enter the dhāraṇī-door of the practice of all-knowledge; the Bodhisattvas thereby attain incalculable eloquence and acquire the four sublime dharmas.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Candrottara, by means of this Dharani-door of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge (Sarvākārajñatā), instructed and empowered the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā;

immediately, the earth shook violently and a great light appeared, such that the wondrous radiance pervaded the infinite and boundless Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, and the ground became as level as the palm of a hand.”

Among them, the assembled bodhisattvas saw the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the immeasurable and boundless worlds of the ten directions; likewise, they saw countless bodhisattvas from immeasurable Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions arriving in this Candana world to make offerings, pay respect, and attend upon the Tathāgata Candrottara, in order to hear this *dhāraṇī-door* that enters the practice of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“Good sons! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottara addressed the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, saying: ‘Good sons!’”
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are in their final birth before Buddhahood; for them, I permit entry into this samādhi of the cessation of mind for ten minor kalpas.

As for the other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, from the time of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Gaganamudrā, they have heard this Dharma-treasury of the bodhisattvas—the dhāraṇī-door of entering the practice of all-knowledge—for ten minor kalpas. During these ten minor kalpas, they behold the countless Buddha-lands of the ten directions and the Tathāgatas currently dwelling in those worlds, having achieved the roots of goodness born of their pure resolve.
Having made offerings to the Tathāgata Candrottara with various and manifold bodhisattva supernormal powers, those bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”
"Will this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā, at the conclusion of ten intermediate kalpas, turn the unsurpassed wheel of the true Dharma?
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is!"
"Good son!
When these ten intermediate kalpas have ended, this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
on the very night he attains Buddhahood, he shall turn the wheel of the true Dharma for all bodhisattvas during that same night."
If there are bodhisattvas who, within ten minor eons, achieve the roots of goodness for entering the *dhāraṇī* gate of the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) by hearing it from him,

then at the moment the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, on that very night he will turn the wheel of the True Dharma, the irreversible wheel, and the supreme wheel, causing countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas to dwell in the state of non-retrogression.

As for those bodhisattvas who, during ten minor kalpas, heard from him the exposition of the dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī for entering the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), they all at that time attained the stage of being born only once more before reaching buddhahood (*ekajātipratibaddha*).

Those bodhisattvas who had heard even a small portion of the Dharma all attained the stages of abiding at that time; they became non-retrogressive regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and at that moment, they all fully acquired this dhāraṇī.

Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottara, having manifested various supernatural transformations of a Buddha for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, manifested for the bodhisattva Gaganamudrā a samādhi named Nārāyaṇa, causing him to receive a vajra-body; he then manifested the Samādhi of Adorned Radiance and, before the wheel of Dharma had yet been turned, for ten intermediate kalpas taught all the bodhisattvas this dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī for entering the practice of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).

In all Buddha-worlds, they see him manifesting the body of a Buddha, with its marks and signs and radiant light; he manifests the Vajracakra Samādhi, sitting upon the Bodhi-seat without yet having turned the wheel of Dharma, preaching various teachings for the sake of the bodhisattvas; and he manifests the Cakramaṇḍala Samādhi, causing the wheel of Dharma to be turned.
At that time, countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings attained the stage of non-retrogression.

Once the Bodhisattva Ākāśamudrā knew that the wheel of Dharma had been turned, he, together with a multitude of countless bodhisattvas, made offerings to the World-Honored One and each returned to his precious upper terrace.
On that very night, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candracchattra entered parinirvāṇa without remainder.
Having completed their offerings to the relics of the World-Honored One, which were worthy of such veneration, those bodhisattvas each ascended back to their precious terraces.

The remaining bodhisattvas each returned to their own lands; among them, those bodhisattvas who were in their final birth before buddhahood entered the samādhi of cessation and remained in profound stillness for ten minor kalpas.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā immediately expounded all dharmas in detail for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas over the course of ten intermediate kalpas, causing the multitude of bodhisattvas to plant various roots of goodness.

Last night he attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; on that very same night, he turned the wheel of Dharma and manifested great supernormal powers, causing countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to dwell in non-retrogression from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

At that time, he further preached the Dharani Door of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge Wisdom (*sarvākārajñatācaryāpraveśa-dhāraṇīmukha*). Eighty nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*);
ninety-two billion sentient beings attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
and seventy-two nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas attained this Dharani Door of Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge Wisdom.
"Countless devas and worldlings have resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vairambha addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“By being endowed with what dharmas does a bodhisattva obtain this dhāraṇī?
The Buddha said,
“A bodhisattva obtains this dhāraṇī by being fully endowed with four dharmas.”
What are these four?

A bodhisattva dwells in the four noble lineages: being content with whatever robes are obtained, being content with whatever food is obtained, being content with whatever dwellings and bedding are obtained, and being content with whatever medicines are obtained.
When a bodhisattva is fully endowed with these four dharmas, they attain the cultivation of this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is endowed with five dharmas, they attain the cultivation of the dhāraṇī-door for entering the practice of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).
What are the five?

One should personally uphold the Prātimokṣa precepts, restrain oneself with propriety, and be fully endowed with dignified conduct; one should train oneself thus, feeling great dread even toward minor transgressions.
To those who do not uphold the precepts, they exhort them to uphold the precepts so that they may abide therein;
to those who lack right view, they exhort them to right view so that they may abide therein;
to those who lack dignified deportment, they exhort them to correct deportment so that they may abide therein.
For sentient beings with distorted intentions, he exhorts them toward right intention and establishes them therein;
for those training as śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, he exhorts them toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and establishes them therein.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed with these five dharmas, they attain entry into the dharanī-door of the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Furthermore, when a bodhisattva is fully endowed with six dharmas, they attain this dharanī.
What are these six?
Having already accumulated much learning, when seeing those with little learning, one encourages them to become learned and establishes them therein;
being personally free from stinginess, one encourages stingy sentient beings to practice giving and establishes them therein.
Not harassing sentient beings, one bestows fearlessness upon them;
rescuing those who are terrified, one enables them to attain liberation;
and being free from deception and hypocrisy.
They always delight in emptiness and stillness;
when a bodhisattva is endowed with these six dharmas, they attain entry into the *dhāraṇī* gate of the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

When a bodhisattva is fully equipped with such dharmas, having briefly prepared everything, they dwell in a secluded place for seven years, reciting these mantra-words day and night during the six periods, with palms joined and single-minded concentration.
Upon arising, he universally cultivates mindfulness of all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions.
After that bodhisattva-mahāsattva has completed seven years, he attains this dhāraṇī gate of entering the practice of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Having attained such a dhāraṇī and having attained such a noble, clear eye of wisdom, one sees the Buddhas currently dwelling in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, manifesting great radiance.
Having witnessed the supernatural powers of those Buddhas, he attained eighty-four thousand dharani-doors, seventy-two thousand samadhi-doors, and sixty thousand dharma-doors.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas attain this *dhāraṇī* gate of entering the practice of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*), and having attained the *dhāraṇī*, they attain great compassion.

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva attains this *dhāraṇī*, even if they have committed the five crimes of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya-karma*), upon casting off this body, these are immediately extinguished; they proceed to the three bodies (*trikāya*) without further residual habits and ascend to the tenth stage (*bhūmi*).

If a bodhisattva has no ānantarya offenses, all other offenses will be completely eliminated; they shall, upon changing bodies, attain the ten stages, and before long realize the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and achieve all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).
“Good son! This *dhāraṇī* gate of entering the practice of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*) brings such great benefit to bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

When the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Dṛḍhasena saw the supernatural power manifested by the Buddha, the World-Honored One, he attained such holy joy in the Dharma and became fully endowed with such supernatural powers.

Having thus made offerings to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and having heard various teachings from those Buddhas and attained samādhi, patience, and dhāraṇī, he returns to this land.
“Good son! This Dharani-door of entering the practice of all-aspect wisdom thus benefits bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, eliminating all karmic obstructions and causing their roots of goodness to increase.”
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
In the past, in the presence of as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the world as there are grains of sand in nine Ganges Rivers, we heard and obtained this dhāraṇī."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke thus:
"I have heard [the names] from as many as two Ganges-sands.
Another spoke of three; and so on.
Again there are four;
again there are five;
again there are six.
Again there are seven;
again there are eight;
again there are nine.
They spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!

In the presence of the World-Honored Ones currently dwelling in the world throughout the past, numbering as many as the sands of nine Ganges Rivers, we heard and attained this Dharani-door of entering the practice of all-knowledge."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya spoke thus:
“Ten *gaṅgā*-sands of *kalpas* in the past, there was a great *kalpa* named Saṃtaraṇa; that Buddha-field was named Sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣita.”

At that time, there was a Buddha named Śālendrarāja, who was perfect in wisdom and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed being, a charioteer of men, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, and a World-Honored One.

Surrounded by hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of nāyutas of bhikṣu-saṃghas, and likewise surrounded by innumerable bodhisattvas, he preached this dhāraṇī gateway for entering the practice of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
I heard this dhāraṇī from him and brought its practice to fulfillment.

Thus, throughout countless kalpas, and further beyond countless asaṃkhyeya past Buddhas, World-Honored Ones—both those currently dwelling in the world and those who have passed away—I made offerings to those Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, with the supernatural powers of countless asaṃkhyeya Bodhisattvas. At the site of each and every Buddha, I planted immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya, ineffable, and boundless roots of goodness and merit. By virtue of these roots of goodness, thousands of Buddhas have bestowed upon me the prediction of enlightenment.

Because I have waited for the proper time and fulfilled my original vow, I have long remained in the world and did not first attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Today, the World-Honored One has conferred upon me the rank of Dharma Prince, untied the knots of the liberation-garland, and [established me in] *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva:
"So it is, so it is! Maitreya Ajita!"
As you have said, from the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sālendrarāja, you heard and obtained this dhāraṇī gate for entering the practice of all-aspect wisdom.
"You, Maitreya!
If you wish to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, you shall be able to fulfill the intention of the Tathāgata within ten great kalpas."
You, Maitreya!
Thus, with such swiftness, you shall enter parinirvāṇa without remainder through unsurpassed parinirvāṇa.
You, Maitreya!
He is thus able to delight in remaining long in the world, because he awaits the proper time due to his original vow.
Maitreya!
You shall now receive from me the office of a Dharma Prince.

At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the entire assembly—the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, humans, non-humans, and so forth. Having surveyed them, at that very moment, he spoke these dhāraṇī verses:
*Tat-ta-ra-bu-mi-dan-ta-bu-mi* (Tad-tara-bhūmi-danta-bhūmi)
Dharmadhātu-vimukti-vimukta-siddhi.
Vire dīpame pāraṃ yāpame viśākara-sthira-pāraṃ-tri-vi.
Mahāpūmi ākucchā pūmi kṣepa parvata.
Vemacitra-samādhi-pariśuddha-vimokṣa-jāti.
Kṣaṇabhūmi samudra vimudra paramamudra vi-
Śakrādṛśyavati viśāṭatīraṇāgāgārapāmuṣe.
Vata-vimati-ūṣa-he-ra-syā-la-ga-ḍhi-mi-ja-rā-ta-mu-lā-va-śi.
Saṃghalome-iti-jūla-vati-mi-khi-vendhara.
Dāharāvatīprajñāpūta akāramitā.

“It is most difficult,

The appearance of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in the world is rare; likewise, the cultivation of the mantra syllables—consisting of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation—is also difficult, for it benefits sentient beings and brings about the accomplishment of the bodhisattva’s merits.
Good son! When the Tathāgata was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, he fulfilled generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

I have drawn near to hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of Buddhas; whether practicing generosity, upholding the precepts, cultivating the holy life, engaging in cultivation, or practicing diligence, patience, and the perfection of meditative concentration, I drew near to and studied wisdom extensively. Having fulfilled various and manifold wholesome karmas, I have thereby now attained unsurpassed wisdom.
"Good son!

When the Tathāgata was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of kalpas, his speech was free from the four faults: he did not speak falsely, he did not engage in frivolous chatter, he did not use harsh words, and he did not use double-tongued speech. By virtue of this, he attained the mark of the broad and long tongue."
"Good son! That which the Tathāgata has spoken is ultimately free from falsehood.

At that time, the World-Honored One, while seated upon his throne, desired to manifest supernatural powers and entered a samādhi called "Gathering All Meritorious Virtues," wherein he extended his broad and long tongue to cover his own face.

From his tongue-mark, he emitted ten billion rays of light; these wondrous lights shone universally throughout the trichiliocosm, pervading everywhere among those in the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, humans, and devas.
For those beings in the hells who were being scorched by fire, because of this light, a cool breeze arose so that they might briefly experience pleasure.
Before each and every person within the hells, he manifested the body of a Tathāgata, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty secondary characteristics.
Because those hell-beings beheld the Buddha, they were filled with joy and this thought arose in their minds:
"Having encountered this Great Being, we now obtain joy and happiness.
Toward the Tathāgata, their hearts gave rise to love, joy, and reverence.
The Tathāgata addressed them:
"Ha! You sentient beings!
By making such a declaration—'Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Sangha'—you shall attain peace and security throughout the long night."
Having heard the Buddha’s words, those beings in the hells joined their palms together and spoke thus:
“Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha!”
Those sentient beings in hell, by virtue of these roots of goodness, immediately abandon the hells; they are either reborn in the heavens or among human beings.
If there are sentient beings in the Cold Ice Hells, a warm breeze blows upon them, until they eventually attain birth among human beings.
Thus, when the light shines upon those hungry ghosts whose bodies are ablaze with hunger and thirst, the fires of hunger and thirst are extinguished, and they obtain happiness.

As each hungry ghost beholds the manifested Buddha appearing before them—whose body is adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty minor characteristics—they are filled with joy and contentment;
toward the World-Honored One, they give rise to feelings of love, delight, and reverence.
The Buddha taught and transformed them according to their words.
By virtue of these roots of goodness, they cast off their bodies therein, with some being reborn in the heavens and others among human beings.
In this manner, he transformed animals and even those among humans and devas.

Within that assembly, countless bodhisattvas attained samādhi, kṣānti, and dhāraṇī.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śāntamati, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By what causes and by what conditions are the other buddha-fields so pure, free from all defilements and impurities, and devoid of the five turbidities, being adorned with all manner of wonderful and marvelous features?”

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are fully endowed with all manner of majestic virtues and are completely satisfied with all kinds of joys; even the names of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do not exist there, let alone any others.
World-Honored One!

By what causes and conditions do you attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this defiled and evil world of the five turbidities—the turbidity of lifespan, the turbidity of the kalpa, the turbidity of sentient beings, the turbidity of views, and the turbidity of afflictions—and preach the Dharma of the fourfold assembly and the three vehicles?
“World-Honored One!
For what reason do you not take up a pure buddha-field that is free from the five turbidities?
The Buddha said:
“Good son! By virtue of their original vows, Bodhisattvas take up pure Buddha-fields; likewise, by virtue of their original vows, they take up impure Buddha-fields.
Good son!”
There are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, being fully endowed with great compassion, take up impure buddha-fields. Why is this?
It is because of their original vows, which state: "May I attain buddhahood in this evil world."
"Listen attentively with a single mind, and I shall speak for you.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Silent Mind (Śāntamati) listened to what the Buddha was saying.
The Buddha said:

“Good son! In the distant past, more than one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa of *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [Ganges-sand] eons ago, in this buddha-field, there was a great kalpa named Dharaṇī. Within that great kalpa, in this buddha-field, there were these four continents.”
At that time, there was a Wheel-Turning King named Vigata-raṇa, who ruled over the four continents.

During the reign of King Vigata-raṇa, there was a royal preceptor, a Brahmin named Sāgara-jaya, who begot a son endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, fully adorned with the hundred merits. His body was encircled by a halo, possessing the color of the *kālānusāri* tree and refined gold.
At the time of his birth, hundreds of thousands of devas came to make offerings; they immediately bestowed upon him the name Sāgaragarbha.
At another time, he left the household life to study the Way, shaving off his hair and beard and donning the dharma robes. He attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and was named Ratnagarbha.
When that Buddha turned the wheel of Dharma, he caused many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings to attain the heavenly realms and the fruits of liberation.

At another time, surrounded and attended by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of śrāvakas, he traveled through villages, cities, towns, and royal residences, gradually arriving at the city of Anuśaṅkara.

Not far from the city where King Viraja, the Wheel-Turning Monarch, ruled, there was the Jambuvana grove; there the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha dwelt together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of śrāvakas.

At that time, King Vigataraṇa heard that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, together with an assembly of countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of śrāvakas, had entered his city and was staying in the Jambhila Garden. The king then thought:
"I should now go to the Tathāgata to make offerings, and to honor, revere, respect, and praise him."

Then King Vigata-rajas, with his great spiritual merit and immeasurable royal majesty, surrounded and escorted by countless hundreds of thousands of millions of ministers and subjects, went forth from the city and proceeded to the Jambuvana Garden.

Having exhausted the ground traversed by his vehicle, he dismounted and proceeded on foot toward the place where the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha was; having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and withdrew to sit to one side.

“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, seeing King Vigataraṇa’s joy in the True Dharma, exhorted and converted him with essential words to make him leap with exultation and joy.
Having used countless expressions to gladden him with the True Dharma and having exhorted him with essential words until he was leaping with joy, he remained silent.”
Then King Vigataraṇa joined his palms together and addressed the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, saying:

"I pray only that the World-Honored One, together with the community of bhikṣus, will accept my invitation for three months to receive offerings of robes, food and drink, bedding, seats, and sleeping requisites, as well as medicines for the sick, according to their needs."
“Good son! The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha accepted the invitation by remaining silent.
King Vigatasaṃgha, knowing that the Buddha had accepted his invitation, performed a prostration, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and departed.”
Then King Vigataraṇa returned and addressed the minor kings, ministers, and people, saying:
"You should know this!
I have invited the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, along with the community of bhikṣus, for three months, providing them with everything they require."
"I have wealth and treasures, as well as articles for making offerings; all that I hold dear and precious, I now bestow entirely upon the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus.
You, too, should take all your own possessions and articles for making offerings, and bestow them entirely upon the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus."
Those people all likewise offered their gifts in return.

Then the Treasurer Minister used gold entirely to cover the grounds of the Jambhila Garden; having finished this in an instant, he immediately constructed for the World-Honored One a terrace made of the seven treasures. On all four sides, the doors were made of the seven treasures, and throughout the garden were placed trees of the seven treasures. Those trees were adorned with various kinds of garments, various banners and canopies, various pearls and necklaces, various dwellings, various ornaments, various precious vessels, various blended incenses, and various flowers and fruits of the seven treasures.

They scattered various kinds of flowers, various silks and brocades, various rugs and cushions, various woolen carpets, and various garments to spread as seats; furthermore, they placed precious wheels outside the platform, which hovered in the air one fathom above the ground directly before the World-Honored One, their radiance exceedingly bright.
The pure white elephant-treasure, with its seven limbs fully developed and level, stood behind the World-Honored One, holding up a precious tree that covered the World-Honored One from above.
That tree was magnificent, adorned with various necklaces made of the seven treasures.

With necklaces of the seven treasures and various ornaments, various garlands and decorations, various silken fabrics, various exquisite garments, and various dwellings, there were canopies upon the trees adorned with the seven treasures.
The primary consort of King Vigatāraṇa stood before the Buddha and scattered powdered sandalwood from the "ox-head" variety, grown on this side of the ocean, over the Buddha.

King Vigatāraṇa personally held a mani-jewel of extreme brilliance and placed it before the Tathāgata; the light of that wheel-light jewel illuminated the garden, its radiance filling it completely. The light of the Buddha’s own radiance illuminated the trichiliocosm, its subtle and wondrous brilliance pervading every single śrāvaka.
They used gośīrṣa sandalwood for their seats and also for footstools to support their feet.
Behind each of the śrāvakas was a white elephant, which held up a precious tree, exquisitely adorned and magnificent, covering them as previously described.

Before each of the śrāvakas stood a court lady, adorned with necklaces of various jewels; they all scattered powdered sandalwood from the "ox-head" variety grown on this shore of the ocean over the Buddha.
Before each of the śrāvakas, a lapis lazuli bead was placed, and various kinds of music resounded throughout the garden.
The noble minister of the Jewel Path led the fourfold army and stood in formation outside the garden, surrounding it to provide guard.

“Good son! At that time, King Vigataraṇa departed from the city at dawn to visit the Buddha. He rode his vehicle as far as the ground would allow for riding, then dismounted and proceeded on foot toward the place where the World-Honored One was.”

Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and paid homage to the assembly of monks; after circumambulating them three times, the king personally poured water over the hands of the Tathāgata and served him various delicacies and a hundred flavors of food and drink, all of which were fully prepared.
Knowing that the meal was finished, the king withdrew his bowl and, holding a precious fly-whisk in his hand, respectfully fanned the Tathāgata.
After the king’s thousand sons and the eighty-four thousand minor kings had likewise made offerings to the assembly of śrāvakas, each of them took up a whisk and fanned the great multitude.
A short time after the meal was finished, countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings all came into the garden for the purpose of hearing the Dharma.

Countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of devas, in the midst of the sky, rained down various celestial flowers and performed various musical performances; they hung in the air various celestial silks, banners, canopies, soft garments, and necklaces.

Forty thousand blue yakṣas, within the sandalwood grove, constantly gather ox-head sandalwood from this side of the ocean to serve as fuel, providing meals for the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus.
At that time, King Vigatasaṃgha lit many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of lamps before the Buddha and the great assembly during that very night. "Good son!

During the night, King Vigatasaṃgha held lamps aloft for the entire night before the World-Honored One—upon his head, his two shoulders, his hands, his knees, and his two feet. By the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, his body felt no fatigue; he experienced bliss within his person, just as a bhikṣu who has entered the third dhyāna remains with his body leaning neither forward nor back and his mind free from weariness."
Thus they made offerings for the full duration of three months.

In this way, the thousand sons, the eighty-four thousand minor kings, and many other hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings each provided offerings to a single śrāvaka for three months, just as King Vigata-rajas had offered to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha; there was no difference between them.
At that time, the king’s principal queen made offerings of flowers and incense to the assembly for three months;
likewise, many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of billions of court ladies also made offerings of flowers and incense to the assembly of śrāvakas for three months in the same manner.

“Good son! At that time, after King Vigataraṇa had completed the three months [of the rainy retreat], he offered eighty-four thousand precious palaces of purple-gold to the World-Honored One as a dedication.”
He also offered eighty-four thousand golden wheels, headed by the wheel-treasure;

eighty-four thousand white elephants, headed by the elephant-treasure; eighty-four thousand horses, headed by the horse-treasure; and eighty-four thousand sun-bright pearls, headed by the jewel-treasure—all of which he gave as offerings to the Buddha.
The eighty-four thousand minor kings, headed by the Treasure of the Steward, offered themselves to the World-Honored One to provide for all his needs.
The eighty-four thousand minor kings, headed by the Treasure of the Holy Guide, offered themselves to the World-Honored One to serve him at his side.
There were eighty-four thousand cities, with the city of Anusha as the foremost, which he offered to the Buddha and the Sangha for their use as they pleased.

There were eighty-four thousand rows of trees made of the seven precious gems, eighty-four thousand clusters of flowers made of various jewels, eighty-four thousand parasols made of the seven precious gems, eighty-four thousand exquisite royal garments, and eighty-four thousand ornaments of various jewel garlands; to speak briefly:

Vehicles, couches and seats, as well as footstools; bedding, footwear, headgear, crowns and turbans; necklaces, golden chains, and pearl necklaces; music, bells, conchs, drums, banners, standards, and fly-whisks; lamps, censers, bathing vessels, gardens, groves, birds, and beasts—all made of various jewels and exquisite delicacies, numbering eighty-four thousand each—having offered these entirely as a gift to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:

"My kingdom’s affairs are many, and I repent before the World-Honored One. I only pray that the Tathāgata will take pleasure in dwelling in this garden so that I may again have the honor of beholding you."
The thousand sons of King Vigatāraṇa stood before the Buddha, and each prince individually invited the Buddha and the Saṅgha to accept all their necessities for three months of offerings;
the World-Honored One accepted the princes' invitation by remaining silent.

At that time, King Vigataraṇa, knowing that the Buddha had accepted the invitation of his sons, prostrated himself at the feet of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, circumambulated them three times to the right, and took his leave to return to the palace.
At that time, among the princes, the eldest was named Animiṣa; for three months, he made offerings to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, just as King Vigata-rajas had done.
Every other day, the prince came once to pay his respects to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, and listened to the subtle and wondrous Dharma. "Good son!

At that time, the Great Master of the State, a brāhmaṇa and the father of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, was named Sāgaradatta. He went throughout Jambudvīpa to beg from men and women, both great and small; he did not accept their offerings immediately, but first required the donors to receive the Three Refuges and establish themselves in Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and only then would he accept the gift."

Within Jambudvīpa, there were none among the wise—whether old or young—who did not receive his offerings; the Brahmin Sāgaradatta exhorted them with the Three Refuges and established them in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
In this manner, he exhorted many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to cultivate the three bases of merit and abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
For three months, Prince Animiṣa made offerings to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus just as King Vigata-rajas had done;

however, with the exception of his city-walls, the natural wheel-treasure, the natural elephant-treasure, the natural horse-treasure, the natural maṇi-jewel, the woman-jewel, the steward-jewel, and the counselor-jewel—having set these aside—he offered eighty-four thousand golden wheels, eighty-four thousand elephants, and eighty-four thousand horses entirely as a gift to the Buddha. To speak briefly:

There were eighty-four thousand sun-bright jewels, court ladies, youths, wish-fulfilling trees, heaps of flowers, garments, canopies, necklaces, vehicles, couches, footstools, bedding, footwear, headwear, crowns, pearls, and necklaces; as well as eighty-four thousand musical instruments, bells, conchs, drums, banners, and fly-whisks; and eighty-four thousand lamps, censers, bathing vessels, groves, and birds and beasts—all made of various precious gems, along with exquisite flavors of the same number.
Having completely dedicated all these offerings, he confessed before the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus.

Prince Nirmokṣa likewise used such articles of worship to provide for the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus for three months, just as Animiṣa had done. Having completed his offerings, he bestowed these precious objects as a *dakṣiṇā*, just as Animiṣa had done.
The princes of the royal assembly made offerings to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus for three months, and their distribution of alms was likewise.
Now, I shall briefly describe those princes:
Prince Abhaya, Prince Gaganagañja, Prince Hastidanta, and Prince Maitrāyaṇīputra.
Prince Madhusūdana, Prince Mādhava, Prince Bhūmipāla, Prince Arthajña, Prince Kumāra,
Prince Mūḍhavimocaka, Prince Puruṣajña, Prince Ārādhana, Prince Dūtapreṣaka, Prince Aṅkamukha, Prince Arthavāk, and Prince A...
The Prince Neṇḍurū, the Prince Yāma, the Prince Hastiyāma, the Prince Candrayāma,
the Prince Sūryayāma, the Prince Indrayāma, the Prince Vajrayāma, the Prince Kṣāntiyāma,
the Prince Sthānayāma, the Prince Javanayāma, the Prince Haranemuka, and the Prince E...
Prince Āvaraṇa, Prince Balāvaraṇa, Prince Saṃkīrṇāvaraṇa,
Prince Saṃkīrṇarata, Prince Rājadravya, Prince Kāmamūrchita, Prince Hārītīputra, Prince Rakṣita,
Prince Rājapraśasta, Prince Lavanāmbuprabhūta, and Prince Vyālaripu.
Prince Vyāghrapāda, Prince Vyāghranu, Prince Hastinu, Prince Candana,
and Prince Anivartita— even down to the thousand sons of King Raṇajaya—
each and every one of them likewise made offerings of all necessities to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the Arhat.
To the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and his immeasurable assembly of bhikṣus, he provided robes, food and drink, bedding,
and medicinal requisites for the sick, as well as all other necessities, each for three months; just as King Animiṣa’s son did,
he offered eighty-four thousand golden wheels, up to eighty-four thousand flavors, for each individual member of the assembly.
They all dedicated their offerings to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus.

Through these great acts of giving, some sought the position of Śakra, some sought the rank of Brahmā, some sought the realm of Māra, some sought the status of a Cakravartin King, some sought great wealth, and some sought the vehicle of a śrāvaka; yet not a single person sought the vehicle of a pratyekabuddha, much less the Mahāyāna.

At that time, King Vigatāraṇa, through this great act of giving, sought to become a Wheel-Turning Sage King; thus, for a full two hundred and fifty years, he also individually repented before the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus.

At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, went to the community of bhikṣus headed by the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and invited them for seven years of offerings, providing all necessities—robes, food and drink, bedding, medicine according to their ailments, and whatever else was required.
At that time, the World-Honored One silently accepted the invitation of the National Preceptor.
Then, the brahmin Sāgaradatta provided all necessary offerings to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, no different from how King Vigataraṇa had done.
“Good son! At another time, the brahmin Sāgaramegha conceived this thought:

‘I have already exhorted many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know what the King Vigata-rajas intends; does he seek to become a celestial king, or a human king, or does he seek the vehicle of the śrāvaka, or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha, or does he seek *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?’”

If I shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, may I cause all sentient beings who have not yet crossed over to cross over; may I cause all sentient beings who have not yet attained liberation to attain liberation; may I cause all sentient beings who suffer from old age, illness, death, grief, lamentation, pain, and affliction to achieve deliverance; and may I cause those who have not yet entered parinirvāṇa to attain parinirvāṇa.

Whether you be a nāga, a yakṣa, a buddha, a śrāvaka, or a Brahmā king, I pray that you reveal this dream to me: does this king seek celestial blessings, human blessings, the stage of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, or is he seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?

“Good son! At that time, the royal preceptor, the brahmin Sāgaradatta, saw such a radiance within his dream, and he beheld the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions.”
Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, all sent lotus flowers to the brahmin; they had silver stems, golden leaves, agate pedestals, and lapis lazuli filaments, and upon each flower a sun appeared.
Above each sun was a canopy made of the seven treasures, and from each sun sixty billion rays of light issued forth; all these rays entered the mouth of the brahmin.
He saw his own body, ten thousand *yojanas* in height, as pure as a mirror.
Within his own body, he saw sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, all sitting cross-legged upon lotus pedestals and entering into samādhi.
He saw those suns surrounding his body on all sides, and he also saw various canopies abiding in the void up to the Brahma-heaven.
Those lotuses surrounding his body emitted a soft sound that surpassed the five celestial musical instruments.
Within it, he saw King Vigata-rajas, with the head of a pig and a human body, smeared with his own blood, running hither and thither as many various insects vied with one another to devour him.
He sat beneath a lowly eranda tree, where many various insects vied with one another to devour him until his body was reduced to white bones; yet, time and again, he would return to life.
