A being with the head of a pig and the body of a human smeared himself with blood, and many various insects vied with one another to come and eat him.
He sat beneath a lowly *eranda* tree, where many various insects vied with one another to devour him until only his white bones remained.

Within that state, he saw various princes—some with the heads of pigs, some with the heads of elephants, some with the heads of water buffaloes, some with the heads of wolves, some with the heads of jackals, some with the heads of dogs, and some with the heads of monkeys—their bodies smeared with blood as many various insects vied to devour them. They all sat beneath the lowly *eranda* tree, where many various insects vied to devour them until they were reduced to white bones; yet their bodies would restore themselves, and the insects would immediately devour them once more.
Furthermore, he saw another prince riding in a water-buffalo carriage, adorned with sumanā flowers, traveling southward along an improper path.
Brahmā, Śakra, and the World Protectors came and spoke to him, saying:
"Ho! [Prince!]"
"O Brahmin!
You who stand surrounding the lotus, first take one flower from among them and present it to the king, and give one flower to each of his princes."
"Then you shall give them to the various minor kings, as well as to your own son and the other people.
When the brahmin heard that the messengers of the gods had thus distributed their tasks, he immediately divided the flowers.
Having awakened from sleep and risen from his seat, he recalled the dream he had seen; while seated, he gave rise to this thought:
"This is a wheel-turning monarch who delights in and seeks out lowly birth-and-death, and who, longing for peace and happiness, aspires to a base and humble state;
the princes and others are likewise thus."
Furthermore, I saw a prince riding in a water-buffalo cart, adorned with sumanā flowers, traveling toward the south; he is one who seeks the Śrāvaka-yāna.

Furthermore, the light that I have seen from the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the ten directions has reached throughout Jambudvīpa on my account, exhorting and transforming many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to accomplish the three grounds of merit and abide therein.

For this reason, I saw a great radiance in my dream and beheld the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, because I had traveled throughout Jambudvīpa to exhort and transform countless sentient beings, causing them to abide in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Furthermore, I now invite the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, together with the community of bhikṣus, for seven years to provide all that is required. For this reason, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, from the various other worlds throughout the ten directions, have now sent these flowers to me to inspire me toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; may these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, likewise send flowers for my sake.
In my vision, I saw the sun upon a lotus flower, and various rays of light entered my mouth; I saw my own body as being exceedingly tall and vast.

I saw the sun surrounding my entire body, and within my own person, I beheld sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas sitting cross-legged upon lotus pedestals, having entered into samādhi. Such dreams as these are beyond my understanding.
Furthermore, I saw Brahmā, Śakra, and the World-Protectors exhorting me to distribute the various flowers; immediately thereafter, I saw myself distributing these flowers.
Such dreams can only be clearly understood by a Buddha!
"For what reason have I seen this great dream?
I should now go to the Buddha's dwelling and ask about the meaning of this dream.
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta prepared a full array of delicacies during the night, and at dawn he went to the Buddha's dwelling, personally offering water for washing.

When the Buddha and the bhikṣus had finished pouring water for one another from top to bottom, he personally served various delicacies according to their needs, providing food for the Buddha and the Saṃgha. When they had finished eating and put away their bowls, he returned to his seat and preached the Dharma.

At that time, King Vigataraṇa, together with his thousand sons and an immeasurable multitude of hundreds of thousands of followers, surrounded and attended him as they proceeded to the place where the Buddha was. Having traveled by vehicle as far as the ground would permit, they dismounted; then, with reverent solemnity, they entered the garden on foot.
Arriving at the place of the Tathāgata, they prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet and those of the assembly of bhikṣus, and sat before the Buddha to hear the sublime Dharma.
At that time, after the brahmin Sāgaramegha had asked the Buddha about the dream he had previously seen, the World-Honored One said to the great brahmin:
"As for the great radiance you saw, it was the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions; they sent those flowers to you."
Looking upward, you saw the sun emitting rays of light, and all those rays entered your mouth.
Because you, O Brahmin, for two hundred and fifty years, traveled throughout Jambudvīpa, exhorting and transforming countless sentient beings, causing them to abide within the three fields of merit.
Furthermore, he exhorts and transforms countless sentient beings, causing them to abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Because of this great giving, O Brahmin!

All those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have bestowed upon you the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; they currently abide in the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, dwelling in the world and preaching the Dharma.
The Buddhas have sent these flowers to you; they have silver stems, golden leaves, agate pedestals, and lapis lazuli filaments, and upon every flower, the sun is visible.
"O Brahmin! That dream which appeared to you is a prior auspicious omen.
You, O Brahmin!"
In a dream, you saw the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the worlds of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, preaching the Dharma.
Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have sent you seven-jeweled canopies; those jeweled canopies remain suspended in the air, reaching as far as the Brahma Heaven.
"O Brahmin!

On the very night you attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, your fame shall spread throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reaching even to the Brahma heavens; and there shall be none who can look upon the crown of your head from above."
"Brāhmaṇa! That dream which appeared was a prior auspicious omen. Brāhmaṇa!"
"In your dream, you saw your own body become exceedingly tall and vast, reaching as far as the Brahma-heaven and remaining with its form encircling the sun. O Brahmin!

As for the countless sentient beings whom you have exhorted and transformed to resolve upon Bodhicitta, when you attain enlightenment, they too shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in as many lands in the ten directions as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world."
Those whom you originally exhorted and transformed toward bodhi will all praise you, saying:

"That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha first exhorted and transformed us toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; therefore, we have now attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and he is our spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)."
"Those Buddhas have all dispatched bodhisattvas to pay respectful homage, make offerings, and praise you.

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have each come from their own buddha-fields, employing various bodhisattva supernormal powers to make offerings to you. Having listened to the Dharma, they have attained various and manifold samādhis, kṣāntis, and dhāraṇī-doors.
Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will each return to their own lands and extol and praise your renown."
"Brahmin! That dream which appeared was a prior auspicious omen. Brahmin!"
"Brahmin, you see within your own body many billions of bodhisattvas sitting cross-legged upon lotus flowers and entering into samādhi.

When you attain enlightenment, you will inspire and transform many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to attain non-retrogression and abide in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"O Brahmin!

Having entered parinirvāṇa through unsurpassed parinirvāṇa, for as many great kalpas as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who rule as Kings of the True Dharma in the lands of the ten directions, shall all praise and extol you. Just as after the passing of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable kalpas, there will be a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha whose name is such-and-such."
"That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha exhorted and transformed us, causing us to abide in Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
for this reason, we have now attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and have obtained the rank of the King of the True Dharma."
“O Brahmin! That dream which appeared to you is a prior omen.
“O Brahmin! [he continued.]
In your dream, you saw other beings with the heads of pigs, elephants, and even dogs, their bodies smeared with blood, upon which many various insects vied to devour them;
you saw yourself sitting beneath a lowly eranda tree, where many various insects vied to devour you, until your body was reduced to white bones and then restored once more.

Having the heads of pigs and even dogs, they smear themselves with blood, and various miscellaneous insects compete to devour them. These foolish men—who dwell in the three grounds of merit practicing generosity, observing precepts, and cultivating meditative concentration—encounter the suffering of seeking the realm of Māra;
the suffering of seeking the heavens and then facing death when their merit is exhausted;
and among humans, the sufferings of old age, sickness, and death; the suffering of encountering the hated; and the suffering of separation from the beloved.
In the realm of hungry ghosts, there is the suffering of hunger and thirst;
in the realm of animals, there is the suffering of ignorance, darkness, slaughter, and dismemberment;
and even those who enjoy existence in the hells undergo various kinds of suffering.
Those who dwell upon the three grounds of merit seek to become a king of the gods in heaven;
they seek to become a king over one world-system among humans, a king over two world-systems, a king over three world-systems, or a king over four world-systems.
Such foolish men devour all sentient beings, and all sentient beings likewise devour those foolish men; thus, for a long time, they remain submerged in the cycle of birth and death.
"Brahmin! That dream which appeared was a prior auspicious omen.
"Brahmin! [he continued].
"Brahmin, you saw in your dream another person who had adorned themselves with sumanā flowers, riding in a water-buffalo cart and traveling south along an improper path."

That son of good family likewise dwells in the three grounds of merit—practicing giving, maintaining precepts, and cultivating meditative concentration—for the sake of his own liberation; he is one who seeks the Śrāvaka vehicle. That dream which appeared to him, involving a person seeking the Śrāvaka vehicle, is a prior auspicious omen.
Chapter Five: Encouraging Resolve The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Chapter Five: Encouraging Resolve “Good son!
At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, spoke thus to King Vigatasaṃgha:
‘Great King!’”

A human body is difficult to obtain, and leisurely tranquility is difficult to find; the appearance in the world of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha is extremely rare, like the udumbara flower which appears but once in an age. It is difficult to seek the roots of goodness with joy, and a correct vow is likewise difficult.
"Great King!

Sovereignty is the root of all suffering. Whether it be the sovereignty over one continent among humans, two continents, three continents, or the four continents, all are fundamentally rooted in suffering."
"O Great King!
This is the vessel for long-enduring suffering within birth and death.
O Great King!"
The karmic rewards of humans and devas are like a swift wind that never pauses, or like the moon reflected in water;
ordinary beings are insatiable in their pursuit of the five desires, intoxicated by sensory objects, and take pleasure in seeking the rewards of human and celestial realms.

Such worldlings repeatedly undergo the suffering of hell, the suffering of animals, and the suffering of hungry ghosts; they experience the suffering of separation from loved ones among humans, the suffering of falling back from the heavens, the suffering of repeated entry into the womb, and the suffering of mutual slaughter and harm.
Ordinary beings thus undergo suffering in succession. Why is this?
Because they lack virtuous friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), they do not give rise to right vows, nor can they seek them;

they consider what they have not yet reached as reached, what they have not yet attained as attained, and what they have not yet realized as realized. Thus, these ignorant ordinary beings do not know contentment, are unwilling to resolve upon *bodhicitta*, and do not feel weary of or distressed by saṃsāra—the very thing that could extinguish all suffering—wherein they repeatedly undergo suffering.
"Great King!
Contemplate the vessel of suffering that is birth and death. Therefore, Great King!
You have now planted roots of goodness and performed various meritorious deeds within the Buddha-dharma; you have already attained faith and joy toward the Triple Gem."
"Great King! Giving to the World-Honored One yields the fruit of great wealth; upholding the precepts yields the fruit of rebirth in heaven; and hearing the Dharma yields the fruit of great wisdom."
"If you have finished establishing your false views, you may now resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The King said, "Stop!"
"O Brahmin! I do not seek the bliss of awakening; I dwell within saṃsāra. O Brahmin!"
"I have already practiced giving, observed the precepts, and listened to the Dharma. O Brahmin!
Anuttarasamyaksambodhi is extremely difficult to attain."
The Brahmin Sāgaramegha spoke again: "Great King!
The path to bodhi is pure; you should form your vows with a focused mind and fulfill them with a pure heart, for this path is pure and the mind is pure."
This path is upright because it is free from flattery;
this path is utterly pure because all fetters have been exhausted;
this path is vast and expansive because it is without obstruction.
This path is equalizing, because of an impartial mind;
this path is fearless, because of refraining from all evils;
this path is great wealth, because of the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā).
This path is most honored because of the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā);
this path is without humiliation because of the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā);
this path is without dwelling because of the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā).
This path is tranquil and still because of the dhyāna-pāramitā;
this path is skillfully explained because of the prajñā-pāramitā;
this path attains true wisdom because of great compassion.
This path attains non-retrogression because of great compassion;
this path attains exultation because of great joy;
this path is steadfast because of great equanimity.
This path has no pits, precipices, thorns, or brambles, because it is free from the delusive conceptions of joy and desire;
this path leads to ultimate peace and security, because the mind is indestructible;
this path is not subject to plunder, because one skillfully understands forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles.
This path eliminates the enmity of Māra, for it skillfully understands the aggregates, elements, and sense bases;
this path is free from Māra, for it extinguishes all fetters;
this path attains the wondrous mind, for it is devoid of thoughts of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
This path flourishes because it receives the power of all Buddhas;
this path reaches the Great Jewel because it accords with the jewel of the knowledge of all modes;
this path is fully revealed because of the light of incalculable wisdom.
This path is a bright guide, for its practice never departs from spiritual friends;
this path has no high or low, for it is free from hatred and attachment;
this path is free from defilement, for it takes no pleasure in the turbidity of anger.
This path is well-gone, for it is free from all that is unwholesome.
Great King!
That path to enlightenment leads to security and reaches the very limit of nirvāṇa.
"Great King!
You should resolve to attain bodhicitta.
The king said:
“Brahmin! Even when a Tathāgata appears in a world where the lifespan of beings is eighty thousand years, he is still unable to extinguish all evil destinies.

Those sentient beings whose roots of goodness have matured will all abide in the fruits [of the path]; some will attain samādhi, dhāraṇī, and patience, while those whose bodhisattva roots of goodness are fully matured will receive the prediction of enlightenment.”
Those who possess even a small amount of roots of goodness receive the blessings of humans and devas;
sentient beings each revolve through various states of existence according to their virtuous or non-virtuous deeds.
Thus the Buddha said:
"If all sentient beings do not plant roots of goodness, suffering will not be extinguished;
although only the Buddha's body is a field of merit, he cannot deliver those who have not planted roots of goodness."

I shall resolve to attain bodhicitta; when I practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, I will enter the inconceivable dharani-dharma-gate through great wisdom to perform the buddha-work of liberating sentient beings, yet I shall not dedicate this impure land toward bodhicitta.

If I should attain such a Buddha-field as I desire, I shall resolve upon the bodhicitta; until I realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, I shall practice the bodhisattva path for that duration of time, extinguishing the suffering of all sentient beings within that Buddha-field.
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha entered the Samādhi of Manifesting Adornments and displayed such supernatural powers."

After the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha had entered the Samādhi of Manifesting Adornments, he immediately manifested such radiance that within each of the worlds as numerous as the atoms in a thousand Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions, all manner of adornments appeared: there were World-Honored Buddhas who had already entered *parinirvāṇa*, and those about to enter it;

there were Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas sitting beneath the Bodhi tree having subdued the hosts of Māra, and those who had attained Buddhahood not long ago and were turning the wheel of Dharma; there were those who had attained Buddhahood long ago and were preaching the Dharma; there were Buddha-lands filled exclusively with Bodhisattvas;
there were lands where even the names of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas did not exist, and places where Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas did exist.
There are lands empty of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas;
there are impure Buddha-lands when the five turbidities arise, and pure Buddha-lands where the five turbidities do not exist;
there are those who are noble and those who are lowly, and those with long lifespans and those with short lifespans.
In some buddha-fields, the calamity of fire arises; in others, the calamity of water arises; and in others, the calamity of wind arises.
Some places have already been destroyed, while others are just beginning to form.
The wondrous light shines upon them all, making everything manifest.
At that time, the great assembly universally beheld the magnificent adornments of those buddha-fields and world-systems.
Then, the brahmin Sāgaradatta said to the king,
"You should now simply observe the adornments of the buddha-field."
"Great King!
You should resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Great King!"
"You may take whichever Buddha-land you please. "Good son!
At that time, King Vigataraṇa joined his palms toward the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Buddha, saying:"
"O World-Honored One!
By what deeds and practices do Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas take up a pure Buddha-field?"
"By what means do beings with impure minds [attain rebirth],
and by what means do they take up long life?
The Buddha said:
"Great King!
A Bodhisattva-mahāsattva takes up a pure Buddha-field free from the five corruptions by means of his vow, and likewise takes up an impure one by means of his vow.
The King said:
"O World-Honored One!

I shall now return to the city and sit in quietude in one place to contemplate my vow: that in the Buddha-land to which I correspond, there shall be no five turbidities, as I dedicate my pure conduct."
The Buddha said,
"Great King!
Now is precisely the right time."

“Good son! At that time, King Vigataraṇa prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and departed. He returned to the city and entered his palace, where he sat alone in one place, contemplating in samādhi the vows for the adornment of a buddha-field.”
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta said to Prince Animiṣa: ‘Good son!’”

"You, too, should resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; you should dedicate all your meritorious deeds—your acts of giving, your observance of precepts, your cultivation of meditative concentration, and all other wholesome practices performed upon the three fields of merit—toward enlightenment."

He said, "I too shall return home and sit alone in one place, contemplating my vows for the adornment of a buddha-field. Once I have awakened the bodhicitta, I will come again to the presence of the Tathāgata to dedicate my bodhicitta and take hold of that adorned buddha-field."

Then that prince prostrated at the feet of the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and returned to his own residence. Sitting alone in one place, he contemplated in this way the vow to adorn a buddha-field.
“Good son! At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, spoke thus to his second son, Nimi:

‘You, young man, should also resolve upon bodhicitta. Thus, he exhorted the sons of the king until they all resolved upon bodhicitta; furthermore, eighty-four thousand minor kings and ninety-two billion other people were likewise exhorted to resolve upon bodhicitta.”
They all spoke thus:
"We too shall each return to our own homes and sit alone in one place, contemplating our vows to adorn Buddha-fields."
Throughout all those seven years, they each sat in samādhi with minds free from affliction or distraction, contemplating their vows to adorn Buddha-fields.
"Good sons!..."
At another time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta conceived this thought:
"I have exhorted many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
furthermore, I have invited the Buddha and an immeasurable saṅgha of bhikṣus, providing them with all their necessities for seven years."

If my aspiration for Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi is fulfilled according to my wish and I shall certainly attain it, I shall exhort and transform the devas, asuras, gandharvas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others through a great assembly of offerings.
“Good son! At that time, the royal preceptor, the brahmin Sāgaradatta, desired to see the Great King Vaiśravaṇa.
Good son!”
At that time, the Great King Vaiśravaṇa, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of yakṣas, went together with them at night to the place where the brahmin Sāgara-jīva was.
Standing before him, he spoke these words: "Brahmin!"
"Why do you think of me? The brahmin said, "Who are you?"
He said, "Brahmin!
Have you not heard that there is a lord of yakṣas named Vaiśravaṇa? I am he."
“Brahmin! What do you wish for me to do? The brahmin said:
"Great King!
You too should assist in this great assembly of giving. He replied:
"Indeed, Brahmin! It is just as you have thought."
"Great King! With my words, you should exhort all the yakṣas to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Furthermore, for those among you yakṣas who delight in seeking merit and who delight in seeking bodhi, you should go daily to the other shore of the ocean to fetch this shore’s ox-head sandalwood (*gośīrṣa-candana*), as well as various types of unguents and various kinds of mixed flowers, and bring them daily to me so that I may make offerings to the World-Honored One."
"Indeed, O Brahmin!
Having heard the words of the Brahmin, King Vaiśravaṇa returned to his own abode and beat the drum to assemble all the yakṣas and rākṣasas.
He spoke these words: "You should know!

In this Jambudvīpa, there is a brāhmaṇa named Sāgaradatta, who is the great teacher of King Vigatasaṃgharṣa. He has invited the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, together with the community of bhikṣus, and for seven years he has provided them with all their necessities."
"You all should rejoice in those roots of goodness, and by means of these roots of goodness, you should resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that very moment, many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of yakṣas and rākṣasas joined their palms together and spoke thus:

"The merit and wholesome karma of the brahmin Sāgaradatta, who invited the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, along with an immeasurable saṅgha of bhikṣus, and provided them with everything they required for seven years—"
"In this way, we rejoice in those meritorious deeds; by these roots of goodness, may we attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Viśramaṇa, the Great King, said:
"O virtuous ones, listen well!

"You who delight in seeking awakening and delight in seeking merit, you should go every day to the other shore of the ocean and bring back ox-head sandalwood from this shore to provide for the brahmin Sāgara-jina, as he prepares a meal for the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus."
Ninety-two thousand yakṣas raised their voices in unison, saying:

"We, O Great Being, shall, during these seven years, fetch ox-head sandalwood from this shore of the ocean to provide for the Brahmin Sāgara-jīva, so that he may make offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus."
Forty-six thousand yakṣas spoke thus:
"We shall bring various kinds of incense.
Fifty-two thousand yakṣas spoke thus:
"I shall bring various flowers.
Twenty thousand yakṣas spoke these words:
"We shall bring the essence of various flavors and place them within the food and drink of the Tathāgata and the assembly of bhikṣus."
Seventy thousand yakṣas spoke these words:
"O Great Being! We shall prepare food and drink for the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta thought of seeing the great king Virūḍhaka.

Immediately, the great king Virūḍhaka went to where the brahmin Sāgaradatta was, and even many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of kumbhāṇḍas were diligently exhorted to resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
In this manner, Virūpākṣa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of nāgas and gandharvas were inspired to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta thought of the world-protectors of the two sets of four continents; through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, they came to where the brahmin was.”
Having thus exhorted and transformed them, the brahmins each returned to their respective places to exhort their own kinsmen toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Even unto all the billions of Vaiśravaṇas in the three thousand great thousandfold Buddha-fields, together with their retinues, they exhorted and transformed others toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
There were ten billion Virūḍhakas, ten billion Virūpākṣas, and ten billion Dhṛtarāṣṭras, together with their retinues, who all exhorted him toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta conceived this thought:
‘If my aspiration for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi must surely fulfill the fruit of my heart’s vow, then I shall divide this great [treasure].’”
If this merit were equal to that of the various devas of the desire realm, and I were to exhort them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
then by virtue of these roots of goodness, should I truly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, should appear here now; likewise,
the sons of the gods of Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin should all appear.

“Good son! As soon as the brahmin Sāgaramegha had formed this thought, Śakra-devānām-indra appeared before him, as did the devaputra Suyāma, the devaputra Saṃtuṣita, the devaputra Nirmāṇarati, and the devaputra Paranirmitavaśavartin.”
The brahmin asked, "Who are you?
After those five heavenly kings had each stated their own names, they spoke as follows:
"O Brahmin! What do you wish us to perform?
What do you wish us to provide for this great sacrifice?"
The brahmin said:

"All the most exquisite jeweled terraces, jeweled trees, kalpavṛkṣa trees, fragrant trees, flowering trees, and fruit-bearing trees that you possess in heaven; the celestial garments, celestial seats, and bedding for the celestial hosts; the various celestial jeweled vessels; and the celestial ornaments, parasols, banners, necklaces, and musical instruments—all such things as these shall be used entirely to adorn this Jambuvana Grove for the Buddha and the Saṃgha."
"Very well, Great Being.
Having heard these words from the brahmin, those five heavenly kings each returned to their respective heavens and addressed the devas Vairañjika, Āṭavaka, Pārṣṇika, Kailāpika, and Nanda, saying:

"You Great Beings, go to the Jambūvana garden in Jambudvīpa; adorn it with such decorations, embellish it with such ornaments, and provide it with such necklaces, seats, and bedding for its adornment, so that they shall be no different from the celestial adornments."
Furthermore, for the sake of the World-Honored One, he constructed a jeweled terrace, adorned with various treasures like a terrace of many jewels.
He replied, ‘Indeed!’

Having heard this from the five heavenly kings, those five sons of gods spent the entire night in Jambudvīpa, adorning the Jambuvana grove in every way—from the precious trees to the banners and streamers;

they further constructed a jeweled terrace for the World-Honored One, like the terrace adorned with various jewels belonging to Śakra Devānām Indra. Having thus adorned the Jambuvana grove so that it was as magnificent as the celestial realms, they returned to the heavens and addressed the heavenly kings:
"Great Beings, you should know!"
The celestial adornments were such that even the adornments of Jambhila Garden in Jambudvīpa, including all its necklaces and ornaments, were exactly like this;

furthermore, for the World-Honored One, they constructed a jeweled terrace, as magnificent with various treasures as the terrace of Śakra Devānām Indra, being no different from those in the heavens or in Jambhila Garden in Jambudvīpa.
At that time, the five heavenly kings—the King of Śakra, Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin—came to Jambudvīpa and said to the brahmin Sāgara-jaya:
“Since you have already adorned the grove for the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, what further remains to be done?”
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke to the various heavenly kings, saying:
"O heavenly kings!
Gather all the celestial hosts from your respective domains and address them with these words on my behalf:”

“In Jambudvīpa there is a brāhmaṇa named Sāgaradatta. He has invited the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, together with an immeasurable saṅgha of bhikṣus, and for seven years he has provided them with all their necessities. You should rejoice in that meritorious deed and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. You should descend to Jambudvīpa to pay homage to and attend upon the World-Honored One and the saṅgha of bhikṣus, and listen to the subtle and wondrous Dharma in the presence of the World-Honored One.”
When those five heavenly kings had heard the words of the brahmin, they each returned to their respective abodes.
Then Śakra-devānām-indra assembled the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven and, using the words of the brahmin Sāgara-mati, exhorted them, saying:
"You great beings, you should know!"

"In Jambudvīpa, King Vigatāraṇa has a great teacher, a brahmin named Sāgaradatta, who has invited the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and an immeasurable saṃgha of bhikṣus to provide them with all their necessities for seven years.
We have already adorned the monastery for the Buddha and the Saṃgha; you should rejoice in those roots of goodness and resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that very moment, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven joined their palms in reverence and spoke these words:
"We rejoice in these meritorious deeds; by means of this rejoicing in meritorious deeds, we dedicate them all toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

In this manner, the Suyāma devaputras gathered the Suyāma devas; [the text] briefly describes... the Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin devaputras gathering the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, until there were many countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of devaputras who, with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words:
"We rejoice in those roots of goodness; by means of these roots of goodness, may we attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

"Therefore, you great beings should descend to Jambudvīpa to pay your respects to the World-Honored One, to attend upon him with reverence and intimacy, and to hear and receive the sublime Dharma, together with the community of bhikṣus."

At that time, each of the five heavenly kings, during that very night, descended to Jambudvīpa accompanied by hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of devaputras, devīs, and male and female youths. Each king, surrounded by this vast retinue, bowed his head at the feet of the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, and listened to the Dharma in the presence of the World-Honored One.

During the day, various celestial flowers—utpala, padma, kumuda, puṇḍarīka, sumana, pāriyātraka, atimuktaka, campaka, māndārava, and mahāmāndārava—rained down from the sky, accompanied by the sounding of celestial music.
Furthermore, son of good family,
the brahmin Sāgaramegha conceived this thought:
"If my aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is fulfilled and my vow is surely accomplished, I shall exhort the asuras toward bodhi."

“Good son! As soon as he had resolved his mind [upon awakening], five asura kings came to the place where the brahmin Sāgaramegha was, along with many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of male and female asuras, both great and small. Using the language of the brahmins, they exhorted them to resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and they came to the place of the Buddha to listen to and receive the Dharma.”
Briefly stated... O Brahmin!

As soon as he thus meditated upon the Māra King, the Māra named Pūrṇa immediately came to where the Brahmin was; even the countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of male and female māras, both great and small, were inspired to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and they even listened to the Dharma.
"Good son!

At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta called to mind the Great Brahmā Śaṅkhakuṇḍala. The Great Brahmā Śaṅkhakuṇḍala also came to the brahmin’s place; having heard [his request], he returned to the Brahma Heaven and, together with many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of Brahmās, exhorted them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Descending from above to the place where the World-Honored One was, they respectfully approached the community of bhikṣus and listened to the Dharma."
"Good son!

At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta called to mind the Śakras of the two sets of four continents, and he called to mind the sons of heaven of Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin. Those five heavenly kings, through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, also came to where the brahmin was; when the brahmin had thus given his instructions, they each returned to their respective realms and, using the brahmin’s words, exhorted their retinues toward bodhi.

In this way, many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sons and daughters of the Heaven of the Thirty-three were inspired to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Furthermore, Śakra came to these four continents to reverently attend upon the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, and to listen to and receive the Dharma."
In this way, the Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, and Nirmāṇarati devas, as well as the sons of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, exhorted the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas toward bodhi.

Many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of sons and daughters of the gods of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven, both great and small, having been inspired to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, came to this four-continent world to reverently approach and attend upon the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, and to listen to and receive the Dharma.
In this way, from two sets of four world-systems, three sets of four world-systems, four sets of four world-systems,

and five sets of four world-systems— including the Asuras, Māras, and Great Brahmās— Śakra, Suyāma, Saṃtuṣita, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin, along with the Asuras, Māras, and Great Brahmās, by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, came together with their retinues to these four world-systems to hear and receive the Dharma.

Even as far as the trichiliocosm Buddha-field, there were ten billion Śakras, ten billion Suyāmas, ten billion Saṃtuṣitas, ten billion Nirmāṇaratis, ten billion Paranirmita-vaśavartin devaputras, ten billion asura kings, ten billion Māras, and ten billion Great Brahmās. Each of these Great Brahmās exhorted countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Brahmā deities to resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Through the majestic spiritual power of the World-Honored One, they all came here to this four-continent world to pay respect and draw near to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, listening to and receiving the Dharma.
At that time, throughout the trichiliocosm, there was not even a space as small as a hair’s breadth that was not covered by the earth.
Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta had this thought:

"If my aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is to be fulfilled, such that ten billion Vaiśravaṇas, up to ten billion Mahābrahmās, all follow me, then I should manifest such great supernormal powers as to cause all sentient beings—humans, animals, hungry ghosts, and those in the hells—throughout the trichiliocosm to have their sufferings stilled and their joys produced; and may a transformation Buddha appear before each and every being to exhort them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, knowing the thoughts in the mind of the brahmin Sāgara-mati, immediately entered the samādhi called Pramoda. Having entered it, he emitted from each and every pore countless rays of light that illuminated this trichiliocosm, their wondrous radiance pervading everywhere.

Those rays of light that reached the hells caused a warm breeze to blow upon the sentient beings in the cold hells; for those sentient beings whose entire bodies were ablaze with fire, a cool breeze blew. The suffering of hunger, thirst, and exhaustion experienced by those sentient beings in the various hells was immediately extinguished, and they attained the experience of supreme bliss.”

In each and every hell, transformation Buddhas appear before the sentient beings, fully endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and adorned with their bodies by the eighty minor characteristics. Once those hell-dwelling sentient beings have experienced joy and bliss, they give rise to this thought:
"By what cause and condition has our suffering been extinguished and this experience of pleasure arisen?"
Seeing the World-Honored One’s body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty minor characteristics, he spoke these words:
“By virtue of the grace of this one who is fully endowed with great compassion, I have come to experience a state of bliss.”
With redoubled joy, a virtuous mind arose within him as he gazed up at the World-Honored One.
The World-Honored One addressed him, saying: "Ho!"
"You sentient beings!
You should speak these words:
'Namo Buddhāya.'"
"Having resolved their minds on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may you sentient beings no longer undergo suffering and always experience happiness.
They then said: "Namo Buddhāya!"
"We have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; by these roots of goodness, may our karmic offenses be forever extinguished.
Among them, those whose lives had ended were reborn in this human world;

as for those beings in hell who were being scorched by fire, once the light reached them, a cool breeze blew upon them, and all their sufferings of hunger, thirst, exhaustion, and pain were immediately extinguished. Eventually, they passed away from that state and were reborn in the human world.
The same was said for animals, hungry ghosts, and humans.
That light returned, circled the Buddha three times, and entered through the crown of his head.

Countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and asuras attained non-retrogression and dwelt in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; those countless beings also attained samādhi, patience (*kṣānti*), and dhāraṇī.

In this Jambudvīpa, in the human realm, at the residence of the king in the city of Anuçūla, within the Yaṃpila Garden, the gods, having adorned themselves with celestial ornaments for the sake of the Buddha and the Saṅgha, had this thought:

"We ought to go and behold, pay homage to, and visit the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha; we shall reverently gaze upon the Noble Assembly and listen to the True Dharma from the presence of the Tathāgata."

At that time, countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of men and women, both old and young, went daily to visit the World-Honored One, paying him respect and drawing near to him along with the community of bhikṣus, as they toured the garden in its entirety.
That garden had twenty thousand gates made of the seven precious substances; by each gate were spread five hundred jeweled couches, upon which five hundred youths sat.

To those who come to enter the garden, those youths instruct them in the threefold refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Noble Sangha; they exhort them to generate the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and establish them therein, and only then do they permit them to enter the garden, where they may see the Buddha and the Saṅgha, approach them with reverence, and survey the garden in its entirety.

“Good son! At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, for seven years exhorted countless devas to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established them therein; he exhorted countless nāgas, asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, gandharvas, pretas, piśācas, and those in the hells;
and he exhorted countless humans, urging them all to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and establishing them therein.”
He exhorted countless sentient beings to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and caused them to abide therein.

When those seven years were about to end, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta prepared eighty-four thousand golden wheels—excluding the natural wheel-treasure—and eighty-four thousand elephants adorned with the seven jewels—excluding the natural elephant-treasure—and so on, up to eighty-four thousand flavors, intending to dedicate them. During those seven years, King Vigatasaṃgha was entirely devoid of thoughts of desire, hatred, delusion, or the notion of "I"; he had no thought of being a king, no thought of giving, no thought of wife or children, no thought of food or drink, no thought of perfumes, flowers, or clothing, no thought of vehicles, no thought of sleep, no thought of pleasure, and no thought of "other" or "self."
During those seven years, he never leaned or lay down; he had no perception of day or night, nor any perception of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, or tangibles.

Throughout the seven years, he never grew weary, but constantly beheld the adornments of worlds as numerous as the atoms within a thousand Buddha-lands in each of the ten directions. The Mount Sumerus did not obstruct his vision, nor did other mountains, the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, the sun, or the moon; even the celestial palaces presented no obstruction, just as he saw the adornments of those Buddha-lands.

He contemplated the vow for the adornment of a pure buddha-field; like King Vigata-rajas, he dwelt happily for seven years through such virtues, thus beholding the adornments of the buddha-fields, as he sat contemplating the vow for the adornment of a pure buddha-field.
The princes Animiṣa, Nimba, and Indragāla, as well as the king’s thousand sons, the eighty-four thousand minor kings, and the remaining ninety-two billion sentient beings, were all likewise.

For seven years, they sat alone in one place and entered samādhi, perceiving worlds as numerous as the atoms within a thousand Buddha-lands in each of the ten directions. During those seven years, they gave rise to no thoughts of desire, harbored no thoughts of malice, and remained free from weariness; they constantly and universally beheld the adornments of Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within a thousand Buddha-lands in each of the ten directions. Mount Sumeru did not obstruct their vision, nor did the other mountains, the Iron Ring Mountains, or the Great Iron Ring Mountains; even the palaces of the sun, moon, and devas presented no hindrance. Just as they had seen the adorned Buddha-lands, they contemplated vows for the adornment of pure Buddha-lands.
All of them dwelt for seven years in such merit and happiness; some had the aspiration to adorn and purify a buddha-field, while others chose an impure buddha-field.

At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta, knowing that seven years had passed, wished to offer the seven treasures as a dedicated gift to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha; with palms joined in reverence, he addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”
I exhorted King Vigataraṇa toward anuttarasamyaksambodhi.
He returned home of his own accord, sat alone in one place, and entered samādhi; no one dared to enter, and no one was able to awaken him.

In this way, I exhorted that king’s thousand sons toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; they likewise each returned to their own homes and entered into *samādhi* while alone in a single place. No one dared to enter there, and no one was able to awaken them.

I have done the same: I have exhorted eighty-four thousand minor kings, as well as ninety-two billion other sentient beings, to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Although they have all returned to their respective homes, they are all gathered in one place and have entered into *samādhi*, such that no one is able to enter it.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will awaken King Vigataraṇa and cause him to arise from his samādhi and come here;

likewise, may all those whom I have exhorted toward bodhi also come, as well as all those who sit alone in samādhi. May they take up the resolve for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi without wavering, and in the presence of the World-Honored One, receive the prediction of their names and their buddha-lands.

“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha entered a samādhi named Nairātmyapada. From his mouth issued rays of light—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and purple. To those dwelling in that samādhi, all manifested brāhmaṇas stood before them and spoke these words:
‘Arise!’”
“Great Being!
Go to see the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus, and attend upon them with reverence.

After the Great Being, the brahmin Sāgara, had completed seven years of *pañcāṅgika* asceticism, the World-Honored One desired to travel through various villages. Having heard the brahmin’s words, they all rose up.
Upon hearing these words, King Vigataraṇa rose from his seat. In the sky, the gods beat bells and drums and performed celestial music.

Then King Vigataraṇa personally mounted a chariot together with his thousand sons, eighty-four thousand minor kings, and ninety-two billion other sentient beings; surrounded by them all, he left the city and proceeded to where the World-Honored One was.
Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the feet of the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, then withdrew to sit to one side;
King Vigatāraṇi was there together with countless billions of sentient beings.
At that time, the brahmin Sāgara-jīva said to King Vigatāraṇi:
"Great King!
You should give rise to sympathetic joy regarding this gift.
Great King!"

For three months you have made offerings to the World-Honored One with all his necessities, as well as to the countless community of bhikṣus; having dedicated various miscellaneous jewels and dedicated eighty-four thousand cities, by means of this merit from rejoicing, all of this may be dedicated toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

In this same manner, he exhorted the king’s thousand sons, the eighty-four thousand minor kings, and many other billions of sentient beings; by means of these meritorious acts of sympathetic joy, he exhorted them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established them therein—this is the *dakṣiṇā* that should be rejoiced in and dedicated.
And he spoke in verse:
"By this giving, I do not seek the state of Śakra, nor do I seek the fruit of Brahmā;
for these are precarious and unstable like a swift wind—how much less would I seek the blessings of a worldly king?"
Having attained the wondrous Bodhi of mastery over the mind, I shall deliver immeasurable sentient beings;
The fruit of this giving is exceedingly vast— May all that I aspire for be fully realized.
The Great Vehicle Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Volume Two.
The Great Vehicle Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Volume Three.
The name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost; it is now appended to the Qin Records.
Chapter Six: The Prophecy of King Aruṇa “Good son!
At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha had this thought:”

"He has exhorted many billions of sentient beings toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established them on the stage of non-retrogression; I should now bestow upon him a prediction of enlightenment and reveal his buddha-field."
At that time, the World-Honored One entered a samādhi called "Never Forgetting the Bodhicitta" and immediately manifested a smile.

Having smiled, his wondrous light universally illuminated immeasurable and boundless buddha-fields, revealing to King Vigataraṇa and many other billions of sentient beings the adornments of those buddha-lands.

At that time, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas from countless buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, having seen the light, came to this world by the Buddha’s majestic power. They approached to behold, pay homage to, and draw near to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus. With various bodhisattva supernormal powers they made offerings to the World-Honored One, prostrating their heads at his feet.
Having prostrated, they each sat to one side before the World-Honored One in order to hear the bestowal of the prediction regarding the vows of bodhisattvas.
“Good son! At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, said to King Vigatasaṃgha:
‘Great King!’”
“You may first take up the adornment of a buddha-field. “Good son!
At that time, King Vigataraṇa joined his palms toward the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Buddha, saying:”
“World-Honored One!
I delight in seeking bodhi.

For three months, I shall provide all necessities for the World-Honored One and the assembly of countless bhikṣus. I dedicate these roots of goodness toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, solely so that I may not remain in this defiled buddha-field.”
“World-Honored One!
Having contemplated the adornment of a buddha-field for these seven years, World-Honored One, may there be no hells, hungry ghosts, or animals therein;

may I attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in such a place. I pray that those who pass away there shall not fall into the evil destinies, and that all shall be universally golden in color, with no difference between humans and devas.”
May the sentient beings therein all spontaneously recognize their own past lives throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of kalpas.
May all sentient beings therein possess this divine eye and see the Buddhas currently dwelling in and preaching the Dharma within more than hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of worlds.
May all sentient beings therein possess this divine ear, hearing the Dharma taught by hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of Buddhas dwelling in the world.

May all sentient beings therein be well-endowed with the knowledge of others' minds, thus knowing the mental activities and thoughts of sentient beings across many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of Buddha-fields.
May all therein be fully endowed with supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*), such that in a single thought-moment they pass through billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields.
May the sentient beings therein be without "self" or "what belongs to self," and without any agency, even regarding their own bodies.
May all sentient beings therein attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

May all sentient beings therein be born by transformation; may there be no women therein, and may the lifespan of the sentient beings therein be immeasurable, except for those who have made other vows.
May there be no mention of unwholesome deeds among the sentient beings therein; may his Buddha-land be free from foul odors, and may fragrances pervade it, surpassing even those of the heavens.
May all sentient beings therein be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man.
May all sentient beings therein attain the stage of being "born once more" before Buddhahood, except for those who have made other vows.

May all sentient beings therein, by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, pass through countless Buddha-lands within the time it takes to eat a small meal, approach and dwell in the presence of countless Buddhas of the world, and thereby achieve accomplishment.
According to their desires, may they employ the supernatural transformations of a Bodhisattva to make offerings to the Buddhas, and then return to their own lands within that same duration of a meal.
May all sentient beings therein each proclaim the Buddha-treasury.
May all those sentient beings be endowed with the strength of Nārāyaṇa.
May immeasurable sentient beings be able to fully know the adorned forms and images within that buddha-field—things which cannot even be known by the divine eye.
May all sentient beings therein attain unimpeded, incalculable eloquence.
May each individual Bodhi tree be one thousand yojanas in height.
May the Buddha-field be luminous and pure, with countless adorned Buddha-fields appearing within it on every side.
May all sentient beings who are born here possess pure conduct (*brahmacarya*) until they reach the limit of enlightenment.
May every sentient being therein be honored and venerated by those free from adversity, and may none among them have incomplete sense faculties until they reach the limit of enlightenment.
May the beings born therein attain the noble joy and bliss that surpasses that of the devas.
May all roots of goodness be gathered therein.
May all beings born therein be spontaneously clothed in saffron robes at the moment of birth.

May the sentient beings born therein attain the skillful discernment of various samādhis; by means of these samādhis, may they travel to countless Buddha-fields to attend upon the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, never failing to behold them until the limit of a bodhisattva’s enlightenment. May those bodhisattvas who are reborn therein, according to their wishes, have the adornments of the Buddha-field appear exactly as they conceive them, manifesting within the jeweled trees of that adorned field.

May all sentient beings born therein attain the Samādhi of Universal Arrival; by means of this samādhi, may they universally behold the Buddhas currently residing in countless Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions, never failing to see them until the very limit of enlightenment.
May those born there obtain such clothing, palaces, ornaments, necklaces, forms, and colors as those of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods.
May their land be free of earth, stones, and black mountains, and likewise free of the Cakravāḍa, Mahācakravāḍa, Sumeru, and the great oceans.
May there be no sound of obstacles or fetters within it.
May there be universally no sound of hell-beings, animals, or hungry ghosts; no sound of the various difficulties; no sound of suffering; and no sound that is neither pleasant nor painful.
"I now wish to seek such a buddha-field.
World-Honored One!
When I was a bodhisattva, I practiced such difficult deeds as these; I shall adorn and purify a buddha-field in this manner."
“‘Bhagavān! This is the conduct of a great man; only after this shall I attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
May my bodhi tree be ten thousand yojanas high, and may I, sitting beneath it, realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the mere time it takes to conceive that thought.’”
May my radiance be immeasurable, illuminating billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields.
May my lifespan be countless billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of kalpas, such that no one is able to calculate it, except for the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñajñāna).
May my assembly of bodhisattvas be so innumerable that no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas are able to count them, except for those possessing the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).
When we attain Buddhahood, may other immeasurable asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields, all buddha-fields, and all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, praise and extol us.

When I attain enlightenment, may those sentient beings in countless other *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields who hear my name dedicate their roots of goodness toward my land; after the end of their lives, may they be reborn in my land, with the exception of those who have committed the five crimes of immediate retribution, those who slander the noble ones, and those who reject the true Dharma.

"When I attain Bodhi, may the sentient beings in countless other Buddha-lands who resolve to attain Bodhi and vow to be born in my land dedicate their roots of goodness; when they are about to pass away, may I appear before them, surrounded by an immeasurable assembly.
Having seen me, may they experience great joy toward me, have all obstacles removed, and after their lives end, be reborn in my land.
Among them, may the Bodhisattvas hear, according to their inclinations, any Dharma they have not yet heard."
When I attain Bodhi, may all Bodhisattvas in incalculable Buddha-fields who hear my name attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi;
may they obtain the first, second, or third *kṣānti* according to their wishes;
and may they immediately attain, at will, samādhis, *kṣāntis*, and dhāraṇīs.

After my parinirvāṇa, may Bodhisattvas in countless eons and countless Buddha-fields who hear my name attain supreme joy; may they pay homage to me, experience what has never been before, and praise and extol me, saying:
"When he was a Bodhisattva, he performed the work of a Buddha, and only thereafter did he attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Having attained extreme joy, they obtain the first, second, and third patiences (*kṣānti*) of a bodhisattva; according to their wishes, they immediately attain samādhis, patiences, and dhāraṇīs as they desire, which continue without interruption until the limit of enlightenment (*bodhi*).

May it be that when I attain bodhi, any woman in incalculable Buddha-fields who hears my name shall experience supreme joy, resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and never again receive a female body until she reaches the limit of bodhi.

May it be that after my parinirvāṇa, those women in countless Buddha-fields who hear my name shall attain supreme joy, dedicate their merit toward the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and never again receive a female body until they reach the limit of enlightenment.
I pray that the World-Honored One may grant my wish!
I seek such a buddha-field, such beings of pure intention, and within such a buddha-field, I shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha addressed King Vigataraṇa, saying:
'Excellent, excellent!'"
Great King!
Your aspiration is most profound.
Great King!
He has taken up a pure buddha-field and purified the minds of sentient beings.
Observe, Great King!

To the west, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of buddha-fields, there is a world named Dustless Sovereignty (*Anavila-vijaya*). Its Buddha is named Sovereign King of Imperial Radiance Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells in the world, teaching exclusively the Dharma of the One Vehicle to bodhisattvas.
In that Buddha-land, there are no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor even their names; the teaching of śrāvakas is not spoken, but only the Mahāyāna is taught.
All sentient beings therein are born by transformation, and among them, even the name "woman" does not exist.
That buddha-field possesses all these virtues, just as the Great King had wished; it takes up immeasurable adornments of a buddha-land and gathers and delivers immeasurable beings of pure intent.
Therefore, Great King,
I name you Amitābha (Immeasurable Purity).
That Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śikhin-vibhu-rāja will enter parinirvāṇa at the end of one intermediate kalpa.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King of Sovereign Radiance shall have his True Dharma remain in the world for ten minor kalpas;

after the extinction of the True Dharma, following sixty minor kalpas, that world shall be named Meruprabhā, and that Buddha shall be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King of the Virtue of Inconceivable Intent.

Just as the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Śakrābhilāgitasvairarāja in the world-system Indravimala is adorned, so too is the Buddha-land of the Tathāgata Acintyamatiguṇarāja in the world-system Meruprabhā adorned; they are identical and no different.
The lifespan of that Tathāgata Acintyamateratnarāja was sixty minor kalpas;
after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Acintyamateratnarāja, the True Dharma remained in the world for sixteen minor kalpas;
and after the extinction of the True Dharma, when a thousand minor kalpas had passed, there was a world named Ananda where the Buddha was named Ratnarcis Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.

Briefly stated, their lifespans will be equal, and their worlds will likewise be equal; after this True Dharma has remained in the world and subsequently perished, that world shall be named Sāla. A Buddha named Ratnadhvaja-svaravijitagarjita Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, will appear in that world, and his buddha-field’s adornments will be equal [to others].

That Buddha will dwell in the world preaching the Dharma for thirty-five intermediate kalpas, and after that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma will remain in the world for seven intermediate kalpas.

After the extinction of the True Dharma, to speak briefly: in that world, immeasurable and innumerable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, have attained Buddhahood and entered nirvana; yet that world has never undergone formation or destruction.

"Anantaprasanna, in a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed and at the beginning of the second asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, that world shall be named Sukhāvatī.
Anantaprasanna, therein you shall attain anuttarasamyaksambodhi, and your name shall be Amitābha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
Then the king said:
"Yes! World-Honored One!"
"Where are those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas now, who were previously before me in that buddha-field to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
The Buddha said, “Amitābha!

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have come from immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya, ineffable, and incalculable worlds throughout the ten directions to pay homage, revere, and attend upon me, sitting here to listen to the Dharma. All the Buddhas of the past have bestowed upon them the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones of the present, likewise bestow upon these sons of good family the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
Among those in that buddha-field who have first attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, O Immeasurable Purity!
each and every one of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has planted various roots of goodness and cultivated wisdom under countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddhas.
“O Amitābha! That son of good family shall first attain Buddhahood within that Buddha-land.
The King said:
"O World-Honored One!
This Brahmin Sāgaramegha has exhorted me and my retinue toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; after how much time will he realize bodhi?"
The Buddha said:
"O Great King! This great Brahmin is fully endowed with great compassion;
you shall surely hear his lion's roar yourself."
Then the king said:
"If the World-Honored One grants me this prediction as he has done, my vow shall surely be fulfilled.

When I prostrate my five limbs at the feet of the World-Honored One, may worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges tremble, and may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently residing in those Buddha-lands, grant me their prediction."

"Good son! At that time, when King Amitāśuddha prostrated himself with his five limbs before the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, touching his head to the ground, Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges immediately shook, surged, and subsided. Then, Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, bestowed upon him this prediction:
'In the Sāṃdṛṣṭika Buddha-land, during the eon named Dhāraṇī, among people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, you shall become a Buddha named Ratnagarbha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.'"

The wheel-turning king of the four continents shall be named Immeasurable Purity (Amitavyūha). Having planted roots of merit under the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, that king, after the passing of more than a *asaṃkhyeya* of *kalpas* equal in number to the sands of the Ganges, will enter the second *asaṃkhyeya* of *kalpas* when the world system shall be named Sukhāvatī.

That King Immeasurable Purity shall therein attain Buddhahood, named Tathāgata Amitābha, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, whose radiance shall universally illumine worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions.
The Buddhas addressed him, saying:
"O Sage of Wondrous Wisdom, you may now arise; the Ten-Powered Ones have already bestowed upon you the prediction.
The mountains and lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges tremble everywhere; you shall become a Honored One among Men, a Supreme Tamer."
“Good son! At that time, King Immeasurable Purity was filled with joy and exultation; he rose from his seat, sat to one side, and listened to the Dharma.
Chapter Seven: The Prophecy for the Three Princes. *The Great Vehicle Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, Chapter Seven: The Prophecy for the Three Princes. “Good son!”
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta said to Animiṣa, the eldest son of King Anantavimala: "In brief,
I have observed the evil realms, wherein sentient beings undergo suffering most acutely."
Furthermore, I observe those in the heavens; because their minds are defiled and turbid, they frequently fall into the evil realms.

I have already observed all sentient beings who, being separated from virtuous friends, dwell in the dharma of poverty and inhabit the darkness until their roots of goodness are exhausted, being shrouded by false views and distressed upon the wrong paths.
"O World-Honored One!
I shall address those sentient beings with a loud voice and dedicate all roots of goodness toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

When I practice the bodhisattva path, if there are sentient beings oppressed by suffering and pain, or those who are terrified, impoverished in the Dharma, dwelling in darkness without refuge, lacking light, lacking rescue, lacking a home, and lacking a destination—if such beings should bring me to mind and call upon my name;

and if, with my divine ear, I hear their voices, and with my divine eye, I see them, yet I do not deliver those sentient beings from their distress and peril, then I shall never attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“World-Honored One!

Just as I have long practiced the bodhisattva path for the sake of making vows for sentient beings, may this intention be fulfilled just like that of the Great King: after one *asaṃkhyeya* of *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* eons, at the beginning of the second *asaṃkhyeya* of *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* eons, I shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the world-realm Sukhāvatī, becoming known as the Tathāgata Amitābha, performing the Buddha-work by purifying the buddha-field and purifying the minds of sentient beings;

and even until the Tathāgata Amitābha, having performed the Buddha-work for immeasurable eons, enters *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa*, I shall continue to practice the bodhisattva path for as long as his True Dharma remains in the world.”

I shall perform the work of a Buddha as a bodhisattva until the end of the True Dharma of the Tathāgata Amitābha; at the very moment it extinguishes during the first watch of the night, I shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi during the final watch.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Likewise, throughout the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, where the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently reside, I shall also address those Buddhas with my voice; those Buddhas shall likewise grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Good son! The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha then bestowed upon him this prediction:
'As for you, good son!'"

Having already observed the miserable realms and further observed the heavens, one contemplates the suffering of sentient beings and is able to give rise to a heart of compassion; for the sake of liberating all sentient beings from suffering, for the sake of eliminating the fetters and afflictions, and for the sake of enabling them to attain happiness.
Therefore, O son of good family!
I shall name you Avalokiteśvara.
You, Avalokiteśvara, shall deliver many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings from suffering.
"You, son of good family!

While acting as a bodhisattva, you shall perform the work of a Buddha. After the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Amitābha, at the end of two *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas equal to the sands of the Ganges, once the True Dharma of the Tathāgata Amitābha has ceased during the first watch of the night, immediately thereafter in the latter watch of the night, the World of Peace and Bliss (Sukhāvatī) shall be named 'Gathering of All Jewels' (*Sarvaratnasaṃcaya*). The adornments of that land shall be immeasurably more excellent than those of the Land of Peace and Bliss."

Then, during the latter part of the night, you, son of good family, will sit upon the diamond throne beneath a bodhi tree adorned with immeasurable jewels and attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, becoming the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named King of the Accumulated Virtue of Universal Radiance and Supreme Honor, with a lifespan of ninety-six billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
"After you have entered parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for sixty-two billion kalpas.
Avalokiteśvara said,
"World-Honored One!"

If my intention is thus fulfilled, when I prostrate at the feet of the World-Honored One, may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, bestow upon me their prediction of enlightenment; may the earth in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges tremble; may the five kinds of musical sounds emerge from all mountains, rivers, stone walls, trees, and groves; and may the minds of all sentient beings attain freedom from desire.

As soon as Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva prostrated with his five limbs before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the lands of as many Buddhas as there are sands in the Ganges all trembled; those Tathāgatas all bestowed upon him predictions of enlightenment, which are here briefly described.
From all mountains, rivers, stone walls, trees, and forests, the sounds of the five kinds of music emerged, and the minds of all sentient beings attained freedom from desire.
The Buddha said:
“Arising from compassion, merit, and joyful sounds, The Buddhas of the ten directions bestow upon you this prediction.”
“The earth and the world shall shake in six ways; you shall become a Buddha, a World-Saving Sage.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaramegha, the royal preceptor, spoke to the second prince, Nimi, saying:”
“Good son! You should rejoice in this great giving;

furthermore, regarding the wholesome karma you have performed, because it is for the sake of all sentient beings, you have resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and dedicated it toward sarvajñā.”
“Good son! At that time, Prince Nimo addressed these words before the Buddha:

‘I shall provide all necessary offerings to the World-Honored One and to the countless community of bhikṣus. Furthermore, I shall dedicate all roots of merit arising from this act of sympathetic joy, as well as all previous wholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind, toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; yet, I shall never realize bodhi within this defiled buddha-field.’”

In the world-system Sarvaratnasamcaya, where the youth Avalokiteśvara shall sit beneath a bodhi tree adorned with immeasurable jewels and attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*—there he shall be named King of the Accumulated Merit of Universal Supreme Radiance (*Prabhāsa-sarvottama-guṇasaṃcaya-rāja*).
I first request that he preach the Dharma; for as long as that Tathāgata remains in the world expounding the Dharma, for that same duration shall I practice the bodhisattva path.
"After that Tathāgata has passed into extinction and the True Dharma has vanished, I shall next attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
May my Buddha-field be adorned in this very same way, and may I likewise perform the work of a Buddha.

After my Parinirvāṇa, may the duration for which the True Dharma remains in the world be likewise the same. May I obtain all such adornments, just like those of the Tathāgata King of Universal Radiance and Accumulated Virtue."
The Buddha said:
“Good son! You have taken up the great objective; you shall surely attain this state.”
"Just as you have perceived it, O son of good family!
You shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in that buddha-field, and your name shall be Tathāgata King of the Accumulated Merit of the Well-Settled Maṇi."
"Because you, son of good family, have taken up this great resolve, I shall name you Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
He addressed the World-Honored One:

"If my intention may be fulfilled in this way, then as I prostrate with my five limbs at the feet of the World-Honored One, may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, bestow upon me their prediction [of enlightenment], and may Mandārava flowers rain down."

“Good son! When the good son Mahāsthāmaprāpta prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, bestowed upon him their prediction of enlightenment. The great earth shook in six ways, and flowers of sumanā fell like rain.”
The Buddha said:
"Arise with firm power and swift merit; the World-Honored Ones of the ten directions have already bestowed their prediction upon you.
The earth has shaken and the *sumana* flowers have rained down; among gods and humans, you shall be the Brahmā."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke briefly to the third prince, Rājasaṃmata.
With palms joined in reverence, he addressed the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, saying:”

"I have already provided all necessary offerings to the World-Honored One and the community of bhikṣus; furthermore, I dedicate all my wholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind, as well as this merit resulting from sympathetic joy, entirely toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. I shall never attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a defiled buddha-field, nor shall I achieve it too quickly."

When I have thus attained bodhi and am practicing the bodhisattva path, I see the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in immeasurable and boundless other worlds throughout the ten directions, whom I previously exhorted and transformed toward bodhi.
"I exhort them to generate the bodhicitta; I cause them to abide in the bodhicitta; I exhort them with the pāramitās, causing them to dwell therein.

When I practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, with my divine eye I see, in each and every direction, within Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in a Ganges-sand number of buddha-lands, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who preach the Dharma and whom I have exhorted and transformed toward bodhi. In this manner shall I practice the conduct of a bodhisattva and perform the work of a Buddha."

For that length of time I practiced the bodhisattva path, purifying the bodies and minds of sentient beings in this way; those born in my buddha-field will be like the sons of gods in the Brahma world, and the adornment and purity of my buddha-field will also be like that of the Brahma world.

I shall cause my single buddha-field to be like as many trichiliocosms as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; I shall cause that buddha-field to be surrounded by walls composed of countless hundreds of thousands of various jewels, interspersed and magnificently adorned, reaching as high as the Peak of Existence.
May that buddha-field consist entirely of lapis lazuli, with its ground everywhere soft, fine, and smooth; may it be free from dust, gravel, and all impurities;
may there not even be the name "woman" therein;

may all sentient beings therein be born through transformation; may the sentient beings therein have no need for solid food, but instead subsist on the food of Dharma, the food of joy, and the food of samādhi.
