May that buddha-field be such that even the names "śrāvaka" and "pratyekabuddha" do not exist; may that buddha-field be filled exclusively with bodhisattvas who dwell in pure brahmacarya, free from the disturbances of afflictions.

May all the bodhisattvas therein be born with the robes and physical form of śramaṇas; as soon as they are born, may they think of food, and may bowls filled with rice of immeasurable flavors appear in their right hands.
Having obtained this, they give rise to this thought:

"It is not fitting for us to eat this morsel-food; we should take this food to other worlds to offer it to the Buddhas currently dwelling in the world, along with their śrāvakas and the poor, as well as to the hungry ghosts who are exhausted by hunger and thirst and whose bodies are aflame, so that we may provide them with sustenance, while we ourselves should abide in the food of joy."
As soon as those bodhisattvas had thus resolved their minds, they attained the inconceivable samādhi of majestic deportment; by means of this samādhi, they remained free from all attachment.

He travels to the immeasurable, incalculable other Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions; there he makes offerings to the currently dwelling Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as well as to their śrāvakas and other sentient beings, and also bestows gifts upon the hungry ghosts. Having preached the Dharma for them, he returns to his own land within the duration of a small meal.

In this manner, within the duration of a small meal, they returned to their own lands and further exchanged robes with one another, even including all the articles of worship possessed by those bodhisattvas within their respective buddha-fields.
May he cause all these offerings to be presented to all Buddhas, as well as to the śrāvakas and other sentient beings, and only thereafter use them himself.

May his buddha-field be free from the eight difficulties and from unwholesome sounds; may it also be without sounds of suffering, and furthermore, without sounds of receiving precepts or repenting for transgressions.
May that buddha-field be adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of various jewels, interspersed with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of various jewels.

May it manifest all manner of forms and images like a *maṇi* gem; from the ten directions, *maṇi* jewels shall come forth—such as have never been seen before and never heard of before—jewels such as these being rare in the world.

Even if one were to spend a hundred million years speaking the names of those various jewels, they could not be exhausted. If there is a bodhisattva who wishes to see gold in the buddha-field, they shall immediately see gold; if they wish to see silver, they shall immediately see silver, yet the gold remains unimpaired.
To state the essentials briefly: for those who wish to see crystal, lapis lazuli, agate, red pearls, and musaragalva, they shall be made to see such various jewel-adorned buddha-fields.

There are *agaru*, *kālānusāri*, *tāmālapatra*, and *sāgara-tīra-candana* incenses; if there are bodhisattvas who wish to see the *gośīrṣa-candana* buddha-fields, he causes them to see them immediately, causing them all to see whatever they desire.
May they wish to see one another yet not behold each other, so that all their aspirations may be completely fulfilled.

May that buddha-field be without sun or moon; when bodhisattvas are born there, may their bodies possess radiance, emitting such light as they desire to illuminate, reaching even unto hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of buddha-fields.
May that buddha-field be such that it has no names for day or night, but is known only by the closing of flowers.

May that buddha-land be free from cold and heat, illness, old age, and death; there shall be only bodhisattvas who, desiring to achieve awakening, go to the Tuṣita heaven in another world and attain awakening there at the end of their lives.

He causes that buddha-field to be free of death; he causes [beings] to attain unsurpassed parinirvāṇa through the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata in the space above; and therein, whatever requisites those bodhisattvas desire, they all obtain them.

He caused hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of musical instruments to resound in the void of all buddha-fields; from these instruments there issued no sounds of sensual desire, but only the sounds of the *pāramitās*, the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṃgha, and the sound of the Bodhisattva Dharma-treasury, so that they might hear such sounds according to the inclinations of the bodhisattvas.

“‘Bhagavān! When I practice the conduct of awakening, may I see the adornments of many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of Buddha-fields throughout immeasurable, boundless, asaṃkhyeya Buddha-lands. May all those adornments, necklaces, their characteristics, their auspicious omens, their locations, their practices, and their vows be present within my own Buddha-field—except for the five corruptions of the Buddha-fields of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.’”

May that land be such that even the names of the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts do not exist; furthermore, may it be free from Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, and all mountains of earth and stone, as well as the great oceans.
May there be no other trees remaining therein, but only various jewel-trees surpassing those of the heavens, arranged in rows throughout that buddha-field.
Furthermore, may there be no other flowers, but only celestial *māndārava* flowers; may all foul odors and impurities be absent, and may various exquisite fragrances fill the buddha-field.

May all those born therein be bodhisattvas in their final birth before enlightenment (ekajātipratibaddha), so that not a single sentient being shall regress and be reborn elsewhere; and may those who do pass away from Tuṣita Heaven attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
“‘World-Honored One!

For that duration of time, I shall practice as a bodhisattva; I shall then accomplish such a conduct of a great man (mahāsattva), establishing such adorned buddha-fields, with such pure intentions, and filling those lands with bodhisattvas who will succeed to their positions in a single lifetime.’”
I shall ensure that there is not a single bodhisattva therein who has not been transformed by me, and none among them who has not been established in the *pāramitās* for the sake of awakening.
Furthermore, those bodhisattvas who are born there shall also be ones whom I previously exhorted and transformed toward awakening and the establishment in the *pāramitās*.
"Now, may they be brought into this Buddha-field, and all these sufferings shall be extinguished. Pray,
World-Honored One!"
When I was a bodhisattva, I accomplished such deeds of a great man, and only thereafter did I attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in that buddha-field.

May the trunk of my Bodhi tree have a circumference equal to ten thousand four-continent worlds, and may its branches and leaves extend for thirteen thousand worlds in every direction; let it be named "The Manifestation of All Jewels.
May the radiance and fragrance of that Bodhi tree pervade the entirety of that Buddha-field.

Beneath it is my Vajra-seat, interspersed with various jewels, equal in length and breadth to four and five *caturdvīpa* worlds, eighty-four thousand *yojana*s in height, named "The Fragrance of Skillful Wisdom that Universally Radiates Inexhaustible Light."

Beneath that Bodhi tree, upon the adamantine throne, I sat cross-legged; in a brief moment, I attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and until my parinirvāṇa, I never altered this seat nor did I abandon it.
Seated beneath the Bodhi tree upon the adamantine throne, I shall not rise until I have dispatched emanated Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to countless Buddha-fields;

each emanated Buddha shall preach the Dharma to sentient beings for the duration of a single small meal, and during that same interval, shall exhort countless sentient beings toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, causing them to abide therein and attain non-retrogression;
I shall cause the emanated Bodhisattvas to act in the same manner.

May it be that when I attain Bodhi, my body shall appear universally throughout countless worlds in the ten directions; and should there be any sentient beings who behold the marks and signs of my body’s adornment, may all those sentient beings become firm in their resolve for Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, until they reach final Nirvāṇa in supreme Bodhi, such that those beings never fail to see the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.

May there be none among them who lack any of the sense faculties. Among them, those bodhisattvas who wish to see me shall have their walking, sitting, and standing follow wherever they go; as soon as those bodhisattvas turn their minds toward mindfulness of the Buddha, may it be so.

May they see me seated beneath the Bodhi tree; having seen me, may their doubts regarding whatever dharmas they have been questioning be suddenly and completely resolved, even without my uttering a single word of Dharma, so that they may understand its meaning.

May my lifespan be immeasurable, such that no one can count it except through the wisdom of *sarvajñā* (omniscience), and may the lifespans of those bodhisattvas also be immeasurable. When I wish to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in that buddha-field, may such auspicious signs and portents appear.
It means that all the bodhisattvas in that buddha-field have their heads shaven and wear the *kāṣāya* robes until they enter parinirvāṇa.
In that buddha-field, there is not a single person who wears decorated hair or lay clothing; they all abide in the appearance of śramaṇas without exception.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent! O virtuous man!"

"You too are sagacious and possessed of understanding and wisdom; your aspiration is most excellent, your resolve is exceedingly great, your majestic virtue is particularly sublime, and your wisdom is most wondrous.
O son of good family!"
Because you have been able, for the sake of all sentient beings, to personally conceive such a wondrous and supreme resolve to take up a wondrously adorned Buddha-land.
Therefore, son of good family!
I name you Manjusri. Manjusri!

In a future age, after two *asamkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges have passed, and at the beginning of the third *asamkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world in the southern direction named Pure and Free from Accumulated Dust; this Sahā world shall also be included within it, adorned with such magnificent and pure buddha-fields. You, Manjusri!
Within this realm, you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Universal Manifestation (*Samantamukha*).
Such a host of bodhisattvas as you have vowed for will all be fully accomplished, exactly according to your aspirations.
When you were a bodhisattva, you planted various roots of goodness in the presence of many billions of Buddhas.
O Mañjuśrī! You are a fine medicine for sentient beings;
you remove the afflictions of the mind, extinguish the multitude of fetters, and increase their roots of goodness.
Then Manjusri said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One!

If my intention is thus fulfilled according to my vow, may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the world and preaching the Dharma throughout the immeasurable *asamkhyeya* worlds of the ten directions, grant me a prediction of enlightenment. May immeasurable *asamkhyeya* Buddha-lands all tremble; may all sentient beings obtain such joy and fulfillment as that of a Bodhisattva sporting in the second dhyāna-samādhi; and may the *mandārava* flowers rain down upon immeasurable *asamkhyeya* Buddha-lands, and may those *mandārava* flowers produce such sounds as these: the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Sangha, the sound of the *pāramitās*, and the sound of the powers and fearlessnesses.”
"If I prostrate my five limbs at the feet of the World-Honored One, may such auspicious responses as these all be made to appear.

Just as when the youth Mañjuśrī prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, the earth in immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* buddha-fields trembled, and *mandārava* flowers rained down; all sentient beings attained such bliss, and their aspirations were thus fulfilled.
Among them, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had heard the Dharma from the various Buddhas all questioned the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones:
"By what cause and by what condition has this auspicious omen appeared?"
All those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, bestowed upon Mañjuśrī the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Buddha spoke in verse:
“Having aroused the supreme mind and vast wisdom, The Lords of the Ten Directions who save the world have bestowed this prediction upon you.”
"The earth shook and flowers rained down as all beings rejoiced: 'You shall become a Buddha and appear in the world.
Chapter Eight: The Prophecy for the Four Princes *The Great Vehicle Sutra of the Compassionate White Lotus* "O son of good family!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta addressed the fourth prince, Viśeṣamati.
To speak briefly, his aspiration was no different from that of Mañjuśrī.
The World-Honored One praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family!

When you are a bodhisattva, you shall shatter the diamond mountains of the fetters and afflictions of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings and perform the work of a Buddha; thereafter, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
"Good son!
For this reason, I name you Vajranāśaprajñālokaśrī.

You, Vajranāśaprajñālokaśrī, in a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed and you have entered the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa, there will be a land named Animiṣa to the east, beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in ten *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* buddha-fields."
"Good son!

Within this realm you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and your name shall be the Tathāgata Samantabhadra, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, up to Buddha Bhagavān. The immeasurable adornments of that buddha-field shall likewise be just as you have vowed."

“Good son! As soon as the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramativibhāsa, immeasurable billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of devas in the void all praised him, saying:
‘Excellent!’”
Vṛṣṭisāgara offered on this side of the ocean *gośīrṣa*, *agaru*, *candana*, and powdered incense.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Yes! [I do so]."

"Bhagavān! If my intention is thus fulfilled— such that when I prostrate with my five limbs at the Buddha’s feet, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are filled with exquisite celestial fragrances—

and if the beings therein, whether in the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, among humans, or among devas, should smell this fragrance, may their physical and mental suffering and afflictions find relief for as long as it takes for my head to touch the ground."

“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Huājīngānghuìmíngzhào prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Bǎozàng. Instantly, worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges were suffused with a sublime fragrance surpassing that of the heavens, and all the physical and mental sufferings of every sentient being therein were completely stilled.”
The Buddha said:
"Arising, you can shatter the diamond; your fragrance and color fill the lands.
Bringing joy and happiness to many sentient beings, you are the Knower of the World."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke briefly to the fifth prince, Abhaya:
‘World-Honored One!...’”

I do not wish to take up this defiled and turbid buddha-field; you should know that I shall attain *samyaksambodhi* in a place where there are no hells, animals, or hungry ghosts, and where the ground of sapphire is adorned as described for the Lotus World.
Prince Abhaya placed a lotus flower before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O World-Honored One! ”

If my wish is thus fulfilled, may I, by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, attain the Samādhi of Manifest Adornment; and just as I am now before the World-Honored One, may I behold rainfalls of lotus flowers as large as chariot wheels throughout Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within Ganges-sands of worlds in the ten directions.

As soon as these words were spoken, through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, he attained the Samādhi of Manifesting Adornments; then, from Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within worlds as many as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, there fell rains of lotus flowers as large as chariot wheels.
Upon seeing this, Prince Abhaya was filled with supreme joy.
The Buddha said,
"Good son!..."
“Your aspiration is most excellent; you have taken up a wondrous buddha-field and, through your words of utmost sincerity, shall swiftly attain samādhi and rain down lotus flowers.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If I am to fulfill my intention for unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, may these lotus flowers hang suspended in the air and remain in the air immediately upon this moment.”
The Buddha said, "Good son!
What you have done is exceedingly swift; you have sealed the void with the Lotus Seal."
"Good son! For this reason, I name you 'Seal of Space' (Gaganamudrā).

You, Gaganamudrā, in a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed and at the beginning of the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world named Padma in the southeastern direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. There, you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and your title shall be Padmottara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, up to Buddha Bhagavān."
"The assembly of pure bodhisattvas shall be immeasurable in number, and their lifespan shall likewise be immeasurable; they will certainly attain all such majestic virtues as you have vowed.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā prostrated himself on the ground with his five limbs touching the earth to pay homage at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
The Buddha said:
"You shall benefit the world, eliminating the defilements of the fetters;
possessing virtues as numerous as the atoms of a world-system, you shall attain awakening, even more excellent than before."

“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke to the sixth prince, Ākāśa. To speak briefly, he did not [aspire] for this defiled buddha-field; the details are as in the vow of the bodhisattva Gaganamudrā.”
“World-Honored One!

If my intention is thus fulfilled, may there appear in the void of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions seven-jeweled canopies, covered above by nets of white pearls and adorned with suspended clusters of precious bells.”
From within the net of precious bells, such sounds emerged, namely:
the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṅgha, the sound of the pāramitās, the sound of the powers, the sound of the superknowledges, and the sound of fearlessness;
all sentient beings therein were made to hear these sounds, causing them to resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"May those who have previously resolved upon bodhicitta not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

As soon as these words were spoken, throughout the entirety of the voids in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions—in brief—a voice such as this resounded; through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, everyone beheld it for themselves.
He addressed the Buddha again, saying: "Yes!
World-Honored One!"
"If my intention is fulfilled according to my wish, may I attain the Samādhi of the Manifestation of Wisdom in the presence of the World-Honored One, thereby increasing wholesome dharmas.

Having attained this samādhi, may the World-Honored One then bestow upon me the prediction of Bodhi; through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, I shall immediately attain the Samādhi of the Manifestation of Wisdom."
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!"
Your aspiration is most wonderful.

By virtue of your meritorious deeds, you shall cover the voids of Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions with jeweled canopies, and emit gentle sounds that awaken many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings.
"Noble son!
For this reason, I name you Vidyottama (Supreme Illumination of Space). You, Vidyottama!"

In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya of kalpas equal to the sands of the Ganges has passed and you have entered the second asaṃkhyeya of kalpas equal to the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world named Candrasūrya (Moon and Sun) located two asaṃkhyeyas of Buddha-fields away to the east.

Therein, you shall attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (samyak-saṃbodhi), and you shall be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, up to Buddha, World-Honored One, named Dharmeśvaradhana-rāja (Dharma-Sovereign Wealth-King).
Then, the Bodhisattva Ākāśapratibhāsa prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
The Buddha said:
"Rise! Cultivate wholesome habits and discipline the mind; Be able to give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings."
"When I have crossed the shore of suffering for the multitude of beings, I shall awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. "Good son!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke thus to the seventh prince, Citrasena; to speak briefly, it was only that he would not [do so] within this turbid buddha-field."

"In the place where I thus attain enlightenment, there shall be no names for hell-beings, animals, or hungry ghosts; nor shall there be women, for the sentient beings therein do not emerge from a womb.

There shall be no Mount Sumeru, no Iron Ring Mountains, no Great Iron Ring Mountains, nor any mountains of earth or stone; there shall be no springs, no rubble, no thorns, no uneven terrain, no foul winds, no trees, and no great oceans. Furthermore, there shall be no sun, moon, stars, day or night, nor darkness. The sentient beings therein shall have no foul odors, excrement, urine, mucus, or saliva;
their forms shall be free from filth and stench, and their bodies and minds shall have nothing upon which to depend."
May its ground not be made of earth or stone, but consist purely of agate and be adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of various jewels.
May that buddha-field have no other grasses, but only *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.

May that buddha-field be adorned with various jewel trees; may those jewel trees be decorated with various jewel canopies, various jewel houses, various jewel garments, various jewel garlands, various jewel necklaces, various jewel ornaments, various musical instruments, various jewel vessels, and various flowers, all adorning the trees.
He causes the various flowers to close and the sounds of music to cease; by this he knows it is night.

When the flowers close, the Bodhisattva is born. As soon as he is born therein, he sits down and composes his mind, attaining the Samādhi of Manifest Adornment. By means of this samādhi, he beholds all the Buddhas currently residing in world-systems as numerous as the atoms within the lands of the ten directions.

At that time, may they attain the pure divine ear and hear the Buddhas currently dwelling in the world and preaching the Dharma in other worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.
May all beings born therein spontaneously recognize their past lives, recollecting the events of as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-land;
may they, once born, obtain the pure divine eye and universally behold the adornments of as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in the Buddhas of the ten directions;

may they, once born, be well-endowed with the knowledge of others' minds, such that in a single thought-moment they know the mental activities and thoughts of all sentient beings within as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a Buddha-land, continuing thus until their awakening and parinirvāṇa, never losing this samādhi.
When the night was about to turn into dawn, fragrant winds from the four directions—subtle, exquisite, soft, and pleasant to the touch, giving rise to joy—came and blew upon the blossoming flowers.

These caused all the bodhisattvas to awaken from their samādhi and arise upon the flower pedestals, granting them such supernatural powers that in the space of a single moment of focused thought, they could travel to Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within each direction’s buddha-fields. Having approached and paid homage to the presently living Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, they returned to their own lands and sat cross-legged upon the pedestals of *mandārava* and *mahā-mandārava* flowers. There they contemplated the Dharma-gates and gazed up at the Tathāgatas; wherever they sat, they turned in accordance with those places so that I might be seen by all in every direction.
If any of those bodhisattvas should harbor thoughts of doubt regarding the Dharma, they shall be made to contemplate my body so that their vision becomes immediately clear and vast.
Furthermore, whatever Dharma those bodhisattvas wish to hear, as soon as they contemplate me, I shall cause them to know it all.

Within that realm, the bodhisattvas are made free of the notion of "mine," and they have no purposeful striving even regarding their own bodies and lives; therein, all bodhisattvas have attained the stage of non-retrogression.
Within that realm, even the name of "unwholesome" does not exist, nor does the name of "receiving precepts" exist in that buddha-field, nor are there any words of confession for transgressions.
May all sentient beings therein be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man and possess the strength of Nārāyaṇa.
May there not be a single person among them whose sense faculties are incomplete, until they reach bodhi and parinirvāṇa.

May all sentient beings therein be born with the śrīvatsa mark upon their heads and wearing the kāṣāya robes, and may they simultaneously attain the samādhi of skillful discernment, never losing it until they reach the limit of bodhi.
May the sentient beings therein universally accumulate roots of goodness, and may those sentient beings therein be free from old age, sickness, and suffering.

When a bodhisattva there reaches the end of his lifespan, he shall enter parinirvāṇa while sitting in the full lotus posture; fire shall issue from his body to cremate himself, and a fragrant wind shall blow.
His relics shall be placed within other lands where no Buddha currently resides, causing them to become wish-fulfilling jewels, like the bright and pure maṇi-gems of a wheel-turning monarch.
Among those sentient beings, some see the light of that mani-jewel, some see the mani-jewel itself, and others even touch it;
they are all caused not to undergo the sufferings of the hells, hungry ghosts, or animals, and until their final nirvana at enlightenment, they never experience pain, passing away from life therein.
Wherever there are Buddhas currently dwelling in the world, they teach the Dharma to sentient beings so that they may be born in such places.
Having been born there, they hear the sublime Dharma from those Buddhas and resolve their minds upon Bodhicitta;
as soon as they have resolved their minds, they cause them to attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

In my buddha-field, there is not a single person who passes away without having entered samādhi; nor is there any passing away accompanied by pain, longing, or attachment to those left behind. Having passed away therein, they shall not be reborn in difficult places or in lands where no Buddha resides.
Until the very limit of enlightenment, they shall never fail to see the Buddha, never fail to hear the Dharma, and never fail to make offerings to the Saṅgha.
They shall cause all sentient beings therein to be free from defilement and turbidity, anger, attachment and aversion, stinginess and envy, ignorance, and the conceit of selfhood.
In that buddha-field, there shall be no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only bodhisattvas.
Bodhisattvas with moistened minds, supple minds, unresentful minds, unturbid minds, tranquil minds, and concentrated minds shall fill it.

May my Buddha-field be adorned, radiant, and pure, appearing within as many other worlds as there are atoms in the Buddha-fields of the ten directions; may its fragrance also reach everywhere, so that those sentient beings therein are constantly filled with joy.
I shall cause that buddha-field to be such that the sound of suffering is never heard.

"For that long I shall practice the bodhisattva path; while acting as a bodhisattva, I will first establish such a pure and adorned buddha-field and settle within that buddha-land a multitude of beings with pure intentions, and only thereafter shall I attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi therein."

When I attain enlightenment, may my radiance be immeasurable; furthermore, may the marks and signs adorning my body appear everywhere throughout thousands of Buddha-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within other Buddha-lands.

Among those beings, for any who see me, I cause them to eliminate greed, hatred, delusion, stinginess, envy, self-attachment, resentment, and the fetters, so that all are utterly extinguished; and by virtue of seeing me, they shall all attain the arousal of the bodhicitta according to their desires, as well as samādhi, dhāraṇī, and patience.
Should there be sentient beings born in the Cold Ice Hell, upon seeing me they shall receive warm and pleasant sensations and attain such happiness, just as a bhikṣu enters the third dhyāna;

having seen me, their bodies and minds will be filled with supreme bliss, and they shall all resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. There, at the end of their lives, they will come to be born in my land and attain non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If sentient beings are born among the hungry ghosts, upon seeing me, they shall—in brief—be made to become non-retrogressive from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The same is said for animals.
Thus, my light shines doubly upon the various devas, making my lifespan immeasurable such that no one can count it, except for the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).
When I attain enlightenment, may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, praise and extol me throughout the immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya, ineffable, and boundless worlds of the ten directions.

I shall cause those sentient beings therein who hear my name to dedicate the roots of goodness they have cultivated toward my buddha-field; upon the end of their lives, they shall be reborn in my land, with the exception of those who have committed the five crimes of immediate retribution, those who have slandered the true Dharma, or those who have reviled the noble ones.

When I attain enlightenment, in immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* other Buddha-fields, if sentient beings hear my name and seek rebirth in my land, at the time their lives are about to end, I shall appear before them, surrounded by an immeasurable multitude of followers, having entered the *anāvila* (unobscured) samādhi.
Thus, through this well-spoken teaching, he causes those sentient beings’ minds to attain joy and all their suffering to be extinguished;

by means of this joy, they awaken to the samādhi of certainty, causing their minds to attain the bliss of the patience of dharmas (*dharmakṣānti*), and after their lives end, they are reborn in my land.

Furthermore, in other buddha-fields where there is a lack of the seven riches, beings do not delight in seeking the three vehicles, nor do they delight in seeking the blessings of humans and devas, nor do they delight in seeking the three grounds of wholesome merit. Instead, they take pleasure in and are attached to non-Dharma, stinginess, greed, and envy; they delight in associating with sentient beings who follow false teachings. For these beings, when their lives are about to end, [the Buddha] appears before them, surrounded by an immeasurable multitude, and preaches the Dharma for them through the *Anupapatti-samādhi* (the Samādhi of Non-falling).

I shall manifest my own buddha-field to those sentient beings to exhort them toward bodhicitta, causing them to experience joy and rapture upon seeing me, thereby inspiring them to resolve for enlightenment. I shall cause all their sufferings to be extinguished, enable them to attain the Sun-Lamp Samādhi so they may abandon ignorance, and ensure that after their lives end, they are reborn in my land.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"
“Your aspiration is most excellent.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

If my intention is thus fulfilled, may there fall a rain of wondrous *sāgara-tīra-candana* powder throughout as many other Buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are atoms in a Buddha-field; and may all sentient beings who smell this fragrance therein resolve their minds toward Bodhicitta, so that I may now attain the Samādhi of Fulfilling Wishes and personally behold it.

"Good son! As soon as he had made that vow, he attained the Samādhi of Fulfilling Wishes and beheld his own Buddha-land. He saw, throughout worlds in the ten directions as numerous as motes of dust, a rain of the powder of *sāgara-candana* from the other shore falling; and he saw, in each of the ten directions, countless sentient beings joining their palms together and giving rise to the bodhicitta."
The Buddha said: "Good son!
The rain of incense fell very swiftly, exhorting countless sentient beings toward Bodhi."
"Noble son!
For this reason, I shall name you Siṃhagandha.

In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed and at the beginning of the second asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world-system named Vimala-gandhaprabhāsa located above this buddha-field, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in forty-two buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges."
"You, Siṃhagandha!

Therein you shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, even up to Buddha, World-Honored One, named Prabhāsavirajottamagandhacandrasvārājendra."
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:”
“Arising as one revered by humans, asuras, and devas, you shall become a World-Honored One to deliver sentient beings;
having severed the bonds of suffering in the three realms, you shall attain the state of a Wondrous Unsurpassed Being.”
9. Chapter on the Prophecy for the Eighth Prince. *Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, Chapter Nine: "The Prophecy for the Eighth Prince. "Good son!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke briefly to the eighth prince, Amogha:
"World-Honored One!

For that duration of time, within a turbid buddha-field, I shall practice the bodhisattva path for the sake of awakening. First, I shall purify ten thousand turbid buddha-fields and establish them as pure, no different from the stainless buddha-land of King of Blue Fragrance Radiance. Having established such roots of goodness and purified my own mind, I shall cause the great vehicle bodhisattvas who seek it to fill those fields; only then shall I attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening therein."
"O World-Honored One!
I shall practice the bodhisattva conduct in such a way that it cannot be practiced by other bodhisattvas."
“World-Honored One!

During these seven years, I sat in a single place in quietude, contemplating the merits of the pure qualities of the Buddhas and the adornments of the Buddha-fields—the merits of purifying the Buddha-lands. Within that state, I gave rise to and cultivated eighteen thousand bodhisattva samādhis, such as the Samādhi of Manifest Adornment.”
World-Honored One!

It is I who, practicing the bodhisattva path of awakening, by means of the *cintāmaṇicakra* samādhi, constantly see all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling and remaining in the immeasurable and boundless worlds of the ten directions, benefiting sentient beings and preaching the Dharma for them.
Furthermore, transcending the three periods of time, I see those Buddhas filling all lands.
World-Honored One!
With a mind as vast as the atoms of the Samantabhadra-samādhi, I see those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, surrounded by assemblies of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and the great multitude.

By the power of the Samādhi of Non-Reliance, I manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field; with each body, I pay homage to every single Buddha, offering supreme variegated jewel-flowers, supreme variegated incense, ointments, powdered incense, garlands, ornaments, and music. With all these supreme adornments, I make offerings to all Buddhas, practicing in each and every Buddha-field for as long as a Great Ocean Kalpa.
By means of the Samādhi of Cultivating All Bodies, in a single thought-moment I know the conduct of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands.
World-Honored One!
By means of the Samādhi of Merit, I offer supreme and wondrous praise to each and every Buddha, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-land.
"Bhagavān!
By means of the Unblinking Samādhi and a mind equal to a single atom, I see Buddhas filling all Buddha-fields.
Bhagavān!"
By means of the *araṇā-samādhi*, in a single moment of thought, I behold the adornments of all Buddha-fields—past, future, and present—within all Buddha-lands.
World-Honored One!

By means of the *śūraṅgama-samādhi*, I enter into the hells, manifesting my own body to preach the Dharma for them, exhorting them toward Bodhi and causing them to resolve their minds upon it. When they pass away from there, they are reborn as humans and encounter the Buddhas who are currently preaching the Dharma; I cause those sentient beings to hear the Dharma from the Buddhas and attain the stage of non-retrogression.

Likewise among animals, hungry ghosts, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, nāgas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas; and likewise among those in the heavens, such as piśācas, pūtanas, and kaṭapūtanas; and likewise among humans, caṇḍālas, merchants, and courtesans.
"So it is, World-Honored One!
I shall assume forms according to the dwelling places of sentient beings, experiencing suffering or joy in accordance with the karmic causes and conditions of those beings.

If there are various crafts or arts, I shall enter among them to manifest and explain their practices; through skillful speech and expedient means, I shall win the hearts of sentient beings, and thereafter instruct them in the True Dharma, exhorting them toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, so that they may abide in the non-retrogressive state of Unsurpassed Perfect Enlightenment."
“O World-Honored One!

For that duration, I shall practice the bodhisattva path and purify ten thousand buddha-fields. Within them, I shall extinguish such poisons as the karmic actions and fetters of all sentient beings; even in the case of a single sentient being, I shall ensure that the four māras’ paths do not exist.”

I shall thus purify and establish ten thousand buddha-fields, just as the buddha-field of the Tathāgata King of Fragrant Moon Sovereignty, Undefiled Body of Radiant Light, is adorned in the world-system Blue Fragrance Free from Dust.
"I shall purify my own buddha-field and its retinue, just as the bodhisattva mahāsattva Siṃhagandha has vowed.
O World-Honored One!"

If such an intention is fulfilled, may all the sufferings of all sentient beings within ten thousand buddha-fields be extinguished; may they attain a mind of universal gentleness and compliance; and may each of them behold the Buddhas within their own respective four-continent worlds.

May those sentient beings have various kinds of jewels, various flowers, incense, powdered incense, ointments, diverse garments, pavilions, banners, standards, and canopies spontaneously appear in their hands, so that they may use them to make offerings to the Buddhas and resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"By the power of the Samādhi of Manifest Adornment, I shall cause myself to see it.
As soon as he spoke these words, everything was seen exactly as he had wished.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, excellent, son of good family!

Just as you have universally established pure Buddha-lands for yourself and purified ten thousand Buddha-lands all around, and purified the bodies and minds of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings, so too shall immeasurable asaṃkhyeya Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, be honored with such immeasurable asaṃkhyeya offerings.”
"Good son! For this reason, I name you Samantabhadra.

You, Samantabhadra, in a future age, after the passing of one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and a small portion remaining of a second asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there will be in the northern direction, sixty Ganges-sand numbers of Buddha-fields beyond this buddha-field, a world named Jñānodakaviśuddhaguṇa. You, Samantabhadra!"
Therein you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and be known by the name Lion’s Vigorous Display Vajra Wisdom Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and so forth, up to Buddha, World-Honored One.
"Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:"
“Arising with wholesome wisdom, you delight in taming the mind; you have made firm and excellent vows regarding all sentient beings.
To ferry sentient beings across the deep river of the fetters—you who know the wondrous torch, become a Buddha for the sake of the world.”
The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Volume Three;
The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Volume Four.
The name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost; it is now appended to the Qin Records.
Chapter Ten: The Prophecy for the Ten Thousand People "Good son!
At that time, ten thousand indolent people raised their voices together and said:"
“O World-Honored One!

We wish to attain the state of Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha within a pure Buddha-field—that pure realm cultivated by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra while practicing the bodhisattva path. Thus, we shall practice the six pāramitās, fulfill that Buddha-field, and attain perfect enlightenment.”
"Good son! The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha was likewise; he bestowed predictions upon those ten thousand indolent ones, saying:

'When the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra attains unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, you all shall likewise attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment in the world-realm Parivarta.'"
There were one thousand [Buddhas] all named Jñānārci-ghaṇṭeśvarasvara Tathāgata;
furthermore, there were one thousand [Buddhas] all named Saṃgrahaiśvarasiṃhanāda Tathāgata;
and furthermore, there were one thousand [Buddhas] all named Vimalasvara-iśvararāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there were one thousand [Buddhas] all named Fear-Dispelling Sound Sovereign King Tathāgata;
another thousand all named Virtuous Stainless Sound Radiance Sovereign King Tathāgata;
and another five hundred all named Sun-Brightness Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there were five hundred others all named Tathāgata Sūryagarbha-viśeṣarāja;
seven named Tathāgata Nāgajīmūta;
and eight named Tathāgata Abhayaghoṣarājāmalaprabha.
The tenth is named Aruṇasvara Tathāgata;
the eleventh is named Svayambhūnirghoṣadharmasaṃbhavaghoṣa Tathāgata;
the ninth is named Guṇadharmanṛpati Tathāgata.
The twentieth is named Tathāgata Acintyamanirāja;
the third is named Tathāgata Ratnadhvajacandrasvairaprabhamuni-jñānasvairakūṭasūkṣmāsvādharāja-acintyamanijñānagarbha;
and the fifteenth is named Tathāgata Jñānottaradhvaja.
The fifty-first is named Tathāgata King of the Ocean of Wisdom;
the second is named Tathāgata Sovereign King of the Sound of Great Diligence and High Virtue in the Kalpa;
the eightieth is named Tathāgata Swift Wisdom Free from Dust.
The ninety-first is named Tathāgata Sovereign Lineage;
the hundredth is named Tathāgata Wisdom-Virtue-Undefiled-Thunder-Sovereign;
the eightieth is named Tathāgata King of the Ocean of Merit Beyond Food, King of the Accumulated Power of Wisdom.
The forty [Tathāgatas] are: Jina-bodhi-vaśavartin-rāja Tathāgata; Muni-citrotpala Tathāgata; Citra-guṇa-mati Tathāgata;
Vajra-siṃha-śīla-prabhā-ghoṣa Tathāgata; Bhadra-agrya Tathāgata; Amitābha Tathāgata; Siṃha-nandi Tathāgata; Akṣaya-jñāna-cita-ratna-prabha Tathāgata; Jñāna-vimala Tathāgata;
Jñāna-vidruma Tathāgata; Siṃha-kīrti Tathāgata; Abhigata-guṇa-rāja Tathāgata; Dharmapadma-varṣa Tathāgata; and Prabhāsa... [Tathāgata].
The Tathāgata Valgusvara, the Tathāgata Dharmotplava-rājāmalaka, the Tathāgata Gandheśvara,
the Tathāgata Vimalanetra, the Tathāgata Mahācaya, the Tathāgata Asaṃkhyeya-balendra, the Tathāgata Svajñāna-puṇyabala,
the Tathāgata Jñānavastra, the Tathāgata Īśvara, and the Tathāgata Asaṃkhyeyaspharaṇa.
...the Tathāgata Āyus, the Tathāgata Jñānakośa, the Tathāgata Mahocchraya, the Tathāgata Balagarbha, the Tathāgata Guṇanidhi,
the Tathāgata Śākhāpuṣpadhvaja, the Tathāgata Saṃbhavaprabha, the Tathāgata Amohaguṇarāja,
the Tathāgata Vajrottama, the Tathāgata Dharmottara, the Tathāgata Ghoṣeśvararāja, and the Tathāgata Svayaṃ...
Vajradhara-ratnadhara Tathāgata, Svairavikrāntadhvaja-kalpasaṃsthita Tathāgata,
Dharmaprayoga-brahmarāja Tathāgata, Samantaguṇasāgararāja Tathāgata, Jñānakūṭa Tathāgata, Jñānārcispuṣpa Tathāgata,
Sarvalokendrādhipati Tathāgata, Udumbarapuṣpa-suvarṇadhvaja Tathāgata.
...the Tathāgata Āgata-dharmadhvaja-rāja, the Tathāgata Candana-sukha-sthita-raja-vikrama,
the Tathāgata Dhvaja-agra-pradīpa, the Tathāgata Jñāna-udaya-raja-vikrama, the Tathāgata Dṛḍha-dhvaja-nirghāta,
the Tathāgata Dharma-kīrti, the Tathāgata Māra-jit-guṇa-jvāla, and the Tathāgata Jñānapāraśāsana.
Tathāgata Jñānapradīpa, Tathāgata Kṣema-rāja, Tathāgata Jñānasvara,
Tathāgata Dhvajasaṃcaya, Tathāgata Vajra, Tathāgata Vajraprabha, Tathāgata Vyūharāja, Tathāgata Jayasena,
Tathāgata Sukhacitta, Tathāgata Candrarāja, and Tathāgata Vikrāntaghoṣarāja.
The Tathāgata Brahmarāja; the Tathāgata Aśīti-siṃhagati;
the Tathāgata Pañcāśat-nārāyaṇavijayagarbha.
Seventy Tathāgatas named Ratnaskandha;
thirty Tathāgatas named Candragarbha;
and twenty Tathāgatas named Jyotiṣprabha.
The Tathāgata Triṃśadguṇabalabrahmarāja;
the ninety Tathāgatas Mṛdusvara and Brahmottaradṛḍha;
and furthermore, the ten named Tathāgatas Gandhapuṣpavijayakīrtirāja.
The Tathāgata King Illumined by the Full Moon of Seventy Radiant Lights;
the Tathāgatas Supreme Fragrant Flower, Ocean of Immeasurable Virtues, Supreme Wisdom, and Jambū Shadow;
and the one hundred and two Tathāgatas Mountain Banner of Virtue and Lion Most Excellent.
One hundred and one Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas named Śataika-nāga-nirghoṣa-prabhāsa-rāja, Sugandha-gotra-niḥsattva, and Amitaguṇaprabhāsa-rāja-kalpa;
and furthermore, there were a thousand others all sharing the name Dharmajñāna-nāgarāja-vimukti-bodhaloka-samudra-netrasthita.
Each of you shall, on the same day, simultaneously attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in different lands, and your lifespan shall be ten minor kalpas.
You shall also enter unsurpassed Nirvana on that same day; thereafter, the True Dharma in all those Buddha-lands shall perish after seven days.
Those ten thousand people prostrated themselves with their five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
"Arise, you who possess the wondrous and firm roar of a dragon! You should seek to cultivate and accumulate the most excellent wealth of merit."
"Diligently cultivate the six perfections without indolence; you shall become a guide for gods and humans.
Chapter Eleven: The Prediction for the Ninth Prince From the *Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra* "O son of good family!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke briefly to the ninth prince, Amogha.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:

"I shall practice the bodhisattva conduct in this manner, so that the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, may bear witness to my practice of the bodhisattva path to enlightenment."
"O World-Honored One!

Just as I now resolve upon bodhicitta before the Buddha, until I attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may I practice the conduct of enlightenment during that interval without regretting my mind; until the very limit of enlightenment, may my vows remain firm, and may I practice according to what I have spoken without disturbing the minds of others."
May I not give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha;
may my mind not give rise to sensual desire, nor dwell together with sleep, arrogance, derision, deception, affliction, or doubt;
may it not dwell together with killing, stealing, unchaste conduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, frivolous speech, ignorance, restlessness, wrong views, envy, and so forth.
May there be no lack of a mind that reveres the Dharma, nor any mind of detachment.
When I practice the bodhisattva path until the very limit of enlightenment, may my mind never harbor such states as these.

May I, until the very limit of enlightenment, maintain a mind that constantly recollects the Buddha with every step I raise and every step I set; and until the very limit of enlightenment, may I never fail to see the Buddha, never fail to hear the Dharma, and never fail to make offerings to the Sangha.

May I always attain renunciation in whatever place I am born; may I always wear rag-robes and maintain only the three robes; may I dwell under trees and always sit in secluded places; may I always beg for food, having few desires and being content; may I always preach the Dharma with words free from attachment;

may I be endowed with immeasurable eloquence; may I never commit a root offense; may I not mix my speech with falsehood or disparage the doctrines of others; may I always contemplate emptiness when preaching the Dharma to women, and may I constantly reflect upon emptiness.
One should not laugh with bared teeth in front of women, nor should one preach the Dharma to others while moving the hands in a flirtatious manner.
I always maintain a mind of service and offering toward Mahāyāna bodhisattvas as if they were my teachers.

If I hear the Dharma from another, I shall regard them with the same reverence as a teacher; I shall always show respect to śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, honoring and making offerings to them solely as I do before the Tathāgata.

I do not practice giving by deliberating over what should or should not be given; I harbor no mind of envy regarding the gift of Dharma; I save those who are destined for death with my own life and body; and through my own diligence, I provide various necessities to rescue sentient beings from their distress.
I do not speak of the relative merits or demerits of being a householder or one who has left the home life;
rather, I constantly observe that gain, support, praise, and reputation are like fire, like poison, and like an enemy, and my mind always keeps them at a distance.
"Bhagavān!

If, until the very limit of my attainment of bodhi, I shall fulfill the vow I have made here before the Bhagavān, may there spontaneously appear in both my hands a wheel-treasure (cakraratna), complete with a thousand spokes, a rim, and a hub, and radiant with blazing flames."
As soon as Prince Amitaku had finished speaking these words, the wheel appeared in his hand according to his wish.
He then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If my intention is thus fulfilled until the very limit of enlightenment, may this precious wheel-jewel travel to the empty buddha-fields of the five corruptions and utter this great sound, like the roar of the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda.
In all buddha-fields, a voice proclaimed these words:
"The Bodhisattva has received the prediction of enlightenment in the wisdom of non-deluded mindfulness.
It further proclaimed: "He cultivates the Dharma-treasury of the immovable mental realm through emptiness."
For all sentient beings who are born therein, the sound of this Dharma-treasury enters their faculty of hearing;
as soon as it enters the ear, it causes their craving for desire to be extinguished, and their anger, ignorance, self-attachment, stinginess, and envy are all extinguished;
it enables them to contemplate the wisdom of the Buddha’s realm and to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

"Good son! Prince Amitauja dispatched those two wheels, which were exceedingly swift—just like the supernatural powers of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas—and thus traveled to the immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) five-turbid, empty Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions."
Upon arrival, he proclaimed for the sake of sentient beings:
"The Bodhisattva has received the prediction of enlightenment through the wisdom of non-delusive mindfulness; he cultivates the Dharma-treasury of the immovable mental realm of emptiness.
Once this sound of the Dharma-treasury entered the faculty of hearing of all those sentient beings, all their sensual desires, up to and including the jealousy of mind and thought, were extinguished.
They all contemplated with a wisdom equal to the realm of a Buddha and resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
in an instant, that wheel returned and stood before the prince.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised Prince Amitakusuma, saying:
‘Excellent, excellent!’”
"Good son!

Your vow to practice the bodhisattva path is most excellent. Send this natural wheel-treasure to that five-defilement void buddha-field, so that many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings may abide in a mind free from defilement and a mind free from affliction, and be exhorted toward bodhi."
"Good son! For this reason, I name you 'The Untroubled.
You, O Untroubled!"
"You shall become a guide for the world; you may take up the adornment of a buddha-field according to your own desire.
Amitābha addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One!..."
I seek such an adornment of a buddha-field as this: namely, that the entire ground be made of gold, level as the palm of a hand, and filled everywhere with various celestial jewels.

May there be no shards, rubble, earth, stones, or mountains; may the ground be soft to the touch like *kārpāsa* cotton, sinking when the foot is placed upon it and returning to its original state when the foot is lifted.
Within it, may even the names of the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts not exist.
In my buddha-field there are no foul odors or impurities; it is filled with the exquisite, superior fragrance of the devas, and celestial *mandārava* flowers cover the entire buddha-field.
The sentient beings therein shall be free from old age and illness; they shall have nothing to fear and shall not be subject to affliction or disturbance.
May the sentient beings therein not suffer untimely death; may they die without regret; and may there be none who passes away without having entered samādhi.

May the sentient beings therein pass away while contemplating the Buddha; having passed away, may they not fall into the evil realms, nor be born in the five turbidities or in empty buddha-fields. Until they attain bodhi and parinirvāṇa, may they never fail to see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, or make offerings to the Saṅgha.
May the sentient beings therein have little lust, anger, and delusion;
may all sentient beings therein cultivate the ten wholesome courses of action;
and may the sentient beings in that buddha-field have no such things as receiving precepts or the names of transgressions and repentance.
May the sentient beings therein not be given any opportunity by Māra;
may the sentient beings therein be free from all ugliness;
and may the sentient beings therein have no discrimination between the noble and the lowly.
May the sentient beings therein be free from the notion of "mine" and free from purposeful striving;
may the śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and even those in their dreams there never experience the emission of impurity;
and may all sentient beings therein love the Dharma and seek the Dharma.
May there not be a single person in that buddha-field who follows heterodox teachings or holds inverted views;
may the bodies of the sentient beings therein be free from weariness and their minds free from fatigue;
and may all sentient beings therein attain the five supernormal powers.

May the sentient beings therein be free from the affliction of hunger and thirst, with precious vessels filled with whatever food they desire appearing before them as among the gods of the Desire Realm;
may the sentient beings therein have no excrement or urine, nor mucus, saliva, tears, or perspiration.
May there be neither cold nor heat therein;

may soft-scented breezes blow to move the hearts of humans and devas, so that according to their desires—whether they seek cool winds, warm winds, the fragrance of *utpala* flowers, the fragrance of *tagara*, the fragrance of *sāgara-pāra*, the fragrance of *tagara*, the fragrance of aloeswood (*agaru*), or the fragrance of all perfumes—they shall obtain them all exactly as they think upon them in their minds.
May there be no such world of five corruptions (*pañca-kaṣāya*) therein.

He causes there to be towers made of the seven treasures within his kingdom; within those towers are thrones made of the seven treasures, upon which cushions and mats are layered and crimson pillows are placed, so soft to the touch as to be like *karpāsa* silk. Wherever people dwell, he causes those treasure towers to be surrounded by ponds filled with water possessing the eight virtues, which those sentient beings use for their needs.

He causes the rows of trees therein to be adorned with *sumana* flowers, and adorns those trees with various kinds of blossoms, various fruits, various fragrances, various garments, various canopies, various necklaces, and various ornaments.
The sentient beings therein take whatever clothing they desire from the wish-fulfilling trees and wear it; likewise, they take and enjoy whatever flowers or even ornaments they wish for.

I shall cause my Bodhi tree to be composed of the seven treasures, reaching a height of one thousand yojanas, with a trunk one yojana in diameter and branches and leaves extending for one thousand yojanas. When a gentle breeze blows and the branches and leaves brush against one another, they shall produce a supple and exquisite sound surpassing that of the heavens—namely, the sounds of the perfections, the supernormal powers, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path. Those who hear it will attain a mind free from desire.

May the women in that buddha-field be endowed with all virtues, just like the goddesses of Tuṣita Heaven; furthermore, may the women therein be free from all foul odors and impurities, and refrain from double-tongued speech, stinginess, jealousy, and envy.

It causes those men not to engage in physical contact or sexual desire with women; even if they give rise to a lustful mind and go to look at a woman, in an instant that lustful mind is extinguished. They depart feeling great shame and remorse, attaining the *vimala-rajas* (pure and dustless) samādhi. By means of this samādhi, they are forever separated from the realm of Māra and will never again give rise to a lustful mind.
Once that woman has gazed upon the man with a mind of desire, she immediately becomes pregnant; as soon as she has looked, both her gaze and her desire perish.
Thus, while dwelling in the womb, the bodies and minds of the male and female experience bliss, just like the joy and delight of the Trāyastriṃśa devas.

May the men and women in that buddha-field experience such bliss while dwelling in the womb for seven days and seven nights; may pregnant women also experience this bliss, just as a bhikṣu enters the second dhyāna.
The one dwelling in the womb there shall not be defiled by the impurities of the womb; at dawn on the seventh day, they shall be born with extreme fragrance and great joy.

They shall cause that woman to experience no pain and enter a bathing pool together. They shall cause that woman’s mind to immediately become free from desire and attain the pure, stainless *samādhi*. By means of this *samādhi*, they shall cause her to remain forever free from the works of Māra and constantly enter into *samādhi*.

Regarding the karmic causes and conditions of actions performed in previous lives that would have required her to receive a female body for many billions of *kalpas*, they shall cause her, through this *samādhi*, to completely eliminate all female bodies, so that until she reaches *bodhi* and *parinirvāṇa*, she shall never again receive such a body.

Furthermore, there may be sentient beings whose karmic actions would cause them to undergo the suffering of gestation for many eons; when I attain Bodhi, those who hear my name and feel joy in their hearts shall, at the end of their lives, come to my land. For all such beings who were once subject to gestation, every one of their karmic actions shall be completely extinguished, and until the limit of Bodhi, they shall never again undergo birth from a womb.

For those sentient beings whose roots of goodness have matured, they cause them to be born by transformation within those flowers; for those with little merit who have not yet planted roots of goodness, they cause them to be born from a womb until all their karmic actions are exhausted.
In my buddha-field, whether it be women or those entering the womb, may those sentient beings experience a state of constant and pervasive bliss.

May gentle breezes blow through the *sumanā*, *tārā*, and *pāṭalī* trees, producing sounds of such joy and delight, as well as sounds of suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self. By means of these sounds, may the people therein attain the Samādhi of Blazing Light; by means of this samādhi, may those sentient beings awaken to the profound emptiness of clarity, and may that buddha-field never produce sounds of sensual desire.
“‘World-Honored One!
May I, while sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a mere moment.
Having attained Bodhi, may that Buddha-field be without the light of the sun and moon, nor shall there be night; let it be known only by the closing of flowers.’”

I shall emit such radiance that it pervades the trichiliocosm, reaching everywhere without exception; by means of this light, I shall cause those sentient beings to obtain such great illumination as to see the present Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in worlds throughout the ten directions, numbering immeasurable asaṃkhyeyas.

When I attain enlightenment, I shall preach the Dharma with such a voice that it pervades the trichiliocosm, causing all sentient beings therein to conceive a mind of mindfulness of the Buddha. Wherever they may dwell—whether walking, sitting, lying down, or turning about—may they all constantly behold me; and as soon as they contemplate me regarding any dharma concerning which they have doubts, may all their uncertainties be completely eliminated.

When I attain enlightenment, may all sentient beings in the immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields of the ten directions—whether they seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the Great Vehicle—who hear the Dharma from me, be enabled to attain profound samādhi, kṣānti, and dhāraṇī, and thereby abide in non-retrogression regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
May my assembly of śrāvaka disciples be immeasurable, such that none can count them except the Tathāgata.

When I attain bodhi, wherever I travel and set foot, may there arise thousand-petaled golden lotuses. May I dispatch those flowers to empty buddha-fields; once they have arrived, may they praise me, and may all sentient beings who hear my name immediately give rise to joy and happiness.
May all the roots of goodness possessed by those sentient beings be entirely dedicated toward seeking rebirth in my land, so that upon the end of their lives there, they may all come to be born here.
May my assembly of śrāvakas be free from the defilements of ascetics and free from flattery and crookedness, and may all sentient beings likewise become thus.

May my retinue hold the Dharma in high esteem, neither craving material wealth nor valuing honor and profit; may they delight in impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, and diligently cultivate vigor while revering the Buddha, rejoicing in the Dharma, and honoring the Saṃgha of bhikṣus.

He causes the non-retrogressive bodhisattvas therein to attain entry into the mind of emptiness, so that wherever they are born, they constantly preach the *prajñāpāramitā*, never forgetting it until they reach the limit of enlightenment.
"When I attain bodhi, may I remain in the world for ten thousand great kalpas, and after my parinirvāṇa, may the True Dharma remain in the world for a thousand kalpas.
The Buddha said,
"Excellent, excellent!"
A husband takes a pure buddha-field.

You, Akṣobhya, in a future age after one asaṃkhyeya of kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and at the beginning of the second asaṃkhyeya of kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world named Abhirati to the east, a thousand buddha-fields away from here, its adornments accomplished exactly according to your vow.
"You shall therein attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and shall be named the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, even unto Buddha, World-Honored One.
Akṣobhya addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

If my intention is thus fulfilled, may all beings throughout all worlds—those who have formed the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, and those who are reckoned among the class of sentient beings—all attain a mind of loving-kindness, free from enmity and free from turbidity.

He causes their bodies and minds to experience bliss; just as a Bodhisattva dwelling on the tenth stage enters the Lotus Samādhi, relinquishes the body, and attains purity, so too does he cause all sentient beings to experience bliss in body and mind.
"Just as when I prostrate my five limbs at the feet of the World-Honored One, may all the earth become golden. "Good son!

When that Bodhisattva Akṣobhya prostrated his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, immediately all sentient beings experienced such bliss as they had wished for, and all that earth became golden."
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
“Arise with a mind of wondrous intent and freedom from affliction; The most wondrous jewel-wheel is now in your hand.
May many billions of sentient beings attain a heart of compassion; You shall purify your mind and become a World-Honored One.”
Chapter Twelve: The Prediction for the Princes. *The Great Vehicle Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. Chapter Twelve: The Prediction for the Princes. “Good sons!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke briefly to the tenth prince, Nimi.
Prince Nimi’s aspiration was also like that of Akṣobhya.
"O World-Honored One!
If my wish is thus fulfilled, may all sentient beings attain the mind of mindfulness of the Buddha; "
"May there be in the hands of each of them sandalwood incense from this side of the ocean;
may they all use this sublime fragrance to make offerings to the Buddha-image.
The Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent!
Son of good family,
your aspiration is most sublime."

"You can cause all sentient beings to have in their hands the wondrous fragrance of *candanamukta* sandalwood from this shore of the ocean, thereby inspiring in them the mind that recollects the Buddha.
Good son! For this reason, I name you 'Fragrant Hand' (*Gandhahasta*)."
"You, Gandhahastin!

In a future age, after the passing of one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and at the conclusion of the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya and the extinction of his True Dharma—seven days thereafter, you, Gandhahastin!"
In that world, he shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and even Buddha, World-Honored One, named Suvarṇapuṣpa.
Gandhahastin said to the Buddha,
“World-Honored One!
If my wish is thus fulfilled, then as I prostrate my five limbs at the feet of the World-Honored One, may this garden be filled everywhere with a rain of campaka flowers.”

"Good son! At that time, when the Bodhisattva Gandhahasta prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, there immediately fell a rain of campaka flowers throughout the garden."
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
"Arise with a mind of supreme wondrous virtue and fine fragrance; Let a rain of campaka flowers fall throughout the garden.
You should manifest the pure and wondrous path To deliver many sentient beings to the shore of fearlessness."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta spoke to the eleventh prince, named Siṃha, briefly saying:
‘Just as the vow of the Bodhisattva Gandhahasta was, so it shall be for the Jewel Banner atop the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.’”
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
“Excellent, excellent, noble son!”
Therefore, I name you Ratnottama (Jewel-Victorious).

In a future age, after the passing of one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges and the remainder of a second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Suvarṇapuṣpa and the extinction of his True Dharma (*saddharma*), at the end of three *kalpas*, the world Sukhāvatī shall be named Surasvatī. There, you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and your title shall be Īśvara-nāga-meghasvara Tathāgata, up to Buddha and World-Honored One. The adornments of your land shall be no different from those of the land of Akṣobhya Buddha.
Ratnavijaya addressed the Buddha, saying:

If my intention is thus fulfilled, then when I prostrate at the Buddha’s feet, may all sentient beings attain such a mind as that of a Bodhisattva dwelling in the Samādhi of Equal Compassion—one who seeks Bodhi for the benefit of all sentient beings and causes them not to regress."

"Good son! When the Bodhisattva Ratnavijaya prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, all sentient beings attained such a thought as this: that all sentient beings have come to abide in a heart of compassion."
"Good son!
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnavijaya, saying:
'Arise, O Great Being of courageous and virtuous mind, Who can, for the sake of sentient beings, establish a firm vow;'"
"Establishing many beings in a dust-free mind, you shall become Buddhas among gods and humans.
[Thus it was said. In brief, the five hundred princes, Maśapī and the others, made such vows:

"Regarding the taking up of the adornment of Buddha-fields, as the Bodhisattva *Gaganamudrā* has made his vow to take up a pure Buddha-field," the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed upon them all the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, saying:
"At the same time, each of you shall realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in different worlds."
Furthermore, there were four hundred princes who made this vow:
"We shall take up the adornment of a buddha-field, just as the Bodhisattva Diamond-Wisdom-Illumination does."
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha likewise bestowed upon them all the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, each for a different world-system.
Furthermore, there were eighty-nine prince-sons who made this vow:
"We shall take up the adornment of Buddha-fields just as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra does."
Furthermore, those eighty-four thousand minor kings all established pure vows, each seeking to take hold of an adorned and pure buddha-field.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed upon them all the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, such that they would all attain enlightenment together in various distinct worlds.

When these ninety-two billion sentient beings had each established their vows and cultivated their respective pure lands, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed upon them all the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, saying:
"At the same time, you shall each attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in different worlds."
13. Chapter Thirteen: The Prophecy for the Eighty Sons. *The Great Vehicle Sutra of the Compassionate White Lotus*. “O sons of good family!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta had eighty sons, all of whom were younger brothers of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha; the eldest was named Sāgaravikrāntagāmin Kumārabhūta.
"Good son!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta said to Sāgaravaradharaprabha:
'Now, you, O youth, may take up a pure and adorned buddha-field.'"
Sāgaradatta said, "Great Master,
you should first let out a lion's roar.
The Great Master replied:
"I shall speak of my thoughts and aspirations later. He then asked:
"Shall I take up a pure land, or an impure one?"
The Great Master replied:
"Those Bodhisattvas who possess great compassion take up impure lands in order to deliver sentient beings whose minds are turbid and whose views are inverted.
You, O youth!"
"You may know this for yourself.
"Good son! At that time, the youth Sāgaramati went before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Buddha, saying:"
“World-Honored One!
I seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and I shall likewise realize this wondrous bodhi among human beings with a lifespan of eighty thousand years, just as the World-Honored One does now.”

I vow that sentient beings may have little fear of greed, anger, ignorance, and the like; that they may regard the body as a source of affliction within birth and death; and that they may obtain ordination within my teaching, while I, for my part, shall preach the Dharma to the assembly by means of the three vehicles.
World-Honored One!
If my intention may be thus fulfilled, I pray that the World-Honored One will grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha Ratnagarbha said:

"In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed and you have entered the second asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, during the Kalpa of Scattered Flowers, this four-continent world-system within this buddha-field shall be named Wondrously Victorious (Miaosheng). Among human beings with a lifespan of eighty thousand years, you shall attain bodhi and be known as the Tathāgata Ratnākara, even unto Buddha, the World-Honored One."
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If my wish is thus fulfilled, may red pearls rain down throughout this garden, and may the sounds of the five kinds of music emerge from every tree."

“Good son! When the youth Samudra-vaśin prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, red pearls rained down throughout the garden, and the sounds of the five kinds of music issued from every tree.”
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
“Arise, you of great power and inexhaustible wisdom! With a compassionate heart, you who pity the multitude, O Sage;
May your aspirations be fulfilled to purify sentient beings, And for the sake of all living creatures, may you attain Buddhahood in this world.”
"The second son of the brahmin was named Siddhārtha; he spoke thus:
'Just as Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña has established his vow, so shall I also.'"
Thus it was briefly said.
The Buddha Ratnagarbha spoke:

...Candrasūrya Tathāgata, Nāgadanta Tathāgata, Vajraprabha Tathāgata,
Rājapraśasta Tathāgata, Nityaprabha Tathāgata, Jyotirvara Tathāgata, Sannibha Tathāgata,
Jñānasiddha Tathāgata, Gandheśvara Tathāgata, Brahmanātha Tathāgata, and Nārāyaṇagarbha Tathāgata.
...Candragarbha Tathāgata. "Good son!
The youngest son of that Great Teacher was named Abhayamkara. He addressed the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, saying:"
“The World-Honored One has bestowed this prediction upon these seventy-nine youths that they shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi during the Flower-Scattering Kalpa.
World-Honored One!”
"I shall resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* throughout the entire Flower-Scattering Kalpa.
World-Honored One!
May I be the very last to realize wondrous enlightenment, with a lifespan equal to that of those seventy-nine Buddhas."
"When I attain Bodhi, may I grant [the prediction] to those who are equal to them alone; just as they have delivered beings, may I likewise deliver them equally.
As they transform others through the three vehicles, I too shall preach the Dharma of the three vehicles."
Just as the number of śrāvaka monks they possess, when I attain Buddhahood, my śrāvakas shall be equal to theirs.

Just as all sentient beings who have attained human form during the seventy-nine buddhas appearing in the Saṃpuṣpita-kalpa reach the end of half a kalpa, at that time I shall realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), and I shall cause all those sentient beings to abide in the three vehicles (triyāna).
“World-Honored One!
If my intention is thus fulfilled, may the Buddha grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. “Good son!”
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised Abhayānanda, saying:
"Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!"

"You are able to bring great compassion and benefit to countless sentient beings. In a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as vast as the sands of the Ganges has passed and you have entered the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as vast as the sands of the Ganges, at the time when half of the *Puṣpāvatī* (Flower-Sprinkling) kalpa has ended, you shall finally attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. You shall be named Anuttaravīrarāja Tathāgata, up to Buddha, World-Honored One.
Just as those seventy-nine Buddhas shared a lifespan of half a kalpa, you alone shall have a lifespan of half a kalpa; furthermore, everything shall be fulfilled exactly as you have vowed."
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If my wish is to be fulfilled, then when I prostrate with my five limbs at the feet of the World-Honored One, may blue lotuses of exquisite and most wondrous fragrance rain down everywhere throughout this buddha-field. And may all sentient beings who smell this fragrance have their four elements harmonized and all their ailments cured.”

“Good son! Just as when the youth Abhaya prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, at that very moment blue lotuses rained down upon all Buddha-lands; sentient beings who smelled their fragrance had the four elements of their bodies harmonized and all their various ailments were healed.”
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
“Arise and practice great compassion to well-tame the mind; Many wondrous World-Honored Ones will all revere you.
