If you can sever the fetters of flattery and the fetters of stinginess, You shall attain the treasury of pure and wondrous wisdom.”
Chapter Fourteen: The Prophecy for the Three Hundred Million Young Boys. *The Great Vehicle Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. "O sons of good family!

At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta had three hundred million disciples who said to him as he sat at the gate of the garden, "Someone has come to us; let us take the Three Refuges and exhort them toward Bodhi."
"Good son!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta said to his disciples:
'You youths, you should resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; each of you should take a buddha-field according to your own desire and make vows as you wish before the Tathāgata.'"
Among his disciples, there was a youth named Candrakṣānti who addressed his teacher, saying: "What is this path?
By accumulating what merit, practicing what conduct, and forming what thoughts shall one attain bodhi?"
The Great Teacher said:
"O youth! A bodhisattva who possesses the treasury of the four immeasurables attains awakening."
What are these four? They are:

possessing the inexhaustible treasury of merit, possessing the inexhaustible treasury of knowledge, possessing the inexhaustible treasury of wisdom, and possessing the inexhaustible treasury of all Buddha-dharmas; these are called the four inexhaustible treasuries.
"Good son!
The Tathāgata has taught this path to bodhi, called 'The Dharma Gate of the Universal Collection of Pure Virtues for Crossing Over Birth and Death.
The Bodhisattva fully practices giving for the sake of delivering sentient beings."
The Bodhisattva fulfills the precepts in order to satisfy his vows;
the Bodhisattva fulfills patience in order to perfect the primary and secondary marks;
the Bodhisattva fulfills diligence in order to accomplish all tasks.
The Bodhisattva is fully endowed with dhyāna for the sake of disciplining the mind;
the Bodhisattva is fully endowed with wisdom for the sake of extinguishing all fetters;
the Bodhisattva is fully endowed with learning for the sake of incalculable eloquence.
The Bodhisattva is endowed with merit, for the purpose of benefiting all sentient beings;
the Bodhisattva is endowed with wisdom, for the sake of incalculable knowledge (*asaṃkhyeya-jñāna*);
the Bodhisattva is endowed with tranquility (*śamatha*), for the purpose of acting according to the mind.
The Bodhisattva is fully endowed with contemplation in order to eliminate doubt and confusion;
the Bodhisattva is fully endowed with loving-kindness in order that the mind may be without obstruction;
the Bodhisattva is fully endowed with compassion in order to deliver beings without weariness.
The bodhisattva is fully endowed with joy, for the sake of delighting in the joy of the Dharma;
the bodhisattva is fully endowed with equanimity, for the sake of eliminating love and hatred;
the bodhisattva is fully endowed with the *maśramaṇa*, for the sake of removing obstacles.
The Bodhisattva fulfills renunciation in order to abandon all conditioned phenomena;
the Bodhisattva fulfills seclusion in order to extinguish unwholesome karma and cultivate beneficial wholesome karma;
the Bodhisattva fulfills mindfulness in order to attain retention.
The Bodhisattva is endowed with mental faculty for the sake of awakening to profound understanding;
the Bodhisattva is endowed with firm resolve for the sake of awakening to the meaning;
the Bodhisattva is endowed with the foundations of mindfulness for the sake of contemplating the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena.
The bodhisattva is fully endowed with right equanimity (*samyak-upekṣā*) for the sake of abandoning all unwholesome dharmas and cultivating the fulfillment of all wholesome dharmas;
the bodhisattva is fully endowed with supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) for the sake of lightening the body and mind;
the bodhisattva is fully endowed with the faculties (*indriya*) for the sake of fulfilling the gathering of the faculties.
The Bodhisattva is endowed with powers in order to subdue all fetters;
the Bodhisattva is endowed with the factors of enlightenment in order to awaken to the true Dharma;
the Bodhisattva is endowed with the six dharmas of harmonious respect in order to purify the minds of those ready for deliverance.
"O youth!
This is called the Dharma-gate of the complete and pure transcendence of birth and death.
The youth addressed his teacher, saying:
"I have heard the World-Honored One say:
'Through giving, one attains great wealth and benefits one's kinsmen;
through observing the precepts, one is reborn in heaven.'"
"Through extensive learning one attains great wisdom;
the World-Honored One taught the cultivation of purity for the sake of crossing over birth and death.
The Great Teacher replied:
"Young man, it is as you have said:
there are those who give while delighting in birth and death.
Young man!"
Good son! Good daughter!
One who has faith and practices the giving of the path to enlightenment does so for the sake of taming the mind.
One observes the precepts for the sake of extinguishing the mind;
one seeks learning for the sake of removing mental turbidity;
and one cultivates compassion for the sake of the mind of great compassion.
Other dharmas are fully accumulated and practiced through wisdom and skillful means. O youth!
This is the path to bodhi; by fully accumulating such virtues, such cultivation, and such mindfulness, one attains bodhi.
O youths! Such is the practice of the path to enlightenment. O youths!
One may seek bodhi. Young men!
The path to bodhi is pure; you should establish your vows with a focused mind, and they shall surely be fulfilled.
O youths! The path to awakening is pure because the mind is pure. O youths!
The path to awakening is straight, for it purifies all fetters by being free from flattery and hypocrisy. O youths!
The path to awakening extends even unto the limit of peaceful, unsurpassed nirvāṇa.
"Therefore, you all should now make vows to take up whichever Buddha-lands you choose, whether they be adorned and pure or not.
"Good son! At that time, the youth Candrakṣānti went before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:"

“World-Honored One! I now wish to resolve my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Among the sentient beings in this defiled Buddha-field, there are few who have little greed, anger, or delusion; who are without forgetfulness, without turbid minds, without hearts of enmity, and without hearts of stinginess or jealousy; who dwell with hearts free from false views and established in right view; who are without unwholesome minds and constantly seek wholesome minds; who are without the minds of the three evil destinies and seek the human or heavenly realms; who gather the roots of goodness of the three fields of merit; and who seek the minds of the three vehicles—I shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* therein.”
“World-Honored One!
If my wish is to be fulfilled, may there appear naturally in my two hands a dragon-elephant.
As soon as these words were spoken, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, a naturally appearing dragon-elephant emerged from his two hands; its body was pure white and its seven limbs were complete.
He personally witnessed this with his own eyes and declared to them:

"You two dragon-elephants, ascend into the void and traverse throughout this land, bringing down an exceedingly fragrant and wondrous rain of eight meritorious qualities to awaken all sentient beings in this Buddha-land;

let the drops of this rain touch the bodies of these beings, and for those who smell the fragrance, cause them to eliminate the five hindrances—namely, sensual desire, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt."
As soon as these words were spoken, those two nāga-elephants immediately ascended into the air with such great speed that they were as swift as a powerful athlete releasing an arrow.
Having completed the task as previously described, the two nāga-elephants returned and stood before him.
“Good son! At that time, the youth Candrakṣānti was filled with supreme joy.
Then, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha addressed him, saying:”
“O son of good family!

In a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed and you have entered the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa, during the Illuminating Eon (*Ālokakara*) in the Buddha-field of Radiant Assembly (*Prabhāsa-saṃcaya*), in this world-system of four continents, you shall attain Buddhahood, named Ratnacchatravikrāntaprabha Tathāgata, up to: Buddha, World-Honored One.”
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Candrakṣānti prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
Ratnagarbha said:”
“Arise! Your dust-free mind is most pure; you have bestowed predictions upon many billions of sentient beings.
Having purified the most wondrous path to bodhi, you shall become a seer and guide sentient beings.”
“Briefly stated, less than a thousand people remained;
three hundred million youths in this buddha-field established the vow for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed the prediction of enlightenment upon them all.”
The last of these were named Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Śikhin Tathāgata, and Viśvabhū Tathāgata;
it was they who conferred the prediction of enlightenment upon the youth.

Chapter Fifteen: The Prophecy for the Thousand Boy Disciples from the Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra. "These thousand boy disciples were all masters of the four Vedas; they served him who was their greatest teacher, named Piyu Viśeṣṭhin."
He said: "I wish to realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in that buddha-field of the five corruptions;
I shall preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings who are afflicted by extremely heavy greed, hatred, delusion, and all the fetters."
The youth Candracūḍa addressed the Great Master, saying:
"What did this Piyu-viśeṣa see that he was able to establish his vow in a Buddha-field of the five turbidities?"
The Great Teacher said:
"Young man!

There is a Bodhisattva of Great Compassion who attains enlightenment in a Buddha-field of the five turbidities. For the sake of those sentient beings who are without protection or refuge, who are distressed by the calamities of the fetters and false views, he acts as their protector and guide for their benefit. He delivers such beings from the ocean of birth and death, establishing them in right view, and fills sentient beings with the flavor of the nectar of Nirvana; this is the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion manifesting his vow to establish himself in a Buddha-field of the five turbidities."
Then the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:

"You, Piyadasi-ṇī, in a future age after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa and the remainder of a second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa—as many as the sands of the Ganges have passed—there will be a world named Saṃyojana-dhvaja, located to the east beyond as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a Buddha-field."
"O virtuous man!
Among them, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and your name shall be Tathāgata Śailendrarāja, even unto Buddha, the World-Honored One."
Pīyavisiṇu addressed the Buddha, saying:
"When I prostrate at the feet of the World-Honored One, I pray that the World-Honored One will, with his two hands adorned by a hundred blessings, stroke the crown of my head."

“Good son! When the youth Piyūṣadhāra bowed his head at the feet of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha stroked the crown of the Bodhisattva Piyūṣadhāra with both hands and addressed him, saying:
‘Arouse the mind of great compassion and profound wisdom; For the sake of bodhi, you have cultivated sublime practices.
"The fetters are exceedingly firm, yet you have severed them with great power; you shall become a Buddha and bring benefit to the world.
"O son of good family!
At that time, the youth Candracūḍa knelt on his right knee before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Buddha, saying:"
“World-Honored One!

I wish to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Among the sentient beings in this buddha-field who possess minds characterized by equal proportions of greed, anger, and delusion, and among those sentient beings who do not abide in either wholesome or unwholesome states of mind, I shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* when the lifespan of human beings is forty thousand years.”
The Buddha Ratnagarbha said:

"In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya of kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and the remainder of a second asaṃkhyeya of kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there shall be a world named Sahā."
Why is it named Sahā?
Because the sentient beings therein endure and tolerate desire, hatred, and ignorance, and because they endure all fetters and bonds, for these reasons it is called Sahā.
At that time, there will be a great eon named Bhadra.
Why is it called Bhadra?

Because within this eon, amidst those who practice desire, hatred, delusion, and the conceit of self and sentient beings, one thousand Great Compassionate Buddhas, the Blessed Ones (Bhagavats), shall appear therein.
"O virtuous man!

At the beginning of this Bhadrakalpa, among a world where the human lifespan is forty thousand years, you shall first attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and your name shall be Krakucchanda Tathāgata, up to Buddha, World-Honored One."

"You should preach the Dharma by means of the three vehicles; there are countless sentient beings being swept away by the swift river of birth, old age, sickness, and death—may you ferry them across and establish them on the further shore of Nirvana."
"Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Candracūḍa prostrated himself with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and withdrew to sit to one side. Good son!"
At that time, the second youth, named Kambala, came forward and addressed the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
I wish to attain Buddhahood after the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, during the era when the human lifespan is thirty thousand years."
The Buddha Ratnagarbha said: "O youth!

In a future age, after the passing of one asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges and the remainder of a second asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, when the Sahā world-system has entered the Bhadrakalpa, you shall attain Buddhahood following the Tathāgata Krakucchanda. Among a world of people with a lifespan of thirty thousand years, you shall become a Buddha named Kanakamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and so forth, up to Buddha, World-Honored One, with your fame spreading far and wide."

Having heard the prophecy from the World-Honored One, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, rose and circumambulated him three times, and scattered flowers before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha. With palms joined, he praised the Buddha in verse:
“Skillfully gathered and harmonized in perfect sequence, Without error, turbidity, or confusion, pure and wondrously renowned;
O Most Exalted Sage of vast and lofty mind, You proclaim the path to enlightenment like a great blazing torch.”
The virtues of the Benefactor arise spontaneously, filled with a hundred blessings; he bestows the path of tranquil bliss upon the mountain of entanglements.
There is nothing that the Muni does not transcend, as he grants the prediction of bodhi to many sentient beings.

“Good son! At that time, the youth named Thūpa placed a bed made of the seven precious substances before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha; it was worth hundreds of thousands of measures of gold. He spread upon it what was appropriate, set out a golden bowl filled with the seven precious substances, and offered both a golden water vessel and the bed of the seven precious substances to the Buddha and the Saṅgha, addressing the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”

I desire that in a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as vast as the sands of the Ganges and the remainder of a second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as vast as the sands of the Ganges, I shall become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha during this Bhadrakalpa.

When all virtues decline and the omens of an evil age appear, sentient beings will dwell in heavy greed, anger, delusion, stinginess, and envy; relying on evil associates and false views, they will constantly delight in associating with minds of unwholesome roots, while being estranged from minds of wholesome roots, lacking right view, and possessing minds of wrong livelihood and distraction.

After the Tathāgata Kanakamuni has entered parinirvāṇa and the True Dharma has been extinguished, when the world is blind and dark and lacks a guide, I shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi among the people of a twenty-thousand-year lifespan.
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said to Ghanavyūha:
'Excellent, excellent!'"

"Brahmin! You are a virtuous man endowed with great wisdom. When an auspicious sign appeared among the wicked people of the world, and even when the lifespan of humans had reached twenty thousand years and they were blind without a guide, you made a vow therein."
Therefore, O virtuous man!
We shall name you Prājñākaruṇāmati.
You, Prājñākaruṇāmati!

In a future age, after the passing of one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and the remainder of a second asaṃkhyeya kalpa, he shall attain Buddhahood in this very Sahā world, among human beings during the twenty-thousand-year lifespan of the Bhadrakalpa, receiving the name Kāśyapa Tathāgata, up to Buddha, World-Honored One.

“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Wisdom and Compassionate Mind prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, stood to one side, and scattered flower garlands and powdered incense over the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, praising him in verse:
‘O Honored One among Men, Canopy of Great Learning, May all give rise to a mind of joy and delight;’”
With skillful and eloquent speech, the one of excellent wisdom dwells among humans and devas.
Bestowing predictions upon many sentient beings that they shall become Buddhas in the ten directions, his supernormal powers, wisdom, and intention are equal; the Buddha-dharma is beyond measure.
"The Honored One manifests the practice of awakening; therefore, I prostrate in homage.
"Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta awakened the fourth youth, named Vimalamati."
"Good son! At that time, the youth Vimalamati came before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and said:

'I wish to seek awakening in this land during this Bhadrakalpa in such a manner, for [I do not wish it] in such an evil age as that after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Kāśyapa, when the True Dharma has been extinguished and among people with a lifespan of ten thousand years, the minds of sentient beings have become increasingly deficient in the seven riches regarding generosity, ethical discipline, and the cultivation of meditative concentration.'"
Respecting evil associates and taking them as teachers, their minds take no pleasure in seeking the three grounds of merit;
nor do they delight in cultivating the three types of wholesome karma, but instead take pleasure in committing the three unwholesome and evil karmas.
Because their minds are darkened and disturbed by various fetters and afflictions, they have no desire to seek the path of the Three Vehicles.
At that time, there will not even be those capable of practicing the path to enlightenment, let alone those living for a thousand years or even a hundred;
at that time, sentient beings will not even have the name "virtuous," much less those who actually practice virtue.

In this world of five turbidities, the lifespan decreases further until it reaches ten years and the kalpa of weapons arises; at that very time, I shall descend from the heavens to rescue sentient beings, causing them to abandon unwholesome deeds and preaching the wholesome Dharma for them, so that those beings may abide in the ten wholesome courses of action. By means of these wholesome actions, I shall eliminate the fetters of sentient beings and also remove the five turbidities.

When the human lifespan reaches eighty thousand years, I shall then attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* therein, preaching the Dharma for sentient beings who have little greed, anger, delusion, ignorance, stinginess, and envy, causing them to abide in the three vehicles.
"Bhagavān!
If my intention is thus fulfilled, Bhagavān, you should grant me the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Bhagavān!"
‘If I do not receive such a prediction, I shall seek the stage of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha to swiftly escape from birth and death.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said, ‘Brāhmaṇa!’

Bodhisattvas have four grounds of indolence; if a bodhisattva possesses these forms of indolence, they will long delight in birth and death, being misled by views and undergoing the sufferings of birth and death, and will not swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
What are the four?
There may be a bodhisattva who maintains humble and lowly deportment, associates with humble and lowly companions, practices humble and lowly distribution of gifts, and makes humble and lowly vows.
What is meant by the humble and lowly deportment of a bodhisattva?

There may be a bodhisattva who violates the precepts of body, speech, and mind, or who fails to maintain dignified deportment; one who dwells together with those training as śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; one who does not practice universal giving, nor gives in all places; one who gives seeking the blessings and pleasures of gods and humans; and one who does not establish a resolute vow to adorn buddha-fields in order to deliver sentient beings.
If a bodhisattva possesses four qualities, they will long endure the suffering of birth and death and will not swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
There are bodhisattvas who, possessing four qualities, swiftly accomplish *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

What are these four? They are: guarding and upholding one’s body, speech, and mind; constantly associating with those who study the Mahāyāna; practicing all forms of giving and giving in all places; and giving with a compassionate heart for the sake of liberating all sentient beings from suffering, while establishing vows with sincere intent to adorn Buddha-lands in order to deliver sentient beings.
These are the four dharmas; by practicing them, a bodhisattva swiftly accomplishes *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, there are four dharmas which, when fully possessed by a bodhisattva, encompass the path to enlightenment.
What are these four?
Diligently practicing the pāramitās; gathering in sentient beings through giving; cultivating and accomplishing the various dhyānas; and sporting with the supernormal powers.
These are the four.
Furthermore, there are four things that never bring weariness, which a bodhisattva should fully possess:
insatiability in giving, insatiability in hearing the Dharma, insatiability in gathering in sentient beings, and insatiability in making vows.
These are the four.
Furthermore, there are four inexhaustible treasuries that a bodhisattva should fulfill:

the inexhaustible treasury of faith that a bodhisattva should fulfill; the inexhaustible treasury of preaching the Dharma that a bodhisattva should fulfill; the inexhaustible treasury of dedication that a bodhisattva should fulfill; and the inexhaustible treasury of rescuing sentient beings in distress that a bodhisattva should fulfill.
These are the four.
Furthermore, there are four purities that a bodhisattva should possess:

purity of precepts through non-self, purity of samādhi through non-sentient beings, purity of wisdom through non-life-force, and purity of the knowledge and vision of liberation through non-personhood.
These are the four dharmas that a bodhisattva should possess.

By means of these, a bodhisattva swiftly accomplishes anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and turns the wheel of space, the inconceivable wheel, the immeasurable and selfless wheel, the ineffable wheel, the wheel of provisional manifestation, the wheel of wearying aversion, and the unprecedented wheel.

"Vimalamati! In a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed, and when there remain but two *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas of the Ganges sands, not long after you have entered the Bhadrakalpa and the five corruptions have been eliminated, among human beings whose lifespan has increased to eighty thousand years, you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and you shall be known as the Tathāgata Maitreya, even unto a Buddha, a World-Honored One."

Then the brahmin Vimalamati, having prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, stood to one side. He made offerings to the World-Honored One with flower garlands and powdered incense, and praised him in verse:
“The Honored One’s face is like the full moon; The mark of the white tuft is like snow.
Your body is pure like a mountain of gold— Who would not wish for the Muni?”
"Valiant as the king of beasts, with immeasurable virtues illuminating the world,
his radiance pervading everywhere— he has now bestowed upon me the prophecy of Buddhahood.
The great teacher, the brahmin Sāgaradatta, exhorted those one thousand men— minus one boy who had mastered the four Vedas— to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
They were as follows:
Kālaka, Sundarika, Nāga, Muni, Kāśyapa, Maitreya, Putra, Dyota, and so forth—a thousand in number, with two youths being slightly fewer.

These youths were masters of the four Vedas; they all established the vow for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Within this Bhadrakalpa, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon them all, identifying the youngest among them as the one destined for it within this Bhadrakalpa.
The Great Master perceived this and said: "Ho! Mahābala!"
"Why do you gaze for so long?
You, Mahāsattva, should abandon other mental conceptions and give rise to great compassion for the sake of sentient beings.
He then addressed him with a verse:
“Sentient beings suffer old age, sickness, and death, Submerged in the river-flow of craving;
Abiding in the terrors of the triple world, They receive the subtle form within the womb.”
Drinking the poison of fetters, they harm one another; in the vast wilderness, they suffer burning and boiling.
Blind with ignorance, they lose the path of goodness and are oppressed by birth and death.
The three realms burn fiercely with suffering, and all abide in false views.
All beings within the five realms of existence revolve like the turning of a wheel.
Sentient beings lack the Dharma-eye; contemplate those who have no savior.
Cultivate wisdom to eliminate doubt and confusion; now you may seek Bodhi.
For the world’s river of craving, you act as a bridge for sentient beings;
because you untie the world’s bonds, your mind is directed toward Bodhi.
You remove delusion and open the Dharma-eye, bestowing the unsurpassed path.
Birth and death are thus within the triple world; fill it with the flavor of the Dharma.
You may swiftly attain great benefit by prostrating at the feet of the Muni.
Establish the most steadfast vow to become a Buddha, a World Teacher.
He consoles all living beings and delivers the multitudes from the wilderness;
he bestows the wondrous path of liberation, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment.
Seeking to rain down the Dharma-rain, he extinguishes the suffering of sentient beings.
"Good son! At that time, the youth Mahābala addressed him, saying:
'Great Master!'"
I do not delight in birth and death, but delight in seeking noble virtue;
furthermore, I do not seek the vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, but desire to seek the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
Observing the realms where I am to transform others, I await the proper time to establish my vows.
“Great Master!
For this reason, I have remained in contemplation until now; wait but a moment, Master, while I let out my lion’s roar. “Good son!”
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta left him and returned to inform his five brahmin disciples who were his constant attendants:
"O young men!..."
"You may resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

They said to their teacher, "We have no wealth or treasures with which to make offerings to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus; how can we, who have not yet planted roots of goodness, resolve our minds upon Bodhi?"
"Good son! At that time, the National Preceptor addressed his disciples: to the first, named Karabhuju, he gave an earring of the seven precious jewels;
to the second, named Tarabhuju, he likewise gave an earring of the seven precious jewels."
The third was named Jarābuśu, to whom he gave a bed of the seven treasures;
the fourth was named Khagabuśu, to whom he gave a staff of the seven treasures;
the fifth was named Varābuśu, to whom he gave a basin for washing made of pure gold.
And he said to them:
"You may use these items to make offerings to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, and resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Then the five attendants approached the World-Honored One; having each presented their offerings to the Buddha and the Saṃgha, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We pray only that the World-Honored One..."
Grant us the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; within that Bhadrakalpa, we shall therein attain the unsurpassed, true, and perfect Way.
Thus it was briefly said:
"O son of good family!
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed upon the youth Karapuṣpa the prediction of his future enlightenment, saying: 'Within this Bhadrakalpa, you shall be named Dṛḍhasvara Tathāgata.'"
After him, Tarapuṣya shall be named Ratisaṃjñāmanas Tathāgata;
after him, Jarapuṣya shall be named Vaṇijagāmin Tathāgata;
after him, Khagapuṣya shall be named Priyaviśuddha Tathāgata.
Thereafter, the youth Śarabhuju shall be named King of the Pure Topknot Tathāgata.
As soon as the Buddha had bestowed these predictions upon those five youths for the Bhadrakalpa, the Great Teacher again addressed Mahāsthāmaprāpta, saying:
"You, Mahāsthāmaprāpta!"

Now, in the presence of the Blessed One, you may make a vow to take up a Buddha-field adorned according to your own wishes; nourish all sentient beings with the flavor of the Dharma, and practice the bodhisattva path with firm vigor—do not delay any longer.
He took the boy by the arm and led him to where the Buddha was.
"Good son! At that time, the youth Mahābala stood before the World-Honored One and addressed the Buddha, saying:"
“World-Honored One!
In the future, during the subsequent Bhadrakalpa, how many Muni-suns will appear in the world?
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha replied:
“O youth! During the half-intermediate kalpa, one thousand and four Muni-suns shall appear in the world.
The youth addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

When, within that Bhadrakalpa, even after the thousand-three Muni-suns have entered parinirvāṇa, that last of them, the youth Śālavasu, shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and be named Rājendra-nīlapatracūḍa Tathāgata.”

For that length of time, I shall practice the bodhisattva conduct and perform difficult and arduous austerities—practicing generosity, maintaining ethical discipline, cultivating meditative concentration, acquiring extensive learning, exerting diligence, and practicing patience. In accordance with my merit and wisdom, I shall fully perfect them all; and before any of the Buddhas of this Bhadrakalpa have long been established in enlightenment, I shall first offer them worship and support.
After his parinirvāṇa, he shall honor the relics according to the rites for śarīras and protect and uphold the True Dharma.
For sentient beings deficient in ethical discipline, he shall exhort them to maintain the precepts and cause them to abide therein;
for sentient beings afflicted by meager insight, he shall exhort them toward right view and cause them to abide therein.
They shall exhort sentient beings with deficient resolve to abide in right resolve;
they shall cause those lacking dignified deportment to abide in dignified deportment;
and they shall manifest various and manifold virtuous practices for the sake of sentient beings.

Not long after those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have entered parinirvāṇa, I shall once again establish the True Dharma, the Eye of the True Dharma, and the Compendium of the True Dharma, and cause the lamp of the True Dharma to blaze forth in the world.

During the kalpa of weapons, I shall exhort and transform sentient beings, causing them to abide in non-killing up to right view. By means of the ten wholesome courses of action, I shall pull sentient beings out from the path of error and establish them upon the good path; I shall eliminate the darkness of their evil conduct and reveal the Dharma of wholesome practice. Throughout the turbidities of the kalpa—including the turbidity of lifespan, views, afflictions, and sentient beings—I shall utterly eradicate them.

During the kalpa of famine, I shall exhort and transform sentient beings, leading them to practice the dāna-pāramitā so that they may abide therein. By means of the six pāramitās, I shall eliminate all the turbidity of the kalpa of famine, as well as its disorder, strife, and enmity or jealousy; and among sentient beings, I shall eradicate the defilements of their fetters.

During the kalpa of pestilence, I shall exhort and transform sentient beings through the six points of respectful harmony and the four methods of attraction, causing them to abide therein, so as to eliminate the darkness of pestilence for sentient beings and even to extinguish their fetters.
Throughout the half-aeon of the Bhadrakalpa in all the Buddha-fields of Sahā, I shall thus rescue sentient beings from their distresses.

After those one thousand and four World-Honored Ones have appeared and entered parinirvāṇa, and after all their True Dharma has vanished, I shall then attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within this Bhadrakalpa, with a lifespan equal to the measure of the lifespans of those one thousand and four Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa.
Once I have attained bodhi, my lifespan shall be equal to theirs;
the number of my assembly of śrāvakas shall also be equal to the number of their śrāvaka assemblies;
and the number of sentient beings I shall deliver alone shall be equal to those delivered by the fourteen thousand Tathāgatas during half an eon.

Should those disciples of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, violate the precepts and fall into the forest of false views; should they fail to revere the Buddhas and harbor much malice, envy, ill will, and harmful intent toward the Dharma and the Saṅgha; should they lose their right mind and, with transgressed minds, slander the noble ones, revile the True Dharma, and commit acts of immediate retribution—I vow that when I attain Bodhi, I shall rescue all such beings from within saṃsāra and establish them in the city of fearless Nirvāṇa.

"Until my parinirvāṇa, and for as long as the True Dharma remains until the end of this Bhadrakalpa, when my True Dharma has perished and the Bhadrakalpa is exhausted, may my teeth and bodily relics transform into immeasurable asaṃkhyeya emanation Buddhas. May their bodies be adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, and may each mark be further adorned by eighty minor characteristics.

May these emanation Buddhas travel to the immeasurable asaṃkhyeya Buddha-less lands throughout the ten directions, and may each emanation Buddha exhort those immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings, causing them to abide in the Three Vehicles."

In any buddha-field that is being destroyed by a kalpa of calamity, he causes those transformation buddhas to go there and rescue sentient beings as previously described; thereafter, he causes them to become wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels.
In those Buddha-fields where there are sentient beings lacking precious jewels, he goes to those lands and manifests the raining down of jewels at will, revealing hidden treasures.

Furthermore, in other Buddha-fields where sentient beings have few roots of goodness and are afflicted by illness, he also goes to them and causes the rain of gośīrṣa sandalwood from the "this-side" of the ocean to fall; by means of this fragrant rain, he eliminates the afflictions of the fetters, physical ailments, and the distress of views for those beings, causing them to diligently cultivate the three fields of merit and attain rebirth in the heavens.
“World-Honored One!
When I practice the bodhisattva path, I wish to deliver sentient beings in this way.
When I attain bodhi, I shall perform the work of a Buddha in this manner.”
"After my parinirvāṇa, may I likewise enable the salvation of sentient beings within such immeasurable and boundless Buddha-fields.
World-Honored One!

If I do not fulfill this in such a way, and am unable to act as a fine medicine for sentient beings to rescue them, then after I have paid homage to the Buddha, may I not see the Buddhas currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma in the immeasurable and boundless worlds of the ten directions; and today, may the World-Honored One not grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

Furthermore, although the World-Honored One has now bestowed the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon many hundreds of millions of sentient beings, he has caused me not to see those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, nor to hear the sound of *bodhi*.

If my wish is not fulfilled in this way, may I continue to wander in saṃsāra without hearing the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, or the sound of the Saṅgha; may I not hear the sound of wholesome karma, and may these various sounds never pass through my ears.
"May I always remain in the Avīci Hell.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha addressed the youth Mahābaladhara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O virtuous man!
You should act as a wholesome medicine for sentient beings to deliver them from all suffering and hardship.
O virtuous man!"
Therefore, I name you Vimalaprabhā Bhaiṣajyarāja.
You, Vimalaprabhā Bhaiṣajyarāja!

In a future age, after the passing of one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and the remainder of a second asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, during this Bhadrakalpa, you shall first make offerings to the fourteen thousand Tathāgatas who have not long attained Buddhahood, even until the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Śyāmāśvatīrṇa-keśarāja, just as you have vowed.
After the extinction of the True Dharma, you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, being named Loushi Tathāgata, up to Buddha, World-Honored One, with a lifespan of half an eon;

the number of your śrāvaka disciples alone shall equal that of the śrāvaka saṃghas of the one thousand and four Buddhas of this Bhadrakalpa, and the number of sentient beings you deliver shall likewise be equal;
after your parinirvāṇa, when the True Dharma has perished and the Bhadrakalpa has come to an end, your teeth and relics shall become various transformation Buddhas.

In this way, it continues until even in Buddha-less lands, sandalwood incense rains down, eliminating the afflictions of the fetters, the maladies of the eyes, and physical ailments, establishing sentient beings in the three grounds of merit so that they all attain rebirth in the heavens.
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimalaprabhā-bhaiṣajyarāja addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”
"If my intention may be thus fulfilled, I only pray that the World-Honored One will place upon the crown of my head a foot adorned with the marks of a hundred merits.
"Good son! [The Buddha said.]
Then the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha immediately stroked his head with his hand, adorned with the marks of a hundred merits.
Son of good family!

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahauṣadhi Vimalaprabha was filled with great joy and his heart leaped with exultation; having prostrated himself on the ground to pay homage at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, he withdrew to stand to one side.
Then the brahmin Sāgara-datta gave him a celestial karpāsa garment and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
O noble man!"
"Your wish is most excellent.
From this day forward, do not serve as my messenger; act according to your own desires.
*The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, Scroll Four.
The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Five.
The name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost; now appended to the Qin Records.
16. Chapter Sixteen: The Great Teacher’s Establishment of Vows. The Great Teacher’s Establishment of Vows, Chapter Sixteen.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta had this thought:

‘I have already exhorted and transformed many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; there is now no one in this great assembly who is not [so resolved].’”
Each of these mahāsattvas established sublime vows to take up pure buddha-fields; with the sole exception of Piyadassin, those belonging to the Bhadrakalpa likewise avoided this degenerate age.

I reflect that in this degenerate age, I should nourish all sentient beings with the flavor of the Dharma; I should be firm and courageous, and I shall let out such a lion’s roar as to cause this entire assembly of bodhisattvas to attain what they have never experienced before.
Furthermore, I shall cause the entire assembly—including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and human beings—to join their palms in prostration and pay respectful homage to me.
May the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, praise me, saying "Excellent," and bestow upon me a prophecy.
Furthermore, may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who currently dwell in the world and preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings throughout the immeasurable,
boundless, and incalculable worlds of the ten directions, praise me, saying "Excellent," and likewise bestow upon me the prophecy of Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi when I utter this lion’s roar.

May he dispatch a messenger to console me, so that this great assembly may see and hear that messenger; therein, I shall establish for future generations the eye of aspiration for Bodhisattvas endowed with great compassion.
May those who, from this time forward until I attain bodhi, hear my vow, also obtain that which is most unprecedented.
Furthermore, may Bodhisattvas endowed with great compassion likewise take the vow for bodhi during such a time of a turbid Buddha-field and a world of great evil.

For those few who are shrouded in the darkness of the afflictions of the fetters and drifting in sickness, I shall rescue them and perform the work of a Buddha, preaching the Dharma for sentient beings.

Even after my parinirvāṇa, throughout inconceivable, immeasurable, and boundless Buddha-fields, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, shall praise and extol me before the assemblies of bodhisattvas, and for the sake of the bodhisattvas, they shall speak of my Eye of Vows.

May that bodhisattva receive the power of great compassion; upon hearing my vow, may they attain what has never been attained before and likewise give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings.
May they take such a vow for enlightenment, no different from the vow I have taken this day, and likewise attain perfect awakening within this turbid world-system.

May they rescue and liberate the multitudes from the four surging waves, transforming and delivering sentient beings through the Dharma of the three vehicles, until they are established on the path to nirvana.

“Good son! At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, having fully cultivated such great compassionate vows, adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder, and went to where the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha was.

At that very moment, many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of devas in the sky played hundreds of millions of celestial instruments, rained down various heavenly flowers, and with one voice praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"O Noble One!
Having approached the World-Honored One, you have now made a sublime vow to extinguish the afflictions, sufferings, and fetters of the sentient beings in this world with the water of wisdom.
The entire great assembly joined their palms toward him and praised him with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
You have attained wondrous wisdom to benefit us; we wish to hear the profound intent of your firm vow.

At that time, the Great Teacher went to where the World-Honored One was and knelt with his right knee upon the ground. Then, this trichiliocosm *Naitilān* Buddha-field shook in six ways, trembling violently and shaking so intensely that it tilted, swayed, surged, and subsided. Bells, chimes, conchs, and drums resounded spontaneously, while beasts and flocks of birds uttered gentle sounds, and even the withered trees of the world all sprouted flowers and leaves.
Among the earth-dwelling spirits within this trichiliocosm, there were those who had been exhorted toward bodhicitta and those who had not;

however, excluding those in the hells, the realm of hungry ghosts, and various forms of animal existence, they all attained a mind of benefit, a virtuous mind, a mind free from enmity and jealousy, a mind free from turbidity, a mind of loving-kindness, and a mind of unprecedented resolve, all of which became fully satisfied.

There are those who dwell depending on space; they find joy in their minds regarding the void and, for the sake of hearing the vow of the Brahmin, offer worship with various flower garlands, incense, music, diverse jewels, banners and canopies, as well as flags, robes, and head-houses, using soft voices.

Even the gods as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven all descended to Jambudvīpa and remained in the air, holding various celestial incenses up to those of Tuṣita, in order to make offerings for the sake of hearing the Brahmin’s vow.
At that time, the brahmin joined his palms in reverence and praised the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha with these verses:
“Your Reverence wanders in samādhi like Brahmā, Your countenance is composed like Śakra;
In bestowing wealth you are like a sovereign, Holding the most wondrous jewels like a venerable seer.”
The sound of his roar of virtue is like that of a lion; he is firm and immovable, comparable to Mount Sumeru.
He is without anger or resentment, like the great ocean; he endures both the good and the evil with equanimity, like the earth.
He removes all defilements, like the great waters; he burns away the forest of fetters, like the fire of the seers.
Unstained by attachment like a swift wind, he reveals the truth like the Great Deity;
the Muni pours forth the Dharma like the rain of a dragon, filling and sustaining the world like seasonal moisture;
he subdues non-Buddhists like a master debater, and the Sage emits the fragrance of virtue like a wondrous flower.
Your wondrous voice is as soft and gentle as that of Brahmā; you cure the world and liberate it from suffering like a skilled physician.
Your mind abides in equanimity like a compassionate mother, and you constantly gather in sentient beings like a father.
You shatter all stubborn enmities like a vajra, and sever the branches of craving like a divine sword.
He ferries sentient beings across like a boatman; he bestows wisdom upon others like a Muni;
he grants cooling light like the moon of the Muni; he causes the flowers of humanity to bloom like the sun;
he bestows the four supreme fruits like a wondrous tree; and he is surrounded by hosts of sages like the king of birds.
Your noble intent is as vast as the great ocean; You regard all beings in the world with equanimity, like blades of grass.
You contemplate the nature of all phenomena as empty space; Your noble equanimity follows the world, just like water.
The Buddha bestows the prediction of Bodhi upon many multitudes; He maintains the most wondrous marks and possesses sublime great compassion.
I have transformed sentient beings in measureless abundance; I pray that you now grant me the prediction of Bodhi.
May I attain Buddhahood in this world of turbidity, fetters, and enmity, And establish all sentient beings upon the path of tranquil stillness.

“Good son! When the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, had praised the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha with these verses, the entire great assembly—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and human beings—exclaimed in praise:
‘Excellent!’”
Then the National Preceptor addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

I have exhorted and transformed many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; each of them, having contemplated this, has accepted a wondrous land and attained a pure intention."

Having planted various roots of goodness, they easily transform sentient beings. These thousand [beings], such as Caturmukhamālā and others, are common to the four Vedas; they are those whom the Tathāgata has prophesied as destined for the Bhadrakalpa. These great men likewise teach and transform with the Three Vehicles those sentient beings who are dominated by greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as the sense of self. They too shall abandon the heavy fetters of affliction in this evil age, renounce the karma of the Avīci hell, and cease slandering the True Dharma, reviling the noble ones, dwelling in false views, and lacking the seven noble riches.
They do not know their parents, do not recognize śramaṇas, and do not distinguish brāhmaṇas; they do not know how to repay kindness, do not understand merit, and do not fear the next world.
They do not seek the three virtues of the heavens or the qualities of a celestial being, but instead commit the ten unwholesome karmas of the three unvirtuous paths.
They are abandoned by all spiritual friends and reviled by all the wise;
they are swept away by the swift currents of afflictions in the three realms, submerged and scorched in the ash-river of birth and death;
obscured by the darkness of ignorance and estranged from all wholesome karma, they cast such sentient beings away into Buddha-less lands.
Having abandoned all roots of goodness and accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, they are exhausted by false paths and dwell in a vast wilderness.
At that time, in the Sahā world during the Bhadrakalpa, the human lifespan will turn to one thousand years; thus, they will be forsaken by these wise and virtuous men.

At that time, being oppressed by the causes and conditions of birth and death within the three realms, these beings have no place to cast themselves, no direction to turn, and no refuge; they are trapped within the vessel of suffering.

[The Bodhisattvas] abandon these beings to instead take up exquisite lands where it is easy to transform them, their minds purified, as they plant various roots of goodness with tireless diligence, having previously approached and made offerings to many Buddhas, thereby rescuing and transforming them.
"World-Honored One!
Is it not so? The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha replied to him, saying:
"So it is, so it is! Brahmin! In accordance with the adornments of the Buddha-fields that those beings have taken up through their vows, I likewise bestow predictions upon them."
The brahmin addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
My heart trembles like the leaves of a plantain tree; my mind is filled with profound anxiety, and my entire body is utterly despondent.”
“World-Honored One!

All these great bodhisattvas have indeed given rise to great compassion; yet they abandon that evil age when it is rampant, and all those sentient beings dwelling in the midst of darkness are likewise forsaken.”
“World-Honored One!

In a future age, after the passing of one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, two *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and three *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—during the Bhadrakalpa, when the lifespan of worldlings is one thousand years—I shall, throughout that period, remain within saṃsāra to practice the conduct of bodhi. I shall not take in and deliver sentient beings through the power of vows; rather, I shall practice the six *pāramitās* to bring them to transformation and deliverance.”
I have heard from the Buddha that being able to relinquish material things as a gift is the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*).
I shall practice this perfection of giving in this manner:
wherever I am born, should there be those who come to me seeking, I shall give to them in this way, namely:

Food and drink, *khañja*, *pūja*, *śaṅkha*, and *liśa*; clothing, bedding, gardens, dwellings, garlands and ornaments, scented ointments, and medicine according to the illness; banners, flags, parasols, wealth, elephants, horses, and carriages; gold, silver, various jewels, *maṇi*, pearls, lapis lazuli, *musāragalva*, *aśmagarbha*, *pravāḍa*, *gomedaka*, *muktikā*, and other treasures—out of compassion for sentient beings, he joyfully gives such things as these. For the sake of delivering sentient beings, he does not hope for karmic retribution; in order to gather in and deliver sentient beings, he bestows them fully and completely.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings who seek that which is extremely difficult to relinquish, and I shall give it to them—namely:

male and female slaves, villages, cities, palaces, royal thrones, wives, concubines, sons, and daughters, as well as my hands, feet, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin, blood, flesh, marrow, and even my life, or even if they seek my head. Out of compassion for sentient beings, I shall bestow such things with supreme joy; seeking no karmic reward, but only for the sake of gathering and delivering them, I shall thus practice the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*).

Never before has there been a bodhisattva practicing the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* who was able to practice the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) in such a manner; nor shall there ever be, in the future, a bodhisattva practicing the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* who is able to perform such a great sacrifice.

Just as I have practiced the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and practiced the *dāna-pāramitā* throughout immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*), hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayuta* eons in whatever places I was born.

"I shall, for the sake of future Bodhisattvas endowed with great compassion, establish them in the light of the merit of bestowing the eye and contemplate all fetters; this is the *śīlapāramitā*. I shall thus practice *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, practicing various forms of upholding the precepts;

I shall perform the unsurpassed and difficult ascetic practices as previously described, not falling away from the objective because I contemplate both self and non-self; this is the *kṣāntipāramitā*. I shall thus cultivate *kṣānti* as previously described."

Furthermore, to feel weary of all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta*), to practice the supreme tranquility of all unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛta*) without regressing—this is the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*).
To practice equanimity toward all activities and dwell in emptiness (*śūnyatā*) and so forth—this is the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*).

The patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena according to their true nature is the perfection of wisdom; with such firm and courageous strength, I shall practice the perfection of wisdom for immeasurable, incalculable billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

Previously, among those bodhisattvas practicing the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, there was no one capable of thus practicing the perfection of wisdom with such firm and courageous resolve; nor will there ever be, in the future, any bodhisattva practicing the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* who can practice the perfection of wisdom with such firm and courageous resolve as I do, for the purpose of establishing the eye of the merit of wisdom for all future bodhisattvas endowed with great compassion.

From my initial generation of the mind of awakening until the manifestation of great compassion for future bodhisattvas and even unto unsurpassed parinirvāṇa, those bodhisattvas have attained what they had never experienced before. Therefore, I do not practice giving, morality, non-reliant patience, signless diligence, non-abiding dhyāna, or unattached wisdom with a sense of duality or self, nor do I seek karmic retribution.

Sentient beings lack the seven noble riches; I abandon all such beings and place them in a land where no Buddha dwells, where they commit acts of immediate retribution, slander the True Dharma, revile the worthy and holy ones, and are entirely possessed of wrong views. Because these beings have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness and fallen into the wilderness, being beset by these false paths, I practice the pāramitās with the most courageous and vigorous effort for their sake.

For the sake of establishing the seeds of roots of goodness for each and every sentient being, I am able to endure the agonies of the Avīci Hell for ten great kalpas; likewise, I can endure such suffering among animals, hungry ghosts, yakṣas, and those who are poor among the poor. Just as the seeds of roots of goodness are planted by all sentient beings, I shall thus gather and deliver those whose minds are empty, weary, and withered, until the end of the Bhadrakalpa. During this time, I shall not seek the blessings of honor and profit from gods or humans, except for the single lifetime remaining before my succession to Buddhahood while dwelling in Tuṣita Heaven awaiting the attainment of Bodhi.

“During that period of saṃsāra, I shall approach as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, and with various offerings as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, I shall make offerings to each and every Buddha;
from each and every Buddha, I shall attain merits as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, and I shall exhort as many sentient beings as there are atoms in a Buddha-field toward Bodhi.”
The Pratyekabuddhayāna and the Śrāvakayāna are also like this; according to their inclinations, I exhort and transform them in such ways.
If there is no Buddha in the world, I become a rishi and, through various wholesome deeds, transform those sentient beings, causing them to abide in supernatural powers.
To those who, due to wrong views, worship the deity Maheśvara, he manifests as Maheśvara to exhort them toward wholesome karma.
He manifests as Nārāyaṇa, the sun, or the moon, and even manifests in the form of Brahmā, exhorting them toward the sublime Dharma.

Sometimes he manifests as a garuḍa to exhort garuḍas to cultivate various virtuous deeds; even manifesting in the form of a rabbit, he satisfies hungry and thirsty sentient beings with the flesh and blood of his own body, saving all those in urgent distress by means of his own life and limb.
"Bhagavān!

For that duration of time, I shall cultivate various difficult practices with supreme vigor for the sake of those whose minds are withered and who lack roots of goodness. For the sake of such sentient beings at that time, I shall undergo the various bitter sufferings of birth and death until, after passing one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa and the remainder of a second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, I enter this Bhadrakalpa, just as the youth Candracūḍa attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, becoming the Tathāgata Kāraka-śunda."

May I, at that time, with the eye of noble wisdom, behold in each of the ten directions as many worlds as there are atoms in a thousand Buddha-fields all those Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, who have already turned the wheel of Dharma and currently abide in the world—those beings whom I previously exhorted and transformed, yet whose minds were parched and who had accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, who lacked the seven noble riches, and who were abandoned by all; those who dwelt in empty Buddha-fields, committed the acts of immediate retribution, slandered the true Dharma, reviled the worthy and holy ones, and were even trapped by false paths in the great wilderness;
and for whom I previously praised *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and exhorted them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, causing them to dwell therein.
Those sentient beings were previously exhorted and transformed by me to abide in the *dānapāramitā*, up to and including the *prajñāpāramitā*;
those sentient beings were by me established in the roots of goodness for unsurpassed *nirvāṇa* and pulled forth from the evil destinies;

they were made to stand firm in the perfection of wisdom and merit, led to the presence of the various Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones currently dwelling in the world, received the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, attained *samādhi*, *dhāraṇī*, and patience, and ascended to the stages (*bhūmi*).

Those beings were previously exhorted and instructed by me to establish vows to take up the adornment of Buddha-fields; they are those who, according to their own desires, have taken up the adornment of Buddha-fields.

“At that time, when I first enter this Bhadrakalpa, at the rising of the holy sun-like Kālakasunda Tathāgata, may I behold the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the worlds of the ten directions—numbering as many as the atoms within a thousand Buddha-fields—who remain in the world preaching the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.

Not long after the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kālakasunda has attained Buddhahood, I shall go to his presence and make offerings to him with various requisites. I shall consult him and pose difficult questions, leave the household life to cultivate the precepts, and become foremost in erudition, samādhi, and preaching the Dharma, with the sole exception of the Tathāgata himself.”

At that time, for those sentient beings whose minds are parched and withered, who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, who are submerged in the path of false views, who commit acts of immediate retribution, and even those sentient beings in the wilderness who are beset by wrong paths, I shall gather them in, deliver them, and preach the Dharma for them.

"After the noble sun has set, I shall fully perform the Buddha-work. Thus, not long after Kanakamuni and Kāśyapa had attained Buddhahood, he went to their respective places and fully performed the Buddha-work;

continuing in this manner until the time of humans with a lifespan of a thousand years, he established sentient beings in the three grounds of merit. After this, he ascended to the heavens above, where he preached the Dharma to the devas and gathered them in for deliverance.

Even until the lifespan of sentient beings reaches one hundred and twenty years, they will be exceedingly foolish, arrogant, and conceited regarding their physical appearance; relying on their own lineage, they will be muddled and ignorant, harboring much envy and anger while dwelling in the darkness of the five turbidities.

These sentient beings will have extremely heavy greed, hatred, and delusion; they will be haughty, jealous, and attached to what is not the Dharma, sustaining themselves through unrighteousness; possessing wrong views and inverted perspectives, they will lack the seven noble riches;
they will regard neither mother nor father as such, nor śramaṇas nor brāhmaṇas; they will not know how to repay kindness, nor will they cultivate merit.

They do not fear future lives; they do not cultivate the three grounds of merit, nor do they seek the Three Vehicles. They do not practice the three wholesome karmas but instead cultivate the three unwholesome karmas; they do not practice the ten wholesome paths of action but delight in practicing the ten unwholesome paths.
Hindered by the four inversions, they dwell within the four cycles of rebirth, follow after the four Māras, and are swept away by the river of the four illnesses.

Constantly following the five hindrances and the six sense-faculties, they are mired in ignorance; submerged in the wilderness of the eight heterodoxies, they perpetually give rise to the various latent tendencies (anuśaya) and do not seek the merit and virtue of devas or humans.

They are beset by inverted views and false paths; they commit acts of immediate retribution and slander the True Dharma; they revile the noble and holy ones and sever all roots of goodness; they are stubborn, coarse, and ungrateful. Whatever they do, they immediately forget;
seeing those who practice virtue, they harbor evil thoughts and revile them. Possessing shallow wisdom, little learning, and great forgetfulness, their faculties are incomplete;

they are emaciated, weak, and lack clothing. While in the womb, they harbor perverse thoughts; beset by myriad ailments, their countenance is ugly and foul. They disregard what lies before or behind them, lacking shame and remorse, and are further haunted by terror.
For even a short duration of time, one may perform many evil deeds of body, speech, and mind, regarding this as noble.

Sentient beings harbor views of eternalism or nihilism; their minds are attached to the five aggregates, greedy for the five desires, and characterized by joyfulness, restlessness, resentment, deceit, turbidity, coarseness, anger, and lack of faith.
A mind that is restless, a mind that is unattached, a mind that is unsubdued, a mind that clings to what is not the Dharma,
a mind that does not abide, a mind that seeks signs, a distracted mind, a mind that harms one another, a mind detached from the Dharma,

a mind that expects no retribution, a mind that calculates the existence of dharmas, a mind that extinguishes goodness, a mind that does not give rise to goodness, and a mind that does not seek nirvāṇa.
A mind that is stilled; a mind that does not know how to make offerings; a mind that accumulates all fetters and bonds;
a mind that views old age, sickness, and death as being without causes or conditions; a mind that undergoes various afflictions; a mind that clings to all obstacles;
a mind that destroys the banner of the Dharma; a mind that raises the banner of [false] views; a mind that mutually reviles one another; and a mind that devours one another.
At that time, there were no sentient beings who did not harbor a mind of self-exaltation, a mind of seeking to distress others, a mind of blazing envy, a mind of mutual slaughter,
a mind of insatiable greed, a mind of jealousy toward all that others possess, a mind devoid of gratitude, a mind of theft,
a mind of sexual misconduct, a mind of deceitful provocation, or a mind lacking aspiration.
Therein, following one another in succession, they hear such sounds as these:
the sounds of hell-beings, the sounds of animals, the sounds of hungry ghosts, the sound of illness, the sound of old age, and the sound of death.
...the sound of harm, the sound of calamity, the sound of being secretly dispatched to another country, the sound of shackles, fetters, manacles, and imprisonment,
the sound of torture and flogging, the sound of speaking of right and wrong, the sound of reviling, the sound of piercing and carving,
the sound of destroying the assembly, the sound of theft and robbery, the sound of military horses, the sound of famine, and the sound of covetousness and sexual misconduct;...
The sound of lying, the sound of madness, the sound of frivolous speech, the sound of harsh words, the sound of double-tongued speech, the sound of jealousy,
the sound of hoarding wealth within and without, the sound of quarreling, the sound of egoism,
the sound of love and hatred, the sound of the beloved and the unloved, the sound of separation from the beloved and union with the hated, the sound of hawking and trading, and the sound of mutual...
The sounds of mutual buying and selling; the sound of dwelling in the womb; the sound of foul stench; the sound of cold; the sound of heat; the sound of hunger; the sound of thirst;
the sound of exhaustion; the sound of illness and pain; the sound of planting and cultivation; the sound of grieving over various karmas;
the sound of being oppressed by various sufferings; the sound of various epidemics; and the sounds of sentient beings harming one another in succession.
From hearing such sounds, there are forty-five [points]:
"At that time, sentient beings who lack roots of goodness, have few spiritual friends, and harbor evil minds will fill the Sahā world."

All sentient beings dwell in Buddha-less lands abandoned by all-encompassing omniscience (*sarvajñā*), where there is no giving, no upholding of precepts, and no cultivation of meditative concentration; where there is no accumulation of wholesome karma and only various unwholesome dharmas abound.
I shall ferry them across the ocean of birth and death by means of the Noble Eightfold Path and establish them in the city of fearlessness.

At that time, because the sentient beings have accumulated heavy evil karma, the Sahā Buddha-field will become extremely corrupt and wretched. It will be abandoned by those who possess merit and have planted roots of goodness. Everywhere on the ground there will grow salt-encrusted soil, shards, gravel, earth, stones, and mountains rising unevenly; it will abound with venomous insects, mosquitoes, gadflies, malignant snakes, and predatory birds and beasts.

At that time, untimely winds will arise in profusion—foul, turbid, coarse, and harsh—and untimely torrential rains will fall, accompanied by calamities such as poisonous mist, salty bitterness, frost, and hail.

The earth will produce such malevolent seeds of plants and trees, whose branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, and various grain species will be devoid of flavor; these will be the only things available for sentient beings to consume and sustain their bodies.
It will be untimely, defiled by evil turbidity, mixed with poison, and coarse; when those sentient beings consume it, they shall all increase in coarseness, wickedness, killing, and deception.

They will engage in the spreading of rumors and the discussion of right and wrong, failing to show mutual respect, giving rise to hearts of fear, hearts of mutual hatred and jealousy, and hearts desiring to harm one another.

They will drink blood, eat flesh, and clothe themselves in skins; they will delight in grasping weapons to wound, kill, and inflict injury; they will rely on physical appearance, lineage, wealth, status, mathematics, and secular texts; they will ride horses, twang their bowstrings, and engage in battle against the masses; they will be envious and arrogant, diligently practicing various such base and contemptible things—this is an age of suffering and hardship.

"At that time, I shall descend from Tuṣita Heaven; for the sake of maturing the roots of goodness of sentient beings, I will enter the womb of the chief consort of the most excellent Wheel-Turning King and dwell therein."

At that time, I shall emit pure light that illuminates the entire Sahā buddha-field, reaching upward as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven and downward as far as the Golden Wheel, its wondrous radiance pervading everywhere.

At that time, those beings born in the Sahā Buddha-field—whether in the hells, as animals, as hungry ghosts, born in the heavens, or born among humans; whether in the realm of form, the formless realm, the sphere of perception, the sphere of non-perception, or the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—all were caused to see this radiance and have it touch their bodies. This caused them all to grow weary of the suffering of birth and death and to joyfully seek nirvana, even reaching the state where the mind’s fetters are extinguished; this was the first planting of the seeds for the path to nirvana.
I shall receive the Samādhi of Certainty in All Dharmas and the Samādhi-mind of the Dharma-gate of Single Intention, remaining in my mother’s womb for ten months.

Furthermore, when I attain Buddhahood, those sentient beings who weary of and seek liberation from birth and death, and whom I am destined to deliver, shall see me during these ten months within the womb sitting cross-legged, their minds entering samādhi like the manifestation of a mani jewel.

When ten months had passed and he was born, through the Samādhi of Accumulating All Merit, the six kinds of earthquakes occurred; all the Sahā Buddha-fields, from the Akaniṣṭha Heaven above down to the Golden Wheel below, were completely shaken.
At that time, those beings born in the Sahā Buddha-field—whether in the hells or even among humans—I shall awaken them all.
I shall emerge from my mother’s right side, and with wondrous light, I shall universally illuminate the Sahā Buddha-field so that there is nowhere it does not reach.

At that time, he likewise awakened all sentient beings in the Sahā buddha-field: for those sentient beings who had not yet planted the seeds of roots of goodness, he planted the seeds of nirvāṇa; for those who had already planted the seeds of nirvāṇa, he caused them to give rise to the vow to reach [liberation].
When my feet tread upon the earth, may this Sahā Buddha-field tremble in six ways, surging and subsiding as far as the limit of the golden wheel.

At that time, I shall awaken all sentient beings—those who rely on water, those who rely on land, those who rely on space, those who dwell in the four modes of birth, and those who abide in the five destinies.
For those sentient beings who have not yet sprouted the tooth of their vow, I shall cause it to grow.
For those who have already sprouted the teeth of their vows, may they be established in the Three Vehicles and attain non-retrogression.

At the time of my birth, may the Great Brahmā, the Māra King, Śakra, the world-protecting devas of the sun and moon, the nāga kings, and the *asaṃjñi-saṃskāra* great-merit *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, nāgas, and *asuras* all come to make offerings to me.
May I, immediately upon birth, walk seven steps.
By means of this teaching on the Samādhi of Accumulating All Merit, may I cause that great assembly to abide in the Three Vehicles;
among that assembly, those who seek the Vehicle of the Śrāvakas, may I cause them to abide in their final existence so that I may deliver them.
For those sentient beings who seek the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, may they all attain the Flower of Manifestation Patience (*vairocana-kusuma-kṣānti*).
For those sentient beings who seek the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, may they all attain the Immovable Samādhi of Holding the Ocean of Vajras; by means of this samādhi, may they ascend to the third stage.

When I wish to bathe, I shall cause that most excellent dragon king to come and bathe me. Furthermore, for any sentient beings who see me bathing, may they all attain such virtues in the three vehicles as previously described.

If there are sentient beings who see me riding in a vehicle, I briefly explain that for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings, I manifest various activities such as those of a youth’s play.

"While in the palace, I played with the court ladies amidst the five desires, yet my mind gave rise to weariness and aversion. In the middle of the night, I departed, casting off my necklaces and ornaments; to subdue the various heterodox teachers—the Nirgranthas, Carakas, Parivrājakas, and Pāṣaṇḍas—I discarded my many-layered robes and sought the dharma-attired garments, proceeding to the Bodhi tree."

If there are sentient beings who see me approaching the Bodhi tree, I shall, by means of the Samādhi of Gathering All Merit, preach such a Dharma for those sentient beings so that they all diligently seek the Three Vehicles.
For those beings who have produced the seed of the śrāvaka, may all their fetters ripen so that they abide in their final body and attain liberation through me.
For those beings who seek the vehicle of the pratyekabuddha, may they all attain the *vimalā-kusuma-kṣānti*.
For those who have planted the seeds of the Mahāyāna, may they all attain the immovable samādhi of the ocean-like Vajradhara; by means of this samādhi, may they ascend to the third bhūmi.
I shall personally take grass and spread it beneath the Bodhi tree to form a vajrāsana; upon that seat, I shall sit cross-legged with body erect and mind upright.

In this manner, I shall enter the immovable dhyāna and cease the inhalation and exhalation of breath; rising from dhyāna once each day, I shall eat half a sesame seed and give the other half away as alms.

For all that time I shall practice such asceticism; now, reaching as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven, throughout the Sahā Buddha-field, may all the devas come to make offerings to me and cause them all to witness my ascetic practices.
For those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the World-Honored One causes all their fetters to be completely extinguished, so that they dwell in their final body and attain liberation through me.
For those who seek the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, it is as previously described.

In this way, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and sages possessing the five supernatural powers—these and others came to make offerings to me, causing them all to witness my ascetic practices.
For those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas, it is as previously described.
Regarding those heterodox practitioners among the four continents who engage in coarse and debased asceticism, devas and non-humans shall proclaim to them:

"Your ascetic practices yield no great fruit and are nothing extraordinary. As for the Bodhisattva in his final existence who dwells in such a place, he practices asceticism by entering this meditative state of equanimity, binding his mental activities, withdrawing from bodily movements, and extinguishing the breath of vocal activity; rising from meditation only once each day to eat half a sesame seed—such is his ascetic practice, and its fruit is truly vast."
"He is vast and expansive; before long, he shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If you do not believe this, you may go and see for yourselves.
Thus, he caused all those who were practicing difficult austerities to abandon them and come in their entirety to see me, the ascetic.
There are those who have planted the seeds of the Śrāvaka vehicle, even as previously described.

If there are kings, ministers, officials, or other commoners among the populace who dwell at home and attend to household affairs, I shall cause them all to come to my presence and witness my ascetic practices;
and those who seek the Śrāvaka vehicle shall be as previously described.
If there are women who come to see me, I shall cause this to be their final female body, so that they will never again receive one;
as for those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas, it is as previously described.
If there are birds or beasts who see me sitting and practicing asceticism, may they never again receive a final animal body;
if there are birds or beasts who have planted the seeds of the Śrāvaka vehicle, may they attain liberation from me after one more lifetime;
and for those who seek the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, it shall be as previously described.
The various animals spoke thus, and the hungry ghosts likewise spoke thus:

"At that time, I shall practice such asceticism; by sitting cross-legged even once, I will cause many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings to witness my asceticism and attain what they have never before experienced."
