Regarding those immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* seeds of liberation that have been planted therein, I shall practice such asceticism that, among the classes of beings—whether they be followers of other paths (*tīrthika*), the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the unsurpassed Mahāyāna—there has never before been anyone capable of practicing such asceticism as I do, nor will there ever be anyone among the classes of beings, from the followers of other paths up to the Mahāyāna, who can practice such asceticism as I do.

Before I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I shall perform the deeds of a great man to subdue the hosts of Māra; having reserved the remaining karmic retribution to shatter the Māra of the fetters (*saṃyojana*), I shall achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Within this assembly, I shall cause one sentient being to attain arhatship; likewise, I shall cause a second to attain arhatship through the teaching of the Dharma; likewise, a third and a fourth shall attain arhatship through the teaching of the Dharma.

"For the sake of these two types of sentient beings, I shall manifest hundreds of thousands of supernatural powers to cause them to abide in right view, and I shall preach many thousands of teachings, complete in both words and meaning, according to the fruits in which they abide."
The mountains of fetters of sentient beings are like adamant; I must shatter them with the vajra-pestle of wisdom and preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.
For the sake of each and every sentient being, I shall travel many hundreds of yojanas at every step to preach the Dharma and establish them on the path of fearlessness.

May there be no obstacles to those who leave the household life in my Dharma; may they not be emaciated, weak, forgetful, deranged, stubborn, arrogant, lacking in wisdom, burdened by many fetters, or have minds disturbed by afflictions and women; and may those who leave the household life in my Dharma be able to receive full ordination.
May I have a fourfold assembly— bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—
and may there be many followers within my Dharma.

"If you cause the devas to see the Truths, and cause the yakṣas, nāgas, and asuras to be endowed with the eight factors of the noble ones, even down to the animals, you would cause them to practice the holy life.
"World-Honored One! [If this were so,]..."

Once I have attained bodhi, if there are sentient beings who harbor ill will or harmful intent toward me—whether with swords, fire, or stones, or with various kinds of weapons—and come before me to revile and insult me with harsh words; or if they slander and spread my evil reputation throughout the ten directions; or if they offer me food and drink mixed with poison—I shall, through such remaining karmic fruits, realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Once I have attained *bodhi*, should there be sentient beings who previously harbored enmity or resentment toward me, who come before me bearing various lethal weapons and instruments, reviling me with harsh words, or offering food and drink mixed with poison, and even drawing blood from my body—I shall, with the Brahma-like, gentle voice of great compassion, sounding like the resonance of bells, drums, and thunder, preach this Dharma to those sentient beings: the precepts, learning, samādhi, and the pure mind. I shall cause those sentient beings to abide in goodness, to repent their evil karma, and to attain the perfection of pure precepts.

"I shall cause those sentient beings to not lose the fruit of liberation, and to be free from the obstacles of desire, the exhaustion of outflows, and karmic retribution; as for me, I shall exhaust all remaining karmic fruits.
"World-Honored One!"

Once I have attained bodhi, I shall manifest as many emanated Buddhas each day as there are pores on my body; all of them shall be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty secondary signs. I shall dispatch those emanated Buddhas to empty Buddha-fields, send others to non-empty places, and likewise dispatch them to Buddha-fields of the five turbidities.
In those various lands, there are sentient beings who commit acts of immediate retribution, slander the true Dharma, revile the worthy and holy ones, and even accumulate roots of unwholesomeness;

among them are those who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas, those who seek the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and those who seek the Great Vehicle. Yet they have flaws in their precepts, lack proper deportment, and commit root transgressions; their minds are withered and parched, they have strayed from the path of goodness, and they fall into the wilderness of saṃsāra. Trapped by false paths and submerged in this wilderness, for each and every one of these transformed Buddhas, he daily teaches the Dharma according to their needs for billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of such sentient beings.

There are sentient beings who serve the deity Maheśvara; to them, I manifest in the form of Maheśvara and preach the Dharma for them, declaring my Sahā Buddha-field and exhorting those beings to dedicate their merit toward their vows.
For all those beings who hear my name, I cause them to aspire to be born in my land.
“World-Honored One!

If, when those beings are about to end their lives, I am not present before them, do not preach the Dharma for them, and do not give rise to wholesome thoughts in them, may I not realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

If, after those beings have ended their lives, they fall into the evil destinies and are not born in my land to receive a human body, may I forget all the True Dharma so that it does not appear before me, and may I be unable to fully accomplish the work of a Buddha.”
If there are sentient beings who serve Nārāyaṇa, even until the end of their lives, should they fall into the evil destinies, I would not fulfill my task of accomplishing the work of a Buddha.

Once I have attained bodhi, may all those in every buddha-field who have committed the acts of immediate retribution, even those who are beset by false paths and fallen into the wilderness, be reborn in my land at the end of their lives; may their physical appearance be like the color of the earth, and their faces like those of piśācas.

Their mindfulness will be forgetful, leading to many lapses; they will be foul-smelling due to broken precepts, frequently ill, short-lived, and lacking in various requisites for offerings. Because the lifespans of those sentient beings are so brief, I shall, for the sake of those beings, descend from the Tuṣita Heaven into the womb of a mother and manifest birth in as many sets of four continents as exist within the Sahā world. To speak briefly, I shall manifest the childhood games, various arts and skills, ascetic practices, the subduing of Māra, the attainment of perfect enlightenment (samyak-saṃbodhi), and the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma across all those four continents. Having fully manifested these Buddha-activities, I shall enter parinirvāṇa and even manifest the distribution of my relics.
“Once I have attained bodhi, I shall preach a single dharma-gate: for those sentient beings who seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas, I shall cause them to understand the teachings of the Śrāvaka-piṭaka;
for those sentient beings who seek the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, I shall cause them to understand the teachings on dependent origination;
and for those sentient beings who seek the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, I shall cause them purely to understand the teachings of the Mahāyāna.”
For those sentient beings who have not yet perfected their merits but desire to seek awakening, he causes them to understand the teaching on the dharma of giving;
for those sentient beings who lack merit and seek the bliss of rebirth in heaven, he causes them to understand the teaching on the precepts;
for those sentient beings whose turbid minds are malicious and who fear one another, he causes them to understand the teaching on the dharma of loving-kindness.
For those who delight in killing, he causes them to attain the teaching of compassion;
for those with stinginess, greed, and envy, he causes them to attain the teaching of wholesome dharmas;
for those who rely on their physical beauty or strength and whose minds are clouded by desire, he causes them to attain the teaching of renunciation.
For those whose minds are attached to sensual desires, he causes them to understand the teaching on the impurity of phenomena;
for those Mahāyāna beings whose minds are distracted by pride, he causes them to understand the teaching on the practice of mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasmṛti);
and for those of little wisdom who seek the light of a lamp, he causes them to understand the teaching on dependent origination (pratītyasamutpāda).
For those who have heard little of the teachings, he provides the discourse on the Dharma of hearing and retaining so that they may attain understanding and not forget;
for those dwelling in the wilderness of false views, he provides the discourse on the Dharma of emptiness so that they may attain understanding;
and for those exhausted by excessive discursive thought, he provides the discourse on the Dharma of non-conceptualization so that they may attain understanding.
For those distressed by impure aspirations, he causes them to attain liberation through the teaching on the dharma of wishlessness;
for those whose body and mind are impure, he causes them to attain liberation through the teaching on the dharma of gentleness of body and mind;
for those distressed by distracted conduct, he causes them to attain liberation through the teaching on the dharma of not forgetting the bodhicitta.
For those who harbor anger and create affliction, he teaches the Dharma for the sake of attaining freedom from resentment;
for those whose minds are afflicted by distress, he teaches the Dharma for the sake of attaining the non-existence of such states;
for those whose hearts are troubled, he teaches the Dharma for the sake of attaining freedom from envy.
To speak briefly: for those who forget the wholesome, it is explained as illumination;
for those who perform the works of Māra, it is explained as purity;
for those who are submerged in heterodox doctrines, it is explained as courageous emergence.
For those whose minds are bound by various fetters, he explains liberation and detachment;
for those who have fallen into deviant paths, he explains the method of returning;
for those with the aspiration for the Mahāyāna, he explains non-retrogression.
For those who weary of birth and death, explain the joy of eloquence of the bodhisattvas;
for those who have not yet attained the wisdom of the wholesome stages, explain the discourse on growth;
for those who do not take delight in roots of goodness, explain the discourse on vexation and regret.
For those with uneven minds, explain the discourse on unimpeded light;
for those who have sunk into evil karma, explain the discourse on deliverance;
for those who fear within the assembly, explain the discourse on the Lion’s Victory.
The four maras that oppress the mind are explained through the discourse on courageous resolve;
those whose minds do not clearly perceive the Buddha-fields are explained through the discourse on the light of adornment;
and those who harbor hatred and attachment are explained through the discourse on liberation via equanimity.
The Buddha-dharma clarifies that for those who lack awakening, the teaching of the "Supreme Banner" (Prathama-ketu) is explained;
for those lacking great wisdom, the teaching of "Radiant Brilliance" (Prabhāsa) is explained;
and for those afflicted by the darkness of folly, the teaching of the "Sun Lamp" (Sūrya-pradīpa) is explained.
One who does not seek inexhaustible words understands the discourse on attainment;
one who seeks me like foam understands the discourse on Nārāyaṇa;
one whose mind is wavering understands the discourse on firm abiding.
Observing the summit is explained as the high banner;
abandoning former vows is explained as firmness;
and retreating from supernormal powers is explained as the adamantine mind.
For those who seek the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), one explains it as the Vajra-site;
for those who wish that all phenomena not be disparaged, one explains it as being like the Vajra;
for those who wish to know the thoughts in the minds of others, one explains it as the sphere of practice (*caryā*).
Those who wish to know the faculties of others should understand the teaching on the path of wisdom;
those whose speech is incoherent should understand the teaching on entering into discourse;
and those who have not yet attained the Dharma-body should understand the teaching on cultivating all bodies.
Those who wish to behold the Tathāgata understand the teaching on the unblinking gaze;
those who possess mindfulness of all creators understand the teaching on non-contention;
those who seek to turn the wheel of Dharma understand the teaching on the stainless wheel.
For those who seek erroneously without cause, explain the teaching on following causes and conditions;
for those who constantly dwell in a single buddha-field, explain the teaching on skillful speech;
for those who have not yet planted the seeds for the marks and signs of excellence, explain the teaching on adornment.
For those unable to discern speech and sounds, he provides explanations through the path of words;
for those seeking all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), he provides explanations on the non-concealment of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);
for those who regress from the Dharma, he provides explanations on steadfastness.
For those who have not yet realized the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), it is explained as universal penetration;
for those who have abandoned their vows, it is explained as non-retrogression;
for those for whom the Way is obscured, it is explained as being without form.
For those seeking wisdom equal to space, he explains the teaching on non-existence;
for those who have not yet fulfilled the perfections, he explains the teaching on pure dwelling;
for those who have not yet perfected the gathering of beings, he explains the teaching on skillful gathering.
For those who have not yet established themselves in the holy life (*brahmacarya*), it is explained as the teaching of equality;
for those who have not yet fulfilled the jewel of the aids to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣa*), it is explained as the teaching of non-abiding practice;
and for those who have lost the mind of wisdom regarding skillful discourse, it is explained as the teaching of the ocean-seal (*sāgaramudrā*).
One who aspires to the mind of the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti) understands the teaching on definitive resolution;
one whose mind widely distributes the Dharma as it has been heard understands the teaching on non-forgetfulness;
and one who mutually and excellently explains [the Dharma] without weariness understands the teaching on being unobstructed.
For those who have not yet attained reverent faith in the Triple Gem, it is explained as the "Accumulation of Merit";
for those who are insatiable regarding the rain of Dharma-gates, it is explained as the "Dharma Cloud";
for those who hold views that sever the Triple Gem, it is explained as the "Jeweled Adornment."
Non-engagement in the karma of wisdom is the explanation of non-arising;
liberation from all bonds of affliction is the explanation of the gate of emptiness;
maintaining a mind of detachment toward all phenomena is the explanation of the seal of wisdom.
For those who have not yet fulfilled the virtues of a Tathāgata, explain the teaching through the gateway of manifesting conventional truth;
for those who have not accumulated merit under previous Buddhas, explain that they must undergo transformation;
and for those who have not yet attained ultimate mindfulness regarding even a single dharma-gate.
He explains the nature of all phenomena to those who do not understand it;
he explains the equality of the reality of phenomena to those who have not yet mastered the various sutras;
and he explains the characteristics of all phenomena to those who have departed from the six dharmas of harmonious respect.
For those who do not contemplate liberation, he teaches through the play of supernormal powers;
for those who wish to enter the secrets of the Tathāgata, he teaches the understanding that seeks nothing from others;
for those who do not diligently cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, he teaches the understanding of attaining wisdom.
"Not manifesting birth" explains the teaching on reaching all places;
"having residual [practice] while performing the bodhisattva deeds" explains the teaching on receiving empowerment;
"the Tathāgata’s ten powers not yet being fulfilled" explains the teaching on the most supreme.
For those who have not yet attained the four fearlessnesses, explain through the discourse on courageous progress;
for those who have not yet attained the unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma), explain through the discourse on the intention of the incalculable (asaṃkhyeya);
for those whose hearing and seeing are not deluded, explain through the discourse on the path of vows.
Those who cannot manifest the awakening to all Buddha-dharmas are explained by the teaching on the pure, stainless seal;
those who possess the wisdom of *sarvajñā* with remainder are explained by the teaching on the well-awakened mind;
and those who have not yet attained the all-encompassing activity of a Tathāgata are explained by the teaching on the dharma of boundless exhaustion.

“There are immeasurable, incalculable bodhisattvas seeking the Great Vehicle who are without guile, without deceit, upright, and honest. May those bodhisattvas, through a single utterance, attain eighty-four thousand dharma-gates, eighty-four thousand samādhis, and seventy-five thousand dhāraṇīs. By these merits, may these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas adorn themselves with great adornments; may they courageously give rise to inconceivable, sublime vows; and may they adorn themselves with the inconceivable merit of knowledge and vision. That is to say:
adorning the body with the primary and secondary marks, and adorning the mouth with skillful speech at will that brings joy to all beings.”
The adornment of the mind through non-retrogression in samādhi; the adornment of mindfulness through maintaining without loss;

the adornment of the intellect through powerful memory; the adornment of arrival through reaching awakening; the adornment of the resolve for meaning through firm vows; the adornment of action through eloquent vows;
the adornment of the ultimate resolve through transcending the stages and what is not the stages; and the adornment of giving through...
They renounce all things; they are adorned with precepts that are pure and stainless;
their minds are adorned with patience toward all sentient beings, free from pride or inferiority; they are adorned with diligence in accomplishing all tasks;
they are adorned with meditative concentration, sporting in all samādhis and supernatural powers; and they are adorned with wisdom in knowing the causes and conditions of the fetters and afflictions.
The adornment of loving-kindness reaches the state of all sentient beings; the adornment of compassion does not abandon any sentient being;
the adornment of sympathetic joy attains freedom from doubt regarding all phenomena; the adornment of equanimity regards praise and blame as non-dual;
the adornment of supernormal powers sports in all supernormal powers; and the adornment of merit attains the "jewel-hand."
The treasury of inexhaustibility, adorned with wisdom, understands the mental activities and thoughts of all sentient beings;
adorned with awakening, it awakens all sentient beings to wholesome dharmas; adorned with clarity, it attains the brilliance of the eye of wisdom;
adorned with eloquence, it attains the analytical powers of meaning, dharma, language, and response; and adorned with valor, it subdues all Māras and...
The adornment of diverse discourses, reaching the unsurpassed virtues of a Buddha through the adornment of virtue;
the adornment of the Dharma, universally preaching the Dharma for all sentient beings through incalculable eloquence; the adornment of clarity, illuminating all Buddha-dharmas;
the adornment of light, illuminating the transformations within all Buddha-fields; and the adornment of exposition, manifesting transformations through infallible predictions.

The adornment of teaching through providing instruction as is appropriate; the adornment of spiritual transformations (*ṛddhi-vikurvaṇa*) through reaching the further shore of all experiences via the four bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*);
the adornment of the Tathāgata through entering the secret Dharma of the Tathāgatas;
the adornment of mastery through wisdom attained not from another and through being respectful and compliant toward all; and the adornment of wholesome qualities (*kuśala-dharma*) through suchness...
I declare that there is none who can cause regression in the practice of all stages.

For the sake of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* beings seeking the Mahāyāna, I purify their many unwholesome states with a single, uniform voice and provide them with fulfillment; thereby, I cause those Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas to attain wisdom regarding all phenomena not through others, to be endowed with the great light of Dharma, and to swiftly achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

Furthermore, there are sentient beings in other worlds who have committed the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*), even those who have violated the root precepts and whose minds are parched with affliction;

yet there are those seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas, those seeking the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and those seeking the unsurpassed Great Vehicle who, by virtue of their vows, are born in my buddha-field, though they have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, are coarse and cruel, delight in evil, are stubborn and hold perverted views, and lack self-restraint.”
For those eighty-four thousand sentient beings whose mental activities and intentions are distracted, I shall extensively expound eighty-four thousand sections of the Dharma.

Among them, for those who seek the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, I shall extensively expound the Dharma of the six pāramitās—extensively expounding the dānapāramitā, and so on, up to extensively expounding the prajñāpāramitā.

Among them, for those who seek the vehicles of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, or those who have not yet planted roots of goodness but seek deliverance from the world, I shall cause them to abide in the three refuges, and subsequently cause them to abide in the pāramitās.

I shall cause those who delight in killing to abide in non-killing; those who are greedy to abide in non-stealing; those who are stained by attachment to what is contrary to the Dharma to abide in non-sexual misconduct; those who speak falsehoods to abide in non-lying; and those who take pleasure in turbidity to abide in non-drinking of intoxicants. For any sentient beings who possess these five ailments, I shall cause them to sever these five afflictions and abide in the Upāsaka precepts.
For those sentient beings who do not delight in wholesome dharmas, I shall cause them to abide for one day and one night in the noble eightfold precepts.
For those who possess even a slight inclination toward roots of goodness, I shall cause them to come near my Dharma, to go forth under the ten precepts, and to abide in the holy life.
For those sentient beings who delight in seeking the wholesome Dharma, I shall cause them to receive full ordination within the wholesome Dharma and abide completely in the holy life (*brahmacarya*).

For the sake of such beings—even those who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*) or those who do not restrain their will—I shall employ various, manifold, and diverse phrases, meanings, and syllables through transformations to preach the Dharma for them. I shall manifest the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense bases (*āyatana*), as well as impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, causing them to dwell in the city of sublime tranquility, fearlessness, and perfect security.
"I shall preach such a Dharma for the fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās:
for those who delight in discursive debate, I shall manifest various methods of debate for them; even for those seeking liberation, I shall manifest the discourse on emptiness for them;
and for those who do not delight in wholesome dharmas, I shall preach and exhort them toward their practice."
"Regarding joy, I shall preach and recite for them the single-minded dhyāna, emptiness, and liberation.

For the sake of each and every sentient being, I shall traverse many hundreds of thousands of yojanas through various and manifold skillful means of phrases, meanings, and characters; enduring such weariness, I shall ultimately establish them in nirvāṇa;
even by the power of my vow, I shall reduce my lifespan by one-fifth."
When I am about to enter parinirvāṇa, for the sake of compassion for sentient beings, I shall shatter my body into relics as small as half a mustard seed before entering nirvāṇa;
may the True Dharma remain in the world for a thousand years after my nirvāṇa, and the Semblance Dharma remain for another five hundred years.

Chapter Seventeen: The Manifestation of Miracles through the Relics and the Establishment of Vows “After my parinirvāṇa, should there be any sentient beings who make offerings of various precious objects to my relics—even those who utter ‘Namo Buddha’ but once, or perform a single prostration, a single circumambulation, a single act of joining their palms, or offer a single flower—may they all, in accordance with the Three Vehicles, attain the stage of non-retrogression.”

After my parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings who, within my Dharma, can receive even a single precept and uphold it as taught, or even recite a single four-line verse for others; and if those who hear it can give rise to a virtuous mind and make offerings to the Dharma-preacher—even by offering a single flower or performing a single prostration—may they all, following the three vehicles, attain non-retrogression until the end of the True Dharma.

When the lamp of the Dharma is forever extinguished and the banner of the Dharma has fallen, may my relics remain upon the golden wheel beneath the earth. For as long as the Sahā world is impoverished of precious treasures, may they become lapis lazuli beads appearing with the color of fire, named "Supreme Intention."
He caused them to abide from that height up to the limit of the Akaniṣṭha heaven, raining down various kinds of flowers:

*māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *pāriyātraka* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers, *rocamāna* flowers, *tārā* flowers, *mahātārā* flowers, *vimalacakra* flowers, hundred-petaled flowers, thousand-petaled flowers, hundred-thousand-petaled flowers, *samantaprabha* flowers, *samantagandha* flowers, *sukhara* flowers, *sattva* flowers, *rocanaka* flowers, *sukhamayūkhacandra* flowers, *candraprabha* flowers, *anekavarṇa* flowers, *anekagandha* flowers, and *anekaprabha* flowers; he caused such a great rain of flowers to fall.
Causing those various flowers to produce all kinds of soft sounds, namely:

The sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṃgha, the sound of the three refuges, the sound of the lay precepts (upāsaka-śīla), the sound of the noble eightfold precepts, the sound of the ten precepts for renunciation, the sound of giving, the sound of morality, the sound of the complete holy life, the sound of exhortation, the sound of recitation, the sound of study, the sound of meditative concentration and contemplation on the nine stages of visualization, the sound of impurity, the sound of mindfulness of breathing (ānāpāna-smṛti), the sound of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the sound of the sphere of nothingness, the sound of the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sound of the sphere of infinite space, the sound of the spheres of mastery (abhibhvāyatana), the sound of the spheres of totality (kṛtsnāyatana), the sound of tranquility and insight (śamatha-vipaśyanā), the sound of emptiness and signlessness, and the sound of dependent origination—these cause the emergence of the complete treasury of the Śrāvaka-piṭaka, cause the emergence of the complete treasury of the Pratyekabuddha-yāna, and fully explain the six pāramitās of the Mahāyāna.

He caused those flowers to produce such sounds that the devas of the form realm (rūpadhātu), upon hearing them, each recalled the roots of goodness they had previously cultivated, so that they would not disparage the Mahāsattva regarding any wholesome dharmas; he caused them to descend from there to teach the ten wholesome karmic paths to all people in the Sahā world, establishing them therein;
and he caused the devas of the desire realm (kāmadhātu) to hear this in the same way.
He causes all of them to abandon their attachment to the pleasures of sensory play;
he causes all of them to individually recollect the roots of goodness they previously cultivated;
and he causes them to descend from the heavens to preach the ten wholesome karmas to all people in the Sahā world, exhorting them to abide therein.
He caused those flowers in the midst of the sky to transform into various jewels,
O World-Honored One!
That is to say:
May gold, silver, mani-jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, musaragalva, agate, as well as conch shells, coral, amber, and right-spiraling rose-pearls rain down upon all the Sahā Buddha-fields;

may anger, strife, litigation, famine, and pestilence in the Sahā Buddha-field be extinguished; may hostile armies, evil winds, and all manner of poisons be entirely eliminated; may [the beings there] be peaceful, healthy, and free from all fighting, litigation, and imprisonment, so that the entire Sahā Buddha-field is prosperous and joyful;

and for those sentient beings who see these jewels, touch them, or use them to create offerings, may they all attain non-retrogression in the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, reaching at the very least the station of the Golden Wheel.
“World-Honored One!

During such an age of the sword-weapon kalpa, may these śarīras further transform into indranīla-rāja maṇi jewels and abide as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven, raining down various kinds of flowers, namely:
māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, pārijātaka flowers, and even up to the flowers of immeasurable light;”
He causes those various flowers to produce all kinds of wondrous sounds, namely:
the sound of the Buddha, and so forth, as previously described;
he causes those relics to abide upon the golden wheel and so on.
Thus, during the kalpa of famine, he further causes the śarīra to ascend into the void and abide as far as the limit of Akaniṣṭha, raining down great flowers as previously described.
Likewise, during the kalpa of pestilence, it shall be as previously described.

Just as within this Bhadrakalpa, after my parinirvāṇa, my relics shall perform the work of a Buddha, exhorting and transforming countless sentient beings so that they abide in the three vehicles and reach the stage of non-retrogression;

even so, throughout great kalpas as numerous as the atoms in five buddha-fields, my relics shall transform sentient beings so that they abide in the three vehicles and reach the stage of non-retrogression.

After the passing of more than a thousand *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who have appeared in the immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* worlds throughout the ten directions, were all those whom I, while practicing the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* as a bodhisattva, first exhorted and transformed; they are those whom I established in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and they are also those whom I exhorted to abide therein through the *pāramitās*. Furthermore, they are those whom I, having attained *bodhi*, exhorted and transformed, establishing sentient beings in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and causing them to abide therein.

Furthermore, after my parinirvāṇa, those sentient beings who, through the miraculous transformations of my relics, give rise to the mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they too—after a period exceeding a thousand *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—will cause those bodhisattvas in immeasurable other worlds throughout the ten directions to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Having done so, they will praise and extol me by saying:
"In the distant past, there was an eon named Bhadra; in that Bhadra Eon, the fourth holy one at its beginning was named thus."

He previously exhorted and transformed us toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and by means of our parched minds, we accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, committed deeds of immediate retribution, and even held wrong views; yet he enabled us to abide in the six *pāramitās*.

It is because of this that we have been enabled to enter into all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), to turn the true wheel of Dharma and the most profound, wondrous wheel, and to cause many hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of sentient beings to be born in heaven and abide in the fruit of liberation.
"Should there be any sentient beings seeking awakening who hear this praise of me from that Tathāgata, they should cause them to ask that Tathāgata thus:
'Venerable One!'"
World-Honored One!
For what purpose and for what meaning did that Tathāgata attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in that world of the five turbidities with its heavy fetters?

He caused those Tathāgatas to speak for the sake of sons and daughters of good family seeking awakening, saying: "I am one endowed with great compassion; this is my original vow concerning the adornment of the buddha-field at the time of my first production of the thought of awakening."

May those sons and daughters of good family who seek awakening attain unprecedented faith and joy in the Great Dharma; may they likewise give rise to such great compassion toward all sentient beings and establish such vows to gather and deliver those in the five turbidities of this evil world with heavy fetters, even those who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution or accumulated roots of unwholesomeness.

May those Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, likewise bestow upon those sons and daughters of good family who possess great compassion and seek awakening this prediction; and may they, according to the wishes of those sons and daughters of good family, again form vows for the five turbidities of this evil world.

Furthermore, other Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will extensively expound this past history for sons and daughters of good family who seek bodhi, using my relics and their miraculous transformations as the basis:

"In the distant past, there was a Holy Sun named such-and-such; after his parinirvāṇa, his relics manifested various and manifold miraculous transformations for sentient beings who were so afflicted by suffering during that time."

By means of that miraculous manifestation of the śarīra, we first awakened to anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, accumulated all roots of goodness, and extensively cultivated the pāramitās, even as previously described.
Chapter 18: The Chapter on Praise The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Chapter Eighteen: The Chapter on Praise “Good son!

At that time, the National Preceptor, the Brahmin Sāgaradatta, stood before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and before the gandharvas and the people of the world, and having established these five hundred vows endowed with great compassion, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”

If my intention were not thus fulfilled, then in a future age—the five turbidities of the Bhadrakalpa, a world of heavy fetters and distraction, a dark time when beings are blind, lacking a teacher or guide, trapped by false views, dwelling long in darkness, and committing acts of immediate retribution—I would remain as previously described.
If I am unable to fully accomplish such Buddha-works as I have vowed, I shall renounce my vow for enlightenment; I shall not dedicate my roots of goodness toward other buddha-fields.
"Bhagavān! This is what I desire:

I do not wish to dedicate these roots of goodness toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, nor do I seek the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*, nor do I seek the vehicle of the *śrāvaka*. I do not seek the rank of a human king or a heavenly king, nor do I seek the pleasures of rebirth in heaven through the five desires or their requisites. Furthermore, I do not seek birth among the *gandharvas*, *asuras*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *nāgas*, or *garuḍas*, nor do I seek birth among humans. I do not dedicate my roots of goodness to any such states."

Although the World-Honored One has taught that giving results in great wealth, upholding the precepts leads to rebirth in heaven, and that extensive learning, great wisdom, and spiritual cultivation are not different [in their merit],
the World-Honored One has further stated that when merit and roots of goodness are dedicated according to one's wish, all things are as declared.
"Bhagavān!

Whatever merit I have acquired through giving, ethical discipline, learning, and cultivation—if, despite my establishing such a vow, my wish should not be fulfilled, I dedicate all these roots of goodness to the sentient beings in the hells.

May those sentient beings who are undergoing various forms of intense suffering in the Avīci Hell be liberated by these roots of goodness; may they be born as humans in this Buddha-field, encounter the Dharma of the Tathāgata, attain arhatship, and enter nirvāṇa."

If the karmic fruits of those sentient beings are not yet exhausted, may I now, at the end of my life, be reborn in the Avīci Great Hell; may a single body of mine be divided into as many bodies as there are atoms in a Buddha-field; may each of these individual bodies be as vast as Sumeru, the King of Mountains; and may each of these bodies experience such agonizing pain as that which my own single body currently experiences.

May I personally undergo the agonizing sufferings of hells as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field for each and every lifetime; furthermore, may all sentient beings in other worlds throughout the ten directions—as numerous as the atoms in a present buddha-field—who have committed acts of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*) up to those who have committed deeds leading to the Avīci hell; and moreover, even those who, throughout future eons as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, commit acts of immediate retribution in other buddha-fields of the ten directions as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, or in this very buddha-field—for the sake of all such sentient beings, I shall dwell in the Avīci hell to undergo their karmic retributions, so that those beings shall not fall into hell, shall be forever parted from suffering, shall encounter the various Buddhas, and shall attain liberation from birth and death to enter the city of Nirvāṇa.

I shall dwell for that long duration in the Avīci Hell to deliver sentient beings; even so, throughout as many other Buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, for those sentient beings who have committed such karma and should be born in the Scorching and Roasting Hells, it shall be as previously described.
In this way, there are various [hells] such as Saṃjīva, Kālasūtra, Saṃghāta, Raurava, Mahāraurava, Asipatravana, and Pratāpana;
such is said regarding the realm of animals,
and the same is said regarding the realm of hungry ghosts.
The yakṣas among those who are impoverished also speak thus;
likewise, the kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, asuras, and garuḍas also speak thus.

In other worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, sentient beings create such karma that they should be born among humans as deaf, blind, mute, crippled, afflicted by a hundred ailments, lacking hands or feet, with distracted minds, or destined to consume impurities—briefly described as previously stated.

I shall again be reborn in the Avīci Great Hell, and for as long as it takes for sentient beings to undergo the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases within the cycle of birth and death, for that same duration, I shall endure for a vast period such various sufferings of hells, animals, hungry ghosts, yakṣas, asuras, rākṣasas, and even humans; I shall undergo all these sufferings just as previously described.

If my aspiration for this *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* were not fulfilled, or even if it were fulfilled as described above, may all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in and preaching the Dharma in the immeasurable, incalculable worlds throughout the ten directions, bear witness to this matter of mine.

I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; that among the people of the world during the one hundred and twenty-year lifespan of that Bhadrakalpa, I shall become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, up to Buddha, World-Honored One, and be able to accomplish such Buddha-work as I have established in my vow.

“At that time, the entire great assembly—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and all worldly people, both those in the air and those dwelling on the ground—with the sole exception of the Tathāgata, all shed tears. Having attained great compassion and profound, wondrous mindfulness toward sentient beings, you have given rise to deep great compassion and established profound, great vows; just as you have established these vows, you cover all sentient beings with your sincere mind and great compassion, and are further able to gather and deliver even those who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution or accumulated roots of unwholesomeness.

By virtue of this vow, I know that you, O Benevolent One, have first resolved your mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. "In brief, at that time the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara praised him with these verses:

The Bodhisattva Vajramativikiraṇaprabha praised him in verse, saying:

The Bodhisattva Ākāśapradīpa praised him with these verses:

Samantabhadra Bodhisattva praised him with these verses:

The Bodhisattva Akṣobhya praised him with these verses:

The Bodhisattva Gandhahasta praised him with a verse:

The Bodhisattva Ratnakūṭa praised him with a verse:

The Bodhisattva Fearless praised him with these verses:
“O Benevolent One, you behold sentient beings suffering in the three realms of the future;

The Bodhisattva Puṣpahasta praised him in verse:
“Compassionate, wise, and diligent, you are the foremost among this assembly;

The Bodhisattva Jñānakīrti praised him with a verse:

The Bodhisattva Dharanimudrā praised him in verse:
"Our progress was not firm, yet we were able to liberate ourselves from the turbid fetters;

The Bodhisattva Flower-Moon praised him with a verse, saying:
“With the power of diligence firm and steadfast, And a mind of virtue and compassion;
Your fame pervades the three realms— You shall surely sever the bonds of birth and death.”
The Bodhisattva Vimalarāja praised him in verse:
“You have now spoken of great compassion, Manifesting the conduct of a bodhisattva;
We now pay homage to you, O peerless one in compassionate pity.”
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta praised him in verse:
“In this degenerate age of afflictions and maladies, you, O Benevolent One, cultivate the practices of bodhi;
you shall sever the roots of all fetters, for your vow is most firm and steadfast.”
The Bodhisattva Candracūḍa praised him with these verses:
“O Treasury of Wisdom, equal toward praise and blame, You establish vows that are pure and stainless;
Practicing the conduct of enlightenment, You are the excellent medicine for all sentient beings.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pratyutpannabala wept and shed tears; having prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the brāhmaṇa and joined his palms in reverence, he praised him in verse:
"How wonderful! O Sage of Luminous Wisdom, You have removed the filth of all fetters and afflictions;

At that time, the Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū Tathāgata, the Gandharvas, and the people of the world prostrated themselves with their five limbs at the feet of the Brahmin. With palms joined, they offered various verses of praise for his manifold meanings and principles."
"Good son!

“By what cause and by what condition does the great earth tremble and a rain of celestial flowers fall?

At that time, to the east, beyond as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there was a world named Ratnasaṃcaya. There dwelt a Buddha named Ratnacandra Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and so forth, up to Buddha, World-Honored One, who currently resides in the world, surrounded by an assembly of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas, expounding the Dharma and teaching exclusively the Mahāyāna.
