In the space of a single thought-moment, they arrived here at the Jambūvana Grove in this Ketumatī Buddha-field and approached the presence of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha."

“At that time, the entire buddha-field of Sarvanetṛla will be filled with such Mahāyāna bodhisattvas, as well as sons of good family who seek the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas and the vehicle of the śrāvakas, and [beings] from the devas down to the mahoragas; it will be filled and matured just like a field of sugarcane, bamboo, reeds, rice, hemp, or a thicket of forest.”

At that time, this buddha-field of Nairañjanā was filled with sons of good family who had set out in the Mahāyāna, up to and including mahoragas; those bodhisattvas prostrated with their heads at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and, having made various offerings through the power of their vows and their bodhisattva supernormal powers, [departed].
Those bodhisattvas also saw, before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, a brahmin and the entire great assembly standing with palms joined, extolling and praising him.
Those bodhisattvas gave rise to this thought:
"This is that Great Being of Great Compassion, whom the Tathāgata Padmavikrāntaprabhāsa bestowed upon as the Moon-Bliss-Stainless Flower."
Those bodhisattvas, having received them from the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, turned them over to the brahmin, gave him the wish-fulfilling stainless flowers, and spoke these words: "O noble son!
The Tathāgata Puṣpavikāsapradyota has given this wish-fulfilling, stainless flower of joy as a token of faith for you.
O noble son! You are excellent, even as previously described, through the three excellences.
"Furthermore, rains of various flowers fell upon the empty buddha-fields, and manifold excellent sounds filled those empty buddha-lands.
Namely:

the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṃgha, the sound of cessation, the sound of the unconditioned, the sound of the perfections, the sound of the faculties and powers, the sound of the fearlessnesses, the sound of the superknowledges, the sound of non-action, the sound of non-arising, the sound of non-extinction, the sound of tranquility, the sound of detachment, the sound of great loving-kindness, the sound of great compassion, the sound of the non-arising of dharmas, the sound of the conferral of office, the sound of ascending the stages, and the sound of the exclusive teaching of the Mahāyāna."
That rain of various flowers, accompanied by these sublime sounds, pervaded all those empty buddha-fields.

Furthermore, within those empty buddha-fields, there were bodhisattvas who possessed great supernatural powers and majesty, who had attained mastery over the profound Dharma, and who dwelt therein for the sake of delivering sentient beings according to their original vows. Having heard these sounds, and sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, they took their original vows as a force of resolve; they then manifested supernatural powers and traveled with such speed that it was like a strong man extending his arm. In this manner, those bodhisattvas departed from their empty buddha-fields and arrived here in this Sahā buddha-field.

Having made offerings to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and to that entire assembly by means of various bodhisattva supernormal powers, those bodhisattvas sat down wherever they found space to listen to the Dharma.
Chapter Twenty: The Prophecy of the Great Teacher *Mahākaruṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra* "Good son!
At that time, the brahmin Sāgaradatta, the national teacher, having made an offering of those *vimala-prārthanā* flowers to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, addressed the Buddha, saying:
'I pray only that the World-Honored One will grant me the prophecy of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.'"

"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha immediately entered a samādhi called 'Lightning Lamp. By means of this samādhi, he caused the entire buddha-field of Nairañjanā to be transformed into the seven treasures."

All mountains, forests, trees, rubble, and the earth were entirely manifested as the seven treasures; according to the wholesome reflections that assisted those sentient beings, he manifested his body in response for those who sat listening to the Dharma.

Among them, some manifested bodies that were blue, some yellow, some green, some purple, some red, some black, and some white; some manifested bodies like the wind, some like fire, some like space, some like a mirage, some like ice, some like foam, some like mountains, some like Brahmā, some like Śakra, some like flowers, some like garuḍas, some like nāgas, some like lions, some like the sun, some like the moon, and some like stars; some manifested their own bodies as skeletons. According to the wholesome reflections they had cultivated to assist others, those who sat listening to the Dharma saw themselves in such a manner.
"Good son!
Just as the sentient beings therein see their own bodies, so too do they see the body of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
Good son!"
At that time, the great assembly saw the brahmin, the national preceptor, seated upon a seven-jeweled thousand-petaled lotus pedestal before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
O son of good family!

Among those sentient beings, whether they were sitting on the ground, on mountains, or in the air, each and every one of them saw the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha sitting before them, gazing at them with his whole heart and preaching the Dharma for their sake.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha praised the brahmin Sāgaramegha, saying:
‘Excellent, excellent!’”

O Greatly Compassionate Great Brahmin, you too have appeared as a Brahmin out of great compassion for the sake of benefiting and illuminating countless sentient beings in the world. It is like a magnificent flower-land, with its various colors, various fragrances, various textures, various leaves, various stalks, various roots, and various virtues—all of which are excellent medicines.

Among them, there were flowers whose fragrance and color illuminated a hundred yojanas, two hundred yojanas, and three hundred yojanas; in brief, there were flowers whose fragrance and color even illuminated worlds as vast as the four continents.

Among those sentient beings, upon smelling the fragrance of that flower, the blind regained their sight and the deaf regained their hearing; even those with impaired faculties all attained full perfection.
If there are sentient beings afflicted by the four hundred and four diseases, their physical ailments are immediately cured upon smelling the fragrance.
Among those sentient beings, any who are insane, deranged, or have lost their senses regain their original minds upon smelling the scent of the flowers.

Within this flower world-system, a single *puṇḍarīka* emerges, made of solid diamond with a stem of lapis lazuli that has a hundred curves; its leaves are of gold, its filaments of agate, and its pedestal of red pearls. It is eighty-four hundred thousand *yojanas* in height, and exactly one hundred thousand *yojanas* in length and breadth. The fragrance, color, and light of this *puṇḍarīka* shine through and illuminate worlds as numerous as the atoms within the Buddha-fields of the ten directions.
"O Brahmin!

Among the sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the atoms within the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, those who are afflicted by physical illnesses due to the disharmony of the four great elements, or whose faculties are incomplete, who are crazed, deranged, confused, or have lost their minds—when those sentient beings see the light of the Pundarīka and smell its fragrance, all their ailments are eliminated and they recover their original minds."

If there are sentient beings whose bones and joints have not yet separated after they have been dead for a long time, when the light of the Puṇḍarīka illuminates those skeletal remains and its fragrant power touches them, those bones immediately come back to life; they are restored and rise up again, see their relatives, and together with them enter gardens to play, delighting themselves with the five desires as they gather and dwell therein. When their lives there end, they are all reborn in the Brahma realm, where they dwell for a long time with immeasurable lifespans; when their lives there end, they are never born in any other place.
"O Brahmin!

Just as in that Flower-Formed Land (Puṣpākara-kṣetra), this great assembly is like the sun first rising; the various flowers bloom and their fragrance and color manifest, reaching heights of a hundred yojanas, even up to a thousand yojanas, to eliminate the manifold diseases of many sentient beings."
Thus it is, O virtuous man!

I have appeared in the world as the Tathāgata, the Sun of Wisdom. Just as when the sun rises its light illuminates all the flowers, causing them to fully bloom with radiant and pure colors, so too does it eliminate the various ailments and afflictions of sentient beings.
"O virtuous man!

My appearance in the world is likewise thus: with the light of compassion, I pervade all sentient beings, awakening the roots of goodness they previously cultivated, and establishing them upon three kinds of stages. You, too, shall exhort and transform immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings, causing them to abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and lead them to my presence."

All those sentient beings each made vows before me to take up a buddha-field according to their preference; some took up pure lands and some took up impure ones, and I likewise bestowed upon them their respective predictions of enlightenment.
"O virtuous man!

There are bodhisattvas among those in my presence who, having taken up pure buddha-fields and having matured sentient beings whose minds are pure and easy to transform and who have already planted roots of goodness, gather them in and deliver them. This is called the conduct of a bodhisattva mahāsattva; it is not the conduct of a Great Man, nor is there great compassion within their minds."
Those bodhisattvas do not seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi for the sake of pitying all sentient beings; rather, they take up a pure buddha-field and abandon all states of distress.

There are bodhisattvas who seek buddha-fields where there are sentient beings who pursue the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; those bodhisattvas lack wholesome wisdom in their intent and make such a vow as this: "May we attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a buddha-field that is without śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, without the accumulation of unwholesome roots, without women, and without the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts."
For the sake of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, he speaks exclusively the Mahāyāna Dharma for the bodhisattvas seeking the Great Vehicle.

Having attained my awakening, I shall obtain a long life and abide for many kalpas, preaching the Dharma for the multitudes of those with pure intentions who are easily transformed and possess wholesome roots.
"Therefore, those bodhisattvas lack the wholesome wisdom of intent; for this reason, they are not called Mahāsattvas. "Good son!

At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha extended his arm, and from the tips of his five fingers issued various immeasurable colors and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of colored rays of light. Those lights illuminated immeasurable asaṃkhyeya Buddha-lands in the eastern direction."

In that realm there is a world named Aṅguli-māla; in that world, the human lifespan is thirty years, their complexions are ugly and foul, they lack shame and dread of blame, they accumulate roots of unwholesomeness, and their height is three cubits.
In that world, there is a Buddha named Candraprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells in the world, preaching the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to the fourfold assembly.
“Good son! This great assembly beholds that Buddha-land, the Tathāgata, and all its sentient beings. The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha then addressed the great assembly, saying:
‘In the past, immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas ago, that Tathāgata Candraprabha first resolved his mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the presence of the Tathāgata Ratnacchatrābhyudgata.’”
He also exhorted and transformed many billions of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Following those sentient beings, they made vows before the Tathāgata Ratnacchattra-avabhāsa-pramuñcana to take up the adornments of Buddha-lands; some took up pure lands, while others took up impure lands of the five turbidities.

Among them, that Mahāsattva first exhorted me toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. In the presence of that Tathāgata Ratnacchatravikurvita, I established the vow for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and took up the adornment of this Buddha-field of the five corruptions.
At that time, that Tathāgata praised me, saying, "Excellent! and bestowed upon me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O virtuous man!

At that time, the spiritual friend who exhorted me toward Bodhi made this vow for himself: to take up those sentient beings who have formed extremely heavy fetters, who dwell in the evil lands of the five turbidities, who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution, and even those who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, whose minds are withered and parched, and who have fallen into the wilderness of saṃsāra; he vowed to take them and deliver them.

At that time, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the world throughout the immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds of the ten directions, sent messengers to him and likewise expressed their approval, bestowing upon him the name "Excellent Great Compassionate Illumination."
That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇāpradīpa is my spiritual friend who has benefited me.
Not long after attaining Buddhahood, he is now turning the wheel of the true Dharma among people thirty years of age in the world-system of Aṅguli-māla.

Once he has also attained enlightenment, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones currently dwelling in the worlds of the ten directions—immeasurable and incalculable in number—will dispatch messengers to make offerings to him;

these are those whom he first exhorted toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established therein, and those whom he first exhorted toward the *dāna-pāramitā* up to the *prajñā-pāramitā* and established therein.
Those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, mindful of his prior kindness, send envoys to that Tathāgata.

“Brahmin! Observe those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who perform the work of a Buddha among sentient beings who possess long lifespans, pure intentions, and are easily transformed within their buddha-fields.”

That Tathāgata Candraprabha attained buddhahood in such a land of the five corruptions; for the sake of sentient beings who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution and even those who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, he performed the most extensive Buddha-work within such a short lifespan. He did not abandon the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, but taught the Dharma to them in this manner.
"O virtuous man!

Among this entire assembly of bodhisattvas, none can equal you; your aspiration is most sublime, for you have resolved to take birth in the five turbid and evil realms, even to create the karma of immediate retribution and gather up those who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, in order to deliver them."

Furthermore, those bodhisattvas who take up pure buddha-fields—excluding the realms of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts; abandoning śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; and taking in only those whose minds are purified, who are easy to transform, and who have already planted roots of goodness—these bodhisattvas are called "like flowers. They are not mahāsattvas, nor are they *puṇḍarīkas*; they perform the work of a Buddha among those who are easily transformed and whose roots of goodness are matured.
“Brahmin! There are four kinds of indolence for a bodhisattva.
What are the four?
First, to establish the vow to dwell in a pure buddha-field;
second, to vow to perform buddha-work among sentient beings with purified minds;
third, to vow that once one has attained bodhi, one shall not preach the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Fourth, they vow that after attaining bodhi, they shall live for a long time as Buddhas.
These are the four grounds of indolence for bodhisattvas.
Therefore, those bodhisattvas are called "like flowers," but they are not *puṇḍarīkas*, nor are they mahāsattvas.
"Brahmin! This assembly of great bodhisattvas is comparable to this:
apart from those who, by means of Vaiśravaṇa, take up impure buddha-fields and gather and deliver sentient beings with turbulent afflictions, there are likewise few others within the Bhadrakalpa."
"Good son!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have four kinds of diligence.
What are the four?
First, the vow to purify impure buddha-fields;
second, the vow to perform buddha-work among sentient beings with impure intentions;
third, the vow that after attaining bodhi, one shall preach the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Fourth, having attained bodhi, he vows that his lifespan shall be moderate, neither too long nor too short.
These are the four kinds of vigor of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
For this reason, those bodhisattvas are like the *puṇḍarīka* and not like ordinary flowers; therefore, they are called bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

"Brahmin! Just as today, amidst an immeasurable and incalculable assembly of bodhisattvas, you have been well-granted the prediction of a buddha-field; and before the Tathāgata, you have emerged like a white lotus of great compassion. By means of your sublime vows, you have taken up the burden of a buddha-field of the five turbidities, even one that gathers those who have committed the karma of the immediate retribution and those who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness."
"O virtuous man!

Because of your voice of great compassion, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the atoms in the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, have sent messengers to praise you, saying 'Excellent!', bestowing upon you the name 'Great Compassion', and furthermore, this entire assembly has made offerings to you."
O Great Compassionate One!

In a future age, after the passing of one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and when slightly less than two *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas have elapsed, in that Sahā Buddha-field, during the Great Kalpa of the Wise (*Bhadra-kalpa*), amidst a world of human beings who live for one hundred and twenty years and are oppressed by old age and sickness, blinded by darkness—where there is no Teacher in the world, where people accumulate roots of unwholesomeness through false paths, where sentient beings in the wilderness commit acts of immediate retribution (*ānantarya-karma*), and where they slander the noble ones, revile the True Dharma, and fall into root transgressions—even unto the extent previously described, such conditions shall fill the world.

You have become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, up to a Buddha, a World-Honored One; you have turned the wheel of the true Dharma, subdued the sovereign Māra, and conquered the Māras of the fetters, so that your fame spreads throughout the infinite and boundless Buddha-fields of the ten directions.

"You shall have a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty śrāvakas; for forty-five years, you shall gradually fulfill the work of a Buddha in accordance with the vows you have established."
At that time, this Great King Immeasurable Purity shall be named Amitābha, and throughout immeasurable kalpas he will fully perform the work of a Buddha.
Thus it is, O Great Compassionate One!

In the Sahā buddha-field, during the Great Kalpa of the Worthy One among human beings with a lifespan of one hundred and twenty years, he thus fully accomplished the great work of a Buddha for forty-five years.
O virtuous man!
After my unsurpassed parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for more than a thousand years; O virtuous man! after the extinction of the True Dharma...
"Your physical relics shall likewise perform the work of a Buddha as you have vowed; for that duration of time, they shall transform and deliver sentient beings as previously described.

Chapter 21: The Great Master’s Vow The Lotus of Compassion Mahāyāna Sūtra, Chapter Twenty-one: The Great Master’s Vow "Good son, at that time there was a Brahmā named Śaṅkhajaṭa who said: 'O virtuous man!'"

While practicing the bodhisattva path throughout immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, in every place where I am born, I shall always serve as your attendant, following and honoring you like a servant; in my final birth, I vow to become your father.
"O virtuous man!
Once you have attained bodhi, you shall be my foremost donor; you should then grant me the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, there was a female sea deity named Samantamati who said:
"In every place where you are born, until your final body, I shall be your mother and give birth to you."
"O Great Compassionate One!
Once you have attained bodhi, please also grant me the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, there was a female earth-deity named Jālinī who said:
"In every place where I am born, until my final body, may I be your mother; and once you have attained bodhi, may you grant me the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, there were two Śākyas: one named Upatiṣya and the other named Kolita. Both of them said:
"O Great Compassionate One!
In whatever place you are born, and until you have attained bodhi, we shall be your foremost śrāvakas in supernatural powers and wisdom."
There was another Śākya named Sudattahasta, who said:
"O Great Compassionate One!
In whatever place I am born, until my final body, may I be your son."
At that time, there was a mountain goddess named Ruci who said:
"O Great Compassionate One!
From your current birth until your final body, I shall be your wife."
"O virtuous man!
Once you have attained bodhi, please bestow upon me the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, there was an asura named Kūṇika who said:
“O Mahākāruṇika!
In whatever place you are born, throughout immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, O virtuous man!
While you practice the bodhisattva path, I shall act as your kinsman, good friend, and servant; in your final existence, I shall provide for you.”
"O virtuous man!

Once you have attained enlightenment and turned the wheel of the True Dharma, may I be the first to realize the fruit at the time of your initial teaching of the Dharma; may I partake of the flavor of the Dharma and obtain the nectar of immortality, until all fetters and defilements are eliminated and I become an Arhat."
"In brief, at that time, gods, nāgas, asuras, and worldlings, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, followed his great compassion and established vows to receive deliverance.
"At that time, there was one of wrong livelihood named Khaṇḍaka who said:
'O Great Brāhmaṇa!'"

I shall act as your friend to assist you in accomplishing all your affairs; throughout immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas in whatever place I may be born, I shall serve as your fellow teacher and friend, and act as your kinsman. Furthermore, I shall constantly go to your side to beg for clothing, bedding, elephants, horses, chariots, carriages, palanquins, villages, cities, sons, daughters, wives, concubines, and all your retinues; and I shall seek out even your skin, flesh, bones, blood, hands, feet, ears, eyes, nose, tongue, and head.
"Great Brahmin! I am your friend;
I shall assist you in accomplishing the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), and even assist you in accomplishing the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Great Brahmin!"

"When you practice the bodhisattva path, I shall assist you in this way to fulfill the six pāramitās, until you attain awakening, so that I may obtain the status of a śrāvaka, uphold eighty thousand dharma sections, and truly become a Dharma teacher; you should then bestow upon me the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

"Good son! Having heard those words, the Great Compassionate Brahmin prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and said to that heretic of false livelihood who harbored thoughts of ruin:
'Excellent, excellent!'
"O virtuous man!

You are my supreme companion in practice. Since you are able to beg from me for clothing, down to my head and eyes, on behalf of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of asankhyeyas of sentient beings, I shall joyfully give them with a pure mind, so that you may never incur a share of sin."
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Compassion again addressed the Tathāgata Jewel Treasury, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”

If, wherever I am born, while practicing the conduct of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* billions of *nayuta* hundreds of thousands of kalpas, there should be anyone who stands before me and seeks food from me—whether with gentle words, harsh words, mocking words, or straightforward speech—and requests it of me.
"World-Honored One!

If, toward those who come seeking, I should for even a single moment give rise to anger or a lack of love and respect, or if I should practice giving while seeking a karmic reward—if such were my giving, may I forever fail to see the Buddhas currently dwelling in the world and preaching the Dharma throughout the immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds of the ten directions, and may I not attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"World-Honored One!

If, with a pure mind, I bestow gifts upon mendicants, and if those who receive such gifts fall into obstacles to wholesome dharmas regarding that gift of faith—even to the extent of a hundred-millionth part of a single hair—may I never again behold the Buddhas."
World-Honored One!
May I fall into the Avīci Hell for even a ten-millionth part of a hair’s breadth of obstructing the wholesome dharmas of the recipient of my gifts;
and may it be the same for the food, drink, and clothing I give.
Even if a beggar were to come to me seeking my head—whether with gentle words, harsh words, mocking words, or straightforward speech—and were to demand my head from me.
"Bhagavān!

If, toward those who seek [my help], I should for even a single moment give rise to anger or a lack of love and respect while wishing to obtain the fruit [of my practice], may I never again behold the Buddhas."
"Bhagavān!
Even if it causes me to enter the Avīci Hell, I shall practice giving in this way;
my practice of ethical discipline shall be likewise, and so too for generosity and relinquishment—thus it should be spoken."
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākāruṇika, saying:
‘Excellent, excellent!’”
"O virtuous man!
You have established this sublime vow with a mind of great compassion.
"Virtuous man! [the Buddha continued].
At that time, the entire great assembly—gods, gandharvas, asuras, and worldlings—stood with palms joined and praised, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
O virtuous and noble man!
With a mind of great compassion, you have established this wondrous vow that is most excellent and firm; you shall likewise satisfy all sentient beings through the six dharmas of reverential harmony.
"Good son! Just as the one named Bhinnasaṃjñā, who lived by wrong livelihood, made a vow to receive the bodhisattva’s alms, eighty-four thousand sentient beings also made vows. Good son!"

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇika, hearing that eighty-four thousand sentient beings had established such perceptions of impermanence as they had conceived, was filled with great joy. He rose, joined his palms in reverence, and having surveyed the entire assembly, his heart was moved by a mingling of compassion and joy, and he said: "How extraordinary! How unprecedented!

In that world of the five turbidities—a time of exhausted Dharma, hardship, great fetters, and distraction—I shall act as a guide and a merchant leader; I shall be a light and a lamp. For those who are powerless and lack awakening, I shall show the way. Indeed, from the moment I first resolved for enlightenment, I have been able to practice such unsurpassed bodhicaryā, and in every place where I am born, I am able to give away my head, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands, feet, blood, flesh, skin, and bones, even to the point of giving my food and drink."
"Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā returned to sit before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Buddha, saying:
'World-Honored One!'"

Throughout immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya-nayuta-śata-sahasra* kalpas in all the places where I am born, there may be those who come to me seeking alms; whether it be food or drink, or even the gift of my head—whatever they receive from my hand, down to a billionth part of a single hair—I shall grant them until the very end of *bodhi*.

If, after I have attained enlightenment, I do not liberate those sentient beings from birth and death, and do not bestow upon them the prediction of the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or the Mahāyāna, may I never again behold the present Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, and may I not attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Good son! The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha again praised that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākāruṇika, saying:
‘Excellent, excellent!’”
"O virtuous man!

You maintain your bodhisattva vows and practices in this very way. Long ago, the Tathāgata Meruprabhā exhorted you to resolve for enlightenment; before the Tathāgata Lokendraprabha, you established such bodhisattva vows and practices, and thus you have practiced the bodhisattva path."

Since first establishing his vow, more great kalpas have passed than the sands of the Ganges River; that Great Man, in the eastern direction, within a hundred-year-old world-system called Jvalantī (Blazing) situated at the furthest edge among billions of Buddha-fields, has attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, up to Buddha, World-Honored One, Jñānakusumanirmalottaravijayabodhīśvara, he performed the deeds of a Buddha for forty-five years and then entered parinirvāṇa without remainder.
"O Mahākāruṇika!

After the parinirvāṇa of that Tathāgata Jñānapuṣpavimalottarabodhyaiśvarya, the True Dharma (saddharma) shall remain for a thousand years; after the extinction of the True Dharma, the Semblance Dharma (pratirūpakadharma) shall likewise remain for a thousand years."
O Mahākāruṇika!

Furthermore, during the period of the True Dharma following the parinirvāṇa of that Tathāgata Jñānapuṣpavimalottarabodhyaiśvarya, there will be bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs in the Semblance Dharma who break the precepts, engage in evil dharmas, perverse conduct, and improper behavior; who are shameless and lack remorse; who destroy the offerings to the Dharma and have no sense of shame or remorse; and who cut off the robes, food, drink, bedding, medicinal requisites, and various articles of worship belonging to the Saṃgha of the four quarters and the present Saṃgha, taking them for themselves, either consuming them personally or giving them to laypeople.
O Mahākāruṇika!
At that time, the Tathāgata Jñānakusumanirupamottarabodhyaiśvarya first bestowed the prediction of enlightenment upon all those of the three vehicles.
O Mahākāruṇika!
Any sentient beings who don the dyed saffron robes within the Dharma of that Tathāgata shall first be granted the prediction of non-retrogression in the three vehicles.

Furthermore, any bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who have committed root offenses, provided they previously served that Tathāgata as their teacher, shall also be granted the prediction of non-retrogression in the three vehicles by virtue of their roots of goodness.
“Good son! The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā again addressed the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”
I have made this vow: for as long as I practice the conduct of unsurpassed bodhi, and for as many beings as I shall convert through that conduct of unsurpassed bodhi.

If, while exhorting and transforming sentient beings through the *dānapāramitā*, I were to practice it even to the extent of a billionth part of a hair’s breadth, yet fail to prevent those sentient beings from remaining in the stages of the three vehicles until they reach non-retrogression—even if only a single person remains so—I would never again behold the Buddhas currently dwelling in and preaching the Dharma throughout the immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* worlds of the ten directions, and I would not attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained unsurpassed wisdom, if there are sentient beings within my Dharma who wear the dyed kashaya robes, even if they have committed root offenses, or if—due to various views—they have fallen away from the Triple Gem and committed numerous transgressions; and if among these bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, there is one who, for even a single moment, conceives the thought of regarding me as their teacher and gives rise to a heart of reverence, or if they give rise to a mind of reverence toward the Dharma and the Saṅgha, World-Honored One!”

If I were not to bestow upon those sentient beings the prediction of non-retrogression in the three vehicles, and were to leave even a single person behind, may I never again behold the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, until I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Bhagavān!

Once I have attained bodhi, I shall cause those who wear the dyed robes of the kāṣāya to be respected, honored, and venerated by devas and humans; and may any sentient beings who see these robes attain non-retrogression in the three vehicles."

Should there be sentient beings oppressed by hunger and thirst, lacking food and drink—whether they be yakṣas in poverty, humans in poverty, or hungry ghost beings among the preta realm—if they obtain even a four-finger-width of this dyed saffron robe, may all their desires for food and drink be fulfilled according to their wishes.

If there are sentient beings who are not in harmony with one another, abounding in resentment and jealousy, and fighting each other—whether they be devas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, nāgas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, or other worldly people engaged in battle—if they are able to bring to mind the *kāṣāya*, it shall cause those sentient beings to attain a heart of compassion, a gentle heart, a heart free from enmity, a pure heart, and a mind that acts accordingly.

If sentient beings, whether in battle or in legal disputes, out of a desire to protect their bodies, honor, revere, and make offerings to the *kāṣāya*, and always carry it with them, those beings will always be victorious wherever they are, none shall be able to overcome them, and they will be safely delivered from battle and dispute.
World-Honored One!

If my *kāṣāya* were not endowed with these five noble virtues, may I never again behold the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions; may I be unable to fully perform the Buddha-work; may I completely forget all the Dharmas; and may I be unable to subdue those of other teachings.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha extended his right arm, rubbed the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika with his hand, and said:
‘Excellent, excellent!’”
"O virtuous man!
Your aspiration is most excellent, and your eloquence is wondrous and supreme.
O virtuous man!"
"In this way, once you have attained bodhi, you shall don the dyed robes of the kashaya and possess these five noble virtues to benefit sentient beings.
Son of good family!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika received this prediction.
"Excellent, excellent!

Rejoicing and leaping for joy, he touched him with his right hand—adorned with the hundred blessings of a Tathāgata, soft, and with fingers joined by a web—and [the youth] was restored to childhood, as if twenty years of age."

“Good son! At that time, the entire great assembly—gods, gandharvas, asuras, and worldly humans—again joined their palms and stood respectfully, honoring and making offerings to the Mahāsattva Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇika. They offered flowers, incense, and even music to the Mahāsattva Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇika; having praised him with sublime verses, they took their seats.”

Chapter 22: On Adornment "Good son!

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā, having prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, sat down again before the Tathāgata and addressed the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, saying:"

World-Honored One,

"Bhagavān!
With what provisions do sons and daughters of good family abide with firm stability?
By means of which gate of decisive samādhi do they adorn themselves?"
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika, saying:
'Excellent, excellent!'"
O Mahākāruṇika!
Your question is most excellent, and your eloquence is supremely wondrous.
Furthermore, O Mahākāruṇika!
He has appeared for the sake of benefiting many, immeasurable, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, O Great Compassionate One,
you are truly able to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding such a meaning as this.
Therefore, O Great Compassionate One!
Listen well;

O Mahākāruṇika!
A son of good family who seeks the Mahāyāna possesses a samādhi called Śūraṅgama; when a bodhisattva dwells in this samādhi, he is able to enter all samādhis.

This is called the gate of the bodhisattva seeking the Great Vehicle’s definitive samādhi.
"What is called the Dharma-gate of the requisites for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?

The bodhisattva’s application of the provision of ethical discipline fulfills his vows;
the bodhisattva’s application of the provision of patience tames the mind;
and the bodhisattva’s application of the provision of wisdom brings knowledge of all fetters and afflictions.
Through the accumulation of hearing, the bodhisattva attains incalculable eloquence;
through the accumulation of merit, the bodhisattva attains the benefit of sentient beings;
through the accumulation of wisdom, the bodhisattva attains incalculable knowledge.
Through the resource of the Bodhisattva’s cessation, the mind of purposeful action is accomplished;
through the resource of the Bodhisattva’s contemplation, there is neither right nor wrong;
through the resource of the Bodhisattva’s loving-kindness, there is an unimpeded mind.
Through the application of the bodhisattva’s provision of compassion, one transforms sentient beings without weariness;
through the application of the bodhisattva’s provision of joy, one finds delight in the joy of the Dharma;

The bodhisattva’s requisite for hearing the Dharma is the relinquishing of hindrances;
the bodhisattva’s requisite for leaving the household life is the relinquishing of all conditioned phenomena;

The bodhisattva attains the attainment of mindfulness through dhāraṇī;
the bodhisattva attains the attainment of mental resources through the realization of the meaning of the mind;
the bodhisattva attains the attainment of ultimate resources through the awakening to ultimate discourse.
Through the application of the Bodhisattva’s foundations of mindfulness, one realizes the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena;

through the application of the Bodhisattva’s bases of supernormal power, one attains lightness of body and mind.
Through the perfection of the bodhisattva’s equipment of the faculties, they fulfill the faculties of all sentient beings;
through the perfection of the bodhisattva’s equipment of the powers, they subdue all fetters and latent tendencies;
through the perfection of the bodhisattva’s equipment of the factors of enlightenment, they awaken to the treasure of the Dharma and attain rebirth in the heavens.
The bodhisattva’s resource of correct understanding functions to resolve the doubts of all sentient beings;
the bodhisattva’s resource of non-reliance functions to attain spontaneous wisdom (*svayambhū-jñāna*);
and the bodhisattva’s resource of spiritual friends functions to access all gateways of merit.
The bodhisattva’s equipment of resolve enables them not to be separated from all worlds;
the bodhisattva’s equipment of action enables them to discern all activities;
the bodhisattva’s equipment of ultimate resolve enables them to reach the most excellent state.
The Bodhisattva, by means of the requisite of contemplation, practices the Dharma as it has been heard;
the Bodhisattva, by means of the requisite of gathering material resources, encourages and inspires sentient beings;
the Bodhisattva, by means of the requisite of gathering the true Dharma, ensures that the lineage of the Three Jewels is never interrupted.
By means of the bodhisattva’s skillful dedication of the resources of practice, one attains the purity of the buddha-field;
by means of the bodhisattva’s skillful dedication of the resources of practice, one fulfills the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).

O Great Compassionate One! When one’s mind regarding all phenomena is like space and as level as the palm of a hand, this is called the fearless adornment of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
Furthermore, what is meant by "fulfilling patience"?
One who is thus does not perceive therein any dharma that can be attained, awakened to, or known; they understand the dharma of non-retribution, namely:
teaching compassion and selflessness.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms within the four continents attained the stage of non-retrogression;

Hundreds of thousands of sections on abandoning the causes and conditions of folly;
hundreds of thousands of sections on samādhis and liberations;
hundreds of thousands of sections on the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities of a Buddha.

and at another time, that Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, entered parinirvāṇa without remainder.

“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā made offerings with various and manifold immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya musical instruments, flower garlands, powdered incense, ointment incense, banners, parasols, pennants, streamers, and other miscellaneous jewels.”
Having performed various cremation rites, he erected a stupa made of the seven precious jewels for the relics, five yojanas in height and half a yojana in length and breadth.

For seven days, he made offerings with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* quantities of music, flower garlands, powdered incense, ointments, banners, parasols, pennants, and other miscellaneous jewels; furthermore, right there, he transformed immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings, causing them to abide in the Three Vehicles.

After those seven days had passed, he went forth into homelessness together with eighty-four thousand people; they shaved off their hair and beards, donned the dharma robes, and having become firm in the True Dharma, all became established in accordance with the Dharma.
After the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha entered parinirvāṇa, he protected and upheld the True Dharma, causing the transformative influence of the Path to flourish for ten thousand years.

During that time, he exhorted and transformed immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings, establishing them in the Three Vehicles: some were established in the three refuges, some in the precepts of an upāsaka, some in the precepts of a śrāmaṇera, and others were fully cultivated in the brahmacarya of a bhikṣu, establishing them therein.

He caused many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings to attain wholesome supernormal powers and to dwell in the cultivation of the Brahma-faring. He caused them to know that the aggregates (*skandhas*) are like enemies and that the sense-bases (*āyatanas*) are like an empty village. Furthermore, he caused them to gain knowledge and vision of the conditioned phenomena born of causes and conditions, manifesting all dharmas as selfless—like shadows, like mirages, and like the moon reflected in water—and as being without arising or ceasing, without continuity, eternally extinguished, tranquil, serene, supremely wondrous, and the cessation that is true *nirvāṇa*.

Having caused them to know this and established them in the Eightfold Noble Path, that Great Compassionate Great Śramaṇa then passed away; thereafter, sentient beings gathered like clouds and made offerings to his relics in the same manner as they would offer to the relics of a Wheel-Turning Sage King.

At that time, having thus made offerings to the relics of the Great Compassionate Great Śramaṇa, on the day his life ended, the True Dharma of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha also vanished. Those Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each took birth in other world-systems according to their original vows: some were born in the Tuṣita Heaven by virtue of their vows, some were born among human beings, some were born among nāgas, some were born among yakṣas, some were born among asuras, and some, according to their vows, underwent various births as animals.
Chapter 23: The Gift of the Eyes The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Chapter Twenty-Three: The Gift of the Eyes “Good son!

At that time, the sentient beings joined their palms together and said with one voice:

At that time, the king’s ministers provided him with many means for sustaining life.

“Good son! At that time, not long after King Puṇyabala had converted one kingdom, he persevered with such firm diligence as to convert a second kingdom.

At that time, King Puṇyabala, having recognized for himself that he had brought all of Jambudvīpa under his dominion as its great king, subsequently exhorted others to refrain from taking the lives of others and to abide in non-killing. At another time, all those seekers from Jambudvīpa came to visit King Puṇyabala, who bestowed upon them various gifts according to their respective needs.
At that time, there was a malevolent spirit named Dhūmrasvara who approached the king and stood before him, saying:
"O Great King!..."
"You are able to bestow various and most extensive gifts for the sake of seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Great King!

The king asked,
"What do you seek? Dharmika Kūṭadanta replied:
"Great King!

"O son of good family!"

"This is my spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), who can urge this fragile body of mine to become firm and solid.
The King said, "Be joyful for now;

"With a heart of joy, I give you my own skin so that I may attain the unsurpassed bodhi of a Buddha.
Son of good family!
At that time, King Puṇyabala plucked out both his eyes with his right hand and gave them to the heterodox ascetic; as blood flowed over his face, he spoke these words:
"Listen to me, you many devas, yakṣas, kinnaras, asuras, and all virtuous deities, as well as those who dwell in the sky or on the earth:
know that I am a bodhisattva practicing this giving!
May I attain the most supreme, wondrous, and tranquil path, and cross sentient beings over the four torrents."
"May they be transferred to Nirvana and reach the other shore.
He further spoke these words:

"If I am to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, may my life-force not be severed for as many days as that, may my mindfulness remain undisturbed, and may no regret arise, so that this heterodox incantation may be fully accomplished through its power."
He said: "Good son! You may take my skin."

“Good son! At that time, was the father of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the Great Compassionate One, anyone else?
Do not harbor such a thought; it was I myself.”

This was my first initial aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. At the moment of that first aspiration, I exhorted countless sentient beings toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; this was my first courageous practice.
Because I followed my vow, after passing away from there, I was born into a *caṇḍāla* family in a defiled buddha-field; this was my second courageous practice.

Being able, within that *caṇḍāla* lineage, to exhort sentient beings to abide in goodness, and through the power of my own progress, eventually attaining the status of a powerful universal monarch (*cakravartin*), I eliminated all strife, enmity, jealousy, and various defilements throughout Jambudvīpa, and furthermore increased the lifespan of its inhabitants; this was my first instance of personally giving my eyes and skin as a gift.
When his life there ended, he was reborn within the two continents of the world-system of Accumulated Impurity; by virtue of his original vow, he was again born into a family of caṇḍālas.

To speak briefly, therein, through such firm diligence, he exhorted sentient beings with wholesome dharmas, until he attained the status of a powerful universal monarch (cakravartin), who eliminated the various impurities of strife, enmity, and jealousy within that realm and increased the lifespan of its inhabitants.

Within that [realm], he also personally gave away his own tongue and ears, and so on, throughout all the impure Buddha-fields of the trichiliocosm; in every single direction, he performed such deeds of a great man, continuing with unflagging vigor and courage through the power of his original vows.

By virtue of his original vows, within Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—afflicted by the five turbidities—he performs such deeds of a great man, exhorting sentient beings to abide in wholesome karma within the Three Vehicles, and further eliminating all manner of defilements, including strife, contention, enmity, and jealousy.
"Good son!

For this reason, the buddha-fields of other Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are pure. This is because when those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, were formerly practicing the conduct for unsurpassed bodhi, they did not speak of the faults of others, did not address others with harsh words, did not manifest intimidation, and did not convert sentient beings by means of the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas. Therefore, those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have attained pure buddha-fields that are completely fulfilled according to their wishes."

In that buddha-field, there is no mention of receiving precepts or transgressing them; nor is there ever heard the sound of coarse speech or unwholesome words, nor any evil sounds. Only the sound of the Dharma fills that buddha-field. The sentient beings therein have whatever they desire at will, and there is not even the name of śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha.

It is not as good as my spending eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges within Buddha-fields as empty and subject to the five turbidities as the sands of the Ganges, urging the multitude toward the practice of goodness through words of intimidation and severity, and causing them to abide in the Three Vehicles according to their inclinations.

Because of those residual karmic effects, this Buddha-field of mine is now defiled and turbid, abounding in various unwholesome things, filled with evil sounds, and teeming with sentient beings who have accumulated roots of non-virtue;

I teach the Dharma through the three vehicles, taking up a Buddha-field according to my previously established vows, and transforming sentient beings accordingly. Thus, by diligently practicing with vigor and performing the conduct of enlightenment, I have obtained such a Buddha-field as I originally planted, just as I had previously vowed.
“Good son! I shall now briefly explain the practice of the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) that I have undertaken.

When I practiced the conduct of awakening (*bodhicaryā*), I gave to the utmost extent; no bodhisattva before me had ever practiced such giving, nor will there ever be a bodhisattva practicing the conduct of awakening who can give in such a manner.”
When I was practicing the bodhisattva conduct, I gave [this] as a gift, with the exception of the eight great beings.

He is named Bodhisattva Dhāraṇidatta; he will attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening in the world-realm Sarvarakṣā in the southern direction, where he will be known as the Tathāgata Vimalaprabha. After that Tathāgata Śreṣṭha had entered parinirvāṇa through unsurpassed parinirvāṇa, and after the passing of great kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, his Great Compassionate Relics (śarīra) still perform Buddha-work today within an empty Buddha-field amidst the five turbidities.

The Bodhisattva Dṛḍhapuṣpa shall practice the bodhisattva conduct through the power of his vows and exertion; ten *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas beyond this world, after the passing of as many great kalpas as there are grains of sand in ten Ganges Rivers, in the north there will be a Buddha-field in the five-turbid age named Indrasuvīra. Therein, that Great Being shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, known by the name Indrapriyadarśanarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and so forth, up to Buddha, World-Honored One.

The bodhisattva named Prajñāprabhābhaya-rati, that virtuous man, after the passing of one great kalpa, shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) in the west, in a world-system of the five turbidities named Tripilavati, amidst a human lifespan of one hundred years. By virtue of his original vow, he shall perform the Buddha-work for ten years and then enter parinirvāṇa; on that very day, the True Dharma shall also perish.

At that time, that buddha-field shall remain empty for ten years. Furthermore, by virtue of his original vow, the Bodhisattva Priyabāhu shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi among human beings with a lifespan of thirty years in the buddha-field of Dhūmaketu, receiving the name Jyotirjvalanavijaya Tathāgata, up to Buddha and World-Honored One.

Having fully performed the Buddha-work during those ten years, he shall enter the realm of nirvana without remainder; yet, by virtue of his original vow, after his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a full seventy years.
"Those two men have received the prediction of their former attainment and have been praised as 'Excellent'; they have received the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Having prostrated with their heads at the feet of the World-Honored One, those two men, filled with such joy, ascended into the air to a height of seven fathoms above the ground. With palms joined together, they praised the World-Honored One in unison with this verse:

With eyes as pure as they are free from dust, the Guide of the World, whose brilliance can subdue all heterodox teachers,

though he made offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, the past Guides did not bestow a prediction upon me.

for those who have lost their way, he proclaims the sublime Dharma, ferrying sentient beings across the river of birth and death.

having trained in these and in samādhi, we follow the World-Honored One like a shadow.
Delighting in the Dharma for my own livelihood, I have no dependence; hearing the Dharma, I conceive of it as the Teacher.
