The Gift of the Body. From the Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra. "Good sons!

In the distant past, beyond immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* great kalpas, at that time this land was named Virajamerudhvaja-nirvṛta. During that great kalpa, when the lifespan of humans was one hundred years, it was within the Semblance Dharma (*pratirūpaka-dharma*) of the Tathāgata Padmagandha.
"Good son!
At that time, I was a powerful Wheel-Turning King of Jambudvīpa named Invincible (Anabhibhū), who had a thousand sons; I exhorted them all toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
He too, at another time, went forth into homelessness and fully cultivated the holy life within the Dharma of the Tathāgata Padmagandha; he also proclaimed the Dharma of the Tathāgata Padmagandha.
Only my six sons did not wish to leave the household life, nor did they wish to resolve upon bodhicitta.
I repeatedly instructed them, saying:
"What do you seek?"
"Did you not resolve to attain bodhicitta and refuse to leave the household life? He replied,
"I cannot leave the household life."

Why is this? Because during the degenerate period of the Semblance Dharma (*pratirūpaka-dharma*), there will be those who have left the household life but are unable to fully maintain the body of precepts. They shall lack the seven riches and dwell perpetually in the abyss of birth and death; they shall further lose the merits of humans and devas, and those who do not fully maintain the Buddha’s prohibitive precepts shall remain long in the three miserable realms.
"Therefore, we are unable to leave the household life.
I asked them again:
"For what reason do you not resolve to attain bodhicitta?"
They said: "If you can give all of Jambudvīpa to us, we shall resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
“Good son! Having heard these words, I was filled with great joy and reflected to myself:
‘I have already caused all the people of Jambudvīpa to abide in the three refuges, exhorted them to observe the eightfold noble fast, and further encouraged them toward the three vehicles.’”
"I should now divide this Jambudvīpa into six portions and bestow them upon my six sons, exhorting them toward Bodhi.
It is fitting that I leave the household life and practice the holy life."
Then, acting upon what I had thought, I divided the entire Jambudvīpa into six parts and gave them to my sons; I myself then left the household life to practice the holy life (brahmacarya).

In that Jambudvīpa, the six kings were not in harmony; they fought, quarreled, harbored resentment, and envied one another. Pestilence spread, and they raised armies to engage in battle, each finding no peace. Consequently, the entire Jambudvīpa suffered from extreme famine; the heavens did not send down rain, the five grains did not ripen, and trees produced neither flowers, leaves, nor fruit. Even the various medicinal herbs failed to grow. The people, birds, and beasts were tormented by hunger and thirst, their bodies aflame with suffering beyond endurance.
I then reflected:
"Now is precisely the time; I ought to give my own body as an offering, providing my own flesh and blood to satisfy sentient beings.
Leaving my bed, I went to Mount Upadarśanavatī in the Middle Kingdom and made this vow:
"Just as I now relinquish my body and life, it is solely out of compassionate concern and not for the sake of becoming a deva;
for the benefit of the world and all devas, I shall become a mountain of flesh to provide for all sentient beings."
As I cast off this body to assume a wondrous form, I seek neither the status of Śakra, Brahmā, nor the Māra King;
for the benefit of the world’s people and all devas, may my flesh and blood become Mount Meru.
Listen, O humans, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and you tree spirits dwelling here on this mountain!
Out of compassion for sentient beings, I offer my own body’s flesh and blood to relieve the multitude of ministers.

"When I established my vow, the palaces of the asuras were all greatly shaken; the earth trembled with extreme severity, Mount Meru tilted and swayed, the waters of the ocean surged in waves, and the devas and all the spirits wept in sorrow."

At that time, I immediately threw myself down from Mount Jālavatī; by virtue of my original vow, it instantly became a mountain of flesh, one yojana in height, and exactly one yojana in both length and breadth.

People, birds, and beasts came to eat its flesh and blood; yet by virtue of its original vow, it grew day and night until it gradually reached a height of one thousand yojanas, with a length and breadth equally measuring one thousand yojanas. On all four sides, there were human heads, each fully complete with hair, nails, eyes, ears, noses, tongues, mouths, and teeth.
Those people raised their voices and cried out: "Ho!
You sentient beings!"

Each may take as they desire, eating flesh and drinking blood; whether it be eyes, ears, noses, tongues, mouths, teeth, or hair—whatever you wish for—you shall obtain it so that your bodies are fully satisfied, according to your every request.

Whether you have resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, or belong to the vehicle of the śrāvakas, or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas—this is the means by which you sustain your bodies; it will not be exhausted so soon as to cause you to incur the sin of misappropriating the faithful offerings, nor will it cause your lives to end prematurely.

Among those sentient beings with the wisdom of liberation, some give rise to the mind of the Śrāvaka vehicle, some give rise to the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, some give rise to the mind of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and some give rise to the mind seeking the blessings of humans and devas.
They eat flesh and drink blood; some take their eyes, some take their ears, some take their noses, some take their lips, some take their teeth, and some take their tongues.

By virtue of his original vow, [the flesh] immediately returned to its former state, neither exhausted nor diminished, for ten thousand years; with the flesh and blood of his body, he filled all the people of Jambudvīpa, as well as the yakṣas and various birds and beasts.

For ten thousand years, I gave away eyes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; I gave blood equal to the four great oceans; I gave my own flesh as vast as a thousand Mount Sumerus; I gave my tongue to others like Mount Cakravāḍa;
I gave my body as large as Mount Meru; I gave my nose like Mount Mahāmeru; I gave my teeth like Vulture Peak Mountain (Gṛdhrakūṭa); and I gave the flesh of my body throughout the Sahā world-system.

“Good son! Observe how, for ten thousand years, I have given my body and life in this manner—immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable—as alms, thereby satisfying immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable sentient beings, without giving rise to a single thought of regret during even a moment.”
I then made this vow regarding them:
"If my intention to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi is thus fulfilled, may my own flesh and blood be sufficient for all within this single world-system."

May I, throughout ten thousand years as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, within every direction of this stainless Mount Meru-like Buddha-field, manifest such a body in each and every direction for ten thousand years, filling sentient beings with my own body, blood, flesh, skin, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, lips, teeth, and hair, and exhorting them toward the Three Vehicles.

If there are humans, yakṣas, rākṣasas, or any beings with the four great elements who eat flesh and drink blood—even down to the hungry ghosts—I shall satisfy them all, just as I have relieved all sentient beings within my single buddha-field with the flesh and blood of my own body.

In this way, throughout the Buddha-lands of the five turbidities, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, he fills those sentient beings with his own body, blood, flesh, eyes, and even his tongue.
With such a body, throughout great kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, one shall satisfy all sentient beings within those Buddha-fields with one's own life and body.

If my vow were not fulfilled, may I never again behold the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who have already turned the wheel of Dharma and currently abide in the world preaching the Dharma in other worlds throughout the ten directions; until then, may I not attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

May I, within the cycle of birth and death, not hear the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṃgha, the sound of the pāramitās, the sound of the powers, or the sound of the fearlessnesses; may I, within the cycle of birth and death, not even hear the sound of what is good.
If my own body were given away to fully satisfy all sentient beings, yet such a vow were not fulfilled, may I dwell forever in the Avīci Hell.

If this vow of mine is thus fulfilled—just as I have here in this single Buddha-field, in every direction, satisfied all sentient beings with my own flesh and blood—may I likewise, throughout the other Buddha-fields of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, satisfy sentient beings with the flesh and blood of my body.

"Good son! Observe the Tathāgata’s practice of the perfection of giving through the continuous gift of his body and the gift of his eyes, which fills the entire Jambudvīpa and extends as far as the summit of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."
“Good son! This is the Tathāgata’s brief explanation of the perfection of giving through the gift of the body.
Chapter Twenty-five: The Gift of Jewels The Lotus of Compassion Mahāyāna Sūtra, Chapter Twenty-five: The Gift of Jewels “Furthermore, good son!”
After that, during an immeasurable number of billions of kalpas, this buddha-field was named Candraprabhā (Moonlight) and likewise possessed the five corruptions (*pañca-kaṣāya*).

At that time, I was a powerful universal monarch (*cakravartin*) in this Jambudvīpa named Dīpapradyota (Lamp-Light). Just as previously described, I exhorted and transformed all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa through such virtuous means.
At that time, as I went out to tour the gardens, I saw a man with both arms bound behind his back most tightly.
I immediately asked my ministers:
"What crime has this man committed?"
The ministers replied, "This person has violated the king’s law;

though he is a subject of this realm, he has failed to pay the annual tax of one-sixth as required by custom. Having disobeyed the command and yet dwelling within the royal domain, he sustains himself through cultivation and planting without complying with the tax obligations; for this reason, his body is bound."
He immediately commanded his ministers:
"Release this man at once; do not press him for provisions, ghee, or oil.
The ministers replied to the king:

"Never has there been anyone who could offer goods to the king with a virtuous heart. Whatever is provided daily for the king’s consort and her retinue, and all that is required for the kitchen offerings, comes from the people; were it not for the king's power, these things could never be obtained, for not a single person has ever given them with a kind heart."
At that time, I was filled with sorrow and anxiety, and I reflected to myself:
"To whom shall this sovereignty over all of Jambudvīpa now be entrusted? At that moment, I had five hundred sons, all of whom I exhorted toward Bodhi.

I then divided this Jambudvīpa into five hundred portions and gave them to my sons; I immediately renounced the world and went to the forest to seek the holy life of a seer. To the south, near the great ocean, I sat in meditation within an Udumbara grove, sustaining my life by eating fruits and roots. Before long, I gradually attained the five supernormal powers.

“At that time, there were five hundred merchants in Jambudvīpa who went to sea to gather treasures and obtained a great mass of jewels. Among them, the leader of the merchants was named King of Constellations (*Sūryarāja*); by the power of his merit, he had obtained a wish-fulfilling *maṇi*. From that island of jewels, he took many precious gems and *maṇis*.

When the funeral procession first set out, the waters of the sea surged with waves; the various nāgas were distressed and agitated, and the sea deities wept. Among them was a nāga-rishi named Aśvakarṇa, who was in truth a bodhisattva born therein by virtue of his original vow.
That Mahāsattva protected the merchants, leading them safely across the sea back to their own abode.

Following those merchants was an evil rākṣasa who constantly pursued them from behind, seeking an opportunity to harm them. During the day, he unleashed violent winds and rain, causing the merchants to lose their way and become utterly terrified, not knowing where they were headed. They raised a great clamor, wailing and weeping in grief, calling upon the gods of heaven, the wind gods, and the water gods, even invoking their parents and beloved children.
At that time, hearing their voices with my divine ear, I immediately went to console them, saying:
"O merchants, do not be afraid! I shall guide you along the path and lead you safely back to Jambudvīpa."
I then bound my own hands with silk cloth, placed them inside oil, and set them ablaze with fire, uttering these words of sincere resolve:

"For thirty-six years in the forest, I have dwelt in the four Brahma-abodes; for the benefit of sentient beings, I have eaten various fruits and the roots of plants. Having already converted eighty-four thousand nāgas and yakṣas, I have caused them to abide in non-retrogression toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"By the karmic retribution of these roots of goodness, may my hands burn so that these merchants may attain the Way and reach Jambudvīpa in safety.
Thus his hands burned for seven days and seven nights, and those merchants returned safely to Jambudvīpa.
At that time, I made this vow for myself:

"Since this Jambudvīpa lacks all manner of precious jewels, if my aspiration to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is fulfilled, may I become a merchant leader who gathers wish-fulfilling gems, and may I cause a rain of various kinds of jewels to fall seven times in every direction throughout all quarters of this buddha-field."
"In this manner, throughout the ten directions, within as many empty Buddha-lands of the five turbidities as there are sands in the Ganges River, it was as previously described.

My intention has been thus fully realized; for as many great kalpas as there are sands in the Ganges River, I have acted as the unsurpassed caravan leader, raining down various jewels upon as many empty Buddha-lands of the five turbidities as there are sands in the Ganges River, raining down rains of various kinds of jewels seven times in each and every direction."
In this way, he satisfied immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings according to their wishes and established them in the Three Vehicles.
Good son! Observe the marks and signs that are the fruit of the Tathāgata’s roots of goodness from his precious giving.
Chapter Twenty-Six: The Bestowal of Medical Prescriptions The Lotus of Compassion Mahāyāna Sūtra, Chapter Twenty-Six: The Bestowal of Medical Prescriptions "Furthermore, good son!

After the passage of immeasurable kalpas, this buddha-field was named *Āloka-mūḍha* (Obscured by Light), and the kalpa was named *Nandana* (Joy); it was likewise characterized by the five corruptions (*pañca-kaṣāya*).
During the time when the human lifespan was fifty thousand years, by virtue of my original vow, I became a brahmin in this Jambudvīpa named Mālāgandha, who was proficient in the four Vedas.

At that time, sentient beings were characterized by extremely heavy views, delighting in resentment and jealousy, and fond of strife and contention. With courageous power, I preached the Dharma for these beings, showing them that the aggregates (skandhas) are like enemies and the sense bases (āyatanas) are like empty villages; I demonstrated the continuous arising and ceasing of causes and conditions, and manifested the contemplation of mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasmṛti). I exhorted them to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and as they dedicated their roots of goodness and all came to abide therein, I myself attained the five supernormal powers (pañcābhijñā).
At that time, immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings, through my instruction, also attained the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*).

Thus, immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings abandoned all enmity, jealousy, and various forms of strife; they went to groves and forests to eat various fruits and roots, sat in meditation and contemplation, and dwelt in the four Brahma-abodes day and night without contention.

When the kalpa is about to end, those worthy of receiving offerings will fill Jambudvīpa; by this, strife, enmity, jealousy, and untimely winds and rains will be extinguished. The five grains will grow upon the earth, all fragrant and delicious, and food will increase physical strength. Yet, because the kalpa is evil, sentient beings will be afflicted by various kinds of diseases.
I then reflected:
"If I cannot eliminate these various illnesses of sentient beings, may I not attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"I am unable to eliminate the disease of the fetters of sentient beings; by what skillful means shall I remove their sickness?
He further conceived this thought:

"I should assemble Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, and all other celestial seers, dragon seers, yakṣa seers, and human seers, so that for the benefit of sentient beings, we may create and manifest medicinal prescriptions."
I then used my supernormal powers to go and inform Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors, as well as the celestial seers, nāga seers, yakṣa seers, and human seers.

There is a mountain named Ayomukha-kapilavastu; they gathered upon its summit at the place of the great physician Vaidūryakaraṅka, where he composed and expounded prescriptions for treating the great diseases of wind, fire, and water, causing the illnesses of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya beings to be completely eliminated.
Within this, I established a vow as follows:

"By means of this illumination of wisdom, I shall now cause immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings to abide in the Three Vehicles, close the gates to the evil destinies, establish them within the heavenly realms, and eliminate all their ailments; thus, for immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings, I shall act as the light of wisdom and place them in peace and happiness."
"By the karmic retribution of these roots of goodness, may this intention of mine be fulfilled.

In this manner, he closes the gates to the evil destinies for immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings in one direction and establishes them within the heavenly realms. For the sake of those afflicted by illness, he gathers the hosts of devas, sages, yakṣas, and nāgas; and for the sake of all beings, he assembles at the summit of Mount Vaidūrya—the gathering place of physicians—to preach the prescriptions and medicines that eliminate all diseases and restore health.
In this manner, throughout all directions within this obscure buddha-field, he performs such deeds of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*), establishing sentient beings upon the path of the devas.

Thus, having assembled devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and human sages, he creates and expounds various incantations and arts for the sake of sentient beings. In this same way, within this obscure buddha-field, amidst as many *pañcakaṣāya* (five-turbidity) empty buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges, he shall perform such deeds of a great man, causing sentient beings to abide in the three vehicles and establish them upon the path of the devas; he shall manifest various incantations and arts to eliminate all diseases in the world.
"Good son! With such fulfillment of my unsurpassed intention, I further perform these deeds of a great man throughout every direction within this obscure buddha-field."

Just as the vows I have established are unsurpassed, so too shall I perform such deeds of a great man in every direction within each and every Buddha-field throughout the ten directions—Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, empty of Buddhas during the five turbidities—exactly as I originally vowed.
"Good son! Observe the Tathāgata’s practice of supreme wisdom and his practice of bodhi; this is the Tathāgata’s third way of well-guarding and sustaining the seeds of the roots of goodness.

Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Manifestation of the Bestowal of Hidden Treasures From the Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra Furthermore, after the passing of incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, at a favorable time, this buddha-field was named Vimala (Free from Defilement). During that *mahākalpa* of great benefit, there were likewise the five corruptions (*pañca-kaṣāya*).
In the fifty-fourth continent to the east, called Jambudvīpa Tiraḷi, I was born there for the sake of delivering sentient beings as a Wheel-Turning Sage King of the four continents, named Ākāśa.
Within that realm, I teach and transform sentient beings by means of the ten virtuous actions, exhorting them toward the Three Vehicles so that they may abide therein.

Furthermore, I practice universal giving and give in all places; whenever anyone comes seeking various precious treasures—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, *yukan*, *daikan*, bright moonstone, or crystal—I bestow them upon them, and my precious treasures increase ever more.
I asked my ministers,
"By what cause have these many treasures been obtained?
The ministers replied:
"The great dragon kings reveal hidden treasures; because these treasures appear, the world abounds in precious gems.
Yet, although they reveal these treasures, they do not equal those who seek jewels from the king."
I then made this vow:

"If my aspiration to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi among those people of a hundred-year lifespan in that world of five turbidities, where the fetters are extremely heavy, is fulfilled, may I become a dragon king named Pratyutpanna-nidhāna in this buddha-field."

In every direction throughout the Buddha-field of Vimala, he received the body of a nāga seven times each; in each and every body, he manifested billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of treasure-vaults filled with various jewels—gold, silver, and even *yukan*, *daikan*, *mingyue*, and crystal—which he bestowed as gifts.
"Each individual treasure-store is one thousand yojanas in length and breadth, filled with such various jewels, which he opens and bestows upon all sentient beings.

Establishing such courageous and heroic deeds in this Buddha-field, he likewise does so seven times in each of the ten directions, throughout all quarters of the worlds of the five turbidities, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, just as previously described.

“Good son! When I established this vow, at that very moment, hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of devas rained down various exquisite flowers from the midst of the sky and praised me, saying:
‘Excellent, excellent!’”
"May all my offerings be as previously vowed, and may my intentions surely be fulfilled.
At that time, the great assembly everywhere heard this voice; the devas in the sky changed the king's title, naming him Sarvadarśin (All-Giver).
Having heard this, the people immediately conceived this thought:
"We should ask him for that which is difficult to relinquish; if he gives it, he may be called 'All-Giver,' but if he does not give it, he is not an All-Giver."
When those sentient beings came to the king to beg for the palace women, the chief queen, and the men, King Ākāśa, with a heart of joy, gave them all away.
Those people then conceived this thought:

"Giving away one's wife and children is not yet difficult; we should now beg for the king's throne and his own limbs. If he can give these, he is called 'All-Giver' (Sarvadada); if he cannot, he is not an All-Giver."
At that time, there was a man who reverently observed the fowl-vow, named Candraprabha (Moonlight). He went before King Gaganarāja and said:
"Great King!
If you are one who gives all things, then this entire Jambudvīpa may be given to me."
Upon hearing these words, the king was filled with great joy; he immediately bathed him in fragrant water, dressed him in royal garments, and installed him as the sovereign of all Jambudvīpa.
He immediately made this vow:

"Just as I today renounce this sovereignty over Jambudvīpa for the sake of fulfilling my aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I now establish this king; may all beings submit to him, may his life-span increase without end, and may he ultimately become a great universal monarch (*cakravartin*)."

"Just as I bestow this royal throne upon him today, I pray that when I attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he shall receive the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) of the office of the successor to my *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
"Furthermore, there was a brahmin named Kūṭadanta who came to beg for my two feet.
With a sincere heart, I took up a sharp blade and cut off my own two feet to give them to him, immediately making this great vow:
'May I attain the unsurpassed feet of precept.'"
Furthermore, there was a brahmin named Daṭṭhāpi who came to beg for both his eyes.
He plucked them out himself and gave them to him, immediately making this vow:
"By means of this gift, may I attain the unsurpassed five eyes."
Again, there was a brahmin named Kaṇḍaraka who came and begged for both his ears.
He cut them off himself and gave them to him, immediately making this vow:
"By means of this gift, may I attain the ear of unsurpassed wisdom."
"Furthermore, there was another heretic named Yilin who came to beg for my male organ.
I cut it off myself and gave it to him, whereupon I immediately made this vow:
'By means of this gift, may I attain the supreme mark of the concealed organ.'"
"Furthermore, when others came to beg for my flesh and blood,
I gave it to them immediately and made this vow:
'By the retribution of this gift, may I attain the mark of golden-colored skin.'"
Furthermore, there was a Pāribhāṣaka named Divyarasa who came to beg for both my hands.
I myself cut off my left hand and had another person cut off my right hand to give to him; immediately thereafter, I made this vow:
"May I attain the fruit of becoming the Supreme Hand of Faith."
"Just as I severed my own limbs and joints, with blood flowing and coating my body, I immediately made this vow:
'If by this giving I am to fulfill the aspiration for Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, may I surely obtain the place where this body was entrusted.'"
“At that time, those ministers and minor kings lacked noble wisdom and failed to recognize his profound gratitude. They deliberated together, saying:
‘The King is utterly foolish and possesses not even a fraction of discernment. Having maimed his own limbs and joints, he disregards the royal throne; he is like a mass of flesh—what use is he?’”
"Now you must abandon me.
He then seized me and threw me into a grave mound outside the city; having abandoned me, he returned home.
While I was there, gadflies, flies, mosquitoes, gnats, foxes, wolves, crows, and vultures came to devour me, yet with a virtuous heart, I immediately made this vow:

"Now, having renounced this entire royal throne and even my own limbs to give them away, I have not for a single moment of thought conceived a sense of resentment, nor do I feel any regret; thus I shall fulfill this intention."
May this body of mine transform into a mountain of flesh; may all sentient beings who eat meat and blood come here in their entirety to consume my flesh and blood.

Once they have come to eat, by virtue of my original vow, may this body of mine grow and increase day by day, gradually becoming a thousand *yojanas* in height and exactly five hundred *yojanas* in both length and breadth, so that for a thousand years I may satisfy sentient beings with the flesh and blood of my body.

Within that place, he gave away his tongue, and when birds and beasts came to eat it, by the power of his original vow, it was immediately restored; though the tongue he had given away was as vast as Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, he then made this vow:
"May I always attain the supreme mark of the broad and long tongue."
Having passed away there, by virtue of his original vow, he was reborn among the dragons of Jambudvīpa in the region of Tīla, where he was named Pratyakṣanidhāna (Manifesting Treasure).

On the very night the dragon king was born, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of treasure-vaults appeared, filled with heaps of various jewels, namely gold, silver, and so forth, up to crystal.
"O you sentient beings!

You should cultivate the ten wholesome karmas and resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, or for the vehicle of the *śrāvaka*, or resolve for the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*; then, according to your respective desires, you may go and take the jewels."

In that state of weeping, he returned to Jambudvīpa seven times as a nāga; throughout seventy-seven billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of years, he manifested immeasurable asaṃkhyeya hidden treasures and bestowed them upon sentient beings.

Therein, he thus exhorted immeasurable asaṃkhyeya sentient beings, causing them to abide in the three vehicles and cultivate the ten wholesome karmas, and provided sentient beings with an abundance of various kinds of precious jewels.
He immediately made a vow to attain the unsurpassed thirty-two marks of a great man.
Thus, for seven lifetimes across two continents, he was born as a nāga, establishing this conduct of a true man.
In this manner, throughout the three continents and even across all directions of the remaining defiled worlds, he established this conduct of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*).

Likewise, within as many Buddha-fields as there are sands in the Ganges River throughout the ten directions—worlds empty of Buddhas and characterized by the five turbidities—in every direction of each of these fields, he likewise became a nāga seven times.
For seventy-seven billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of years, he bestowed immeasurable, incalculable hidden treasures upon sentient beings, as previously described.

“Good son! Observe that the Tathāgata, through the power of his supreme diligence, performed the practices for awakening while fully possessing the thirty-two marks. No previous bodhisattva was able to perform such practices for awakening with such extreme diligence; there is none now, nor will there ever be a bodhisattva in the future who can perform the practices for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* with such extreme diligence, except for those eight individuals whom I have previously mentioned.”

After incalculable eons, during another auspicious period, this buddha-field was named Coral Well; manifesting the emptiness of the five turbidities within the great kalpa of the Lotus, at that time I was a Śakra of these four continents, named Equal Illumination.

Seeing that the sentient beings of this Jambudvīpa do not seek the practice of the precepts, I immediately transform my body into that of a terrifying and fearsome evil yakṣa and descend before these people of Jambudvīpa to stand in their presence.
Upon seeing me, he was struck with great terror and asked me,
"What do you seek? I replied:
"I require food; do not use anything else, but prepare it quickly.
He asked, "What kind of food do you wish to have?"

I said: "I eat only human flesh and no other substance. If you can, for as long as life lasts, abstain from taking life up to and including wrong views; if you can resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, or upon the mind of the *pratyekabuddha-yāna* or the *śrāvaka-yāna*, and are able to practice in this way, I will not eat you."
He manifests as a transformed being and takes their food.
When those sentient beings see this, they experience extreme terror.

For the remainder of their lives, they abandon killing, stealing, and even wrong views; some resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, some resolve for the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*, and some resolve for the vehicle of the *śrāvaka*. Thus, he causes all these sentient beings throughout the four continents to cultivate the ten wholesome actions and abide in the three vehicles.
In that state, I made this vow:
"If my aspiration for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi is fulfilled, and if this vow is realized, may all sentient beings in these four continents be established upon the wholesome paths."

"In this manner, throughout all the four continents of this Buddha-field, such terrors were manifested to cause beings to cultivate the karma of the ten paths of wholesome action and establish them in the Three Vehicles; furthermore, within the empty Buddha-fields of the five turbidities throughout the ten directions, they were likewise led to cultivate the ten wholesome karmas and established in the Three Vehicles."
“Good son! My aspirations have been thus fulfilled;
throughout this entire world-system of Coral Wells, I have subdued worldly beings in the form of a yakṣa and established them in wholesome dharmas.”

In this way, throughout the Buddha-fields of the five turbidities as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, I have tamed worldly beings by assuming the form of a yakṣa and established them in the practice of the wholesome path.

Because I have terrified and constrained sentient beings so that they might abide in virtuous conduct, these residual karmic effects have led me to desire the attainment of bodhi; thus, while I sat beneath the Bodhi tree at the Vajrāsana, Māra Pāpīyān brought forth a great host of troops to intimidate me and create obstacles for my bodhisattva practice.
"Good son! This is my brief explanation of the practice of the *dānapāramitā* as a bodhisattva practice.

Without yet having attained profound patience (*kṣānti*), profound dhāraṇīs, or profound samādhis—except for the two previous bodies which attained the five worldly supernormal powers—one establishes such conduct of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa*) and thus exhorts and transforms immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings, causing them to abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
He exhorted and transformed immeasurable, incalculable sentient beings, causing them to attain abiding in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle;
he exhorted and transformed immeasurable, incalculable sentient beings, causing them to attain abiding in the Śrāvaka Vehicle.

Except for the time when I was practicing the conduct of enlightenment, during which I approached as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field and obtained merits from each Buddha equal to drops of the great ocean; I have made offerings to countless Pratyekabuddhas, offered to countless Tathāgatas and Śrāvakas, and likewise made offerings to my parents and ṛṣis possessing the five supernatural powers.
"When I previously practiced the bodhisattva path out of compassion for sentient beings, I satisfied them with my own flesh and blood.
That kind of compassion does not exist now in Arhats."
The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Seven;
The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Eight.
The name of the Tripiṭaka Master is lost; it is now appended to the Qin Records.
Chapter Twenty-Eight: The Assembly of Bodhisattvas “Good son!

Just as I, with my Buddha-eye, behold the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the atoms within the Buddha-lands of the ten directions who have already entered parinirvāṇa—all of whom were those whom I exhorted toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established therein, and all of whom were those whom I first exhorted toward the *dāna-pāramitā* up to the *prajñā-pāramitā* and established therein—even so shall it be said regarding those of the future.”

Furthermore, I see the present Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the east—immeasurable and incalculable in number—who are turning the wheel of the True Dharma and preaching the Dharma for the sake of the multitudes; these are also those whom I first exhorted to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi and established therein, and this applies likewise to the six pāramitās.
The same is said for the south, west, north, and the directions above and below.
"Good son!

I see that to the east, beyond eighty-nine hundred thousand buddha-fields from this buddha-field, there is a world named Flower-Blossom. There dwells the Tathāgata named King of Stainless Virtue and Radiance, currently remaining in the world to preach the Dharma for the sake of the assembly."

That Blessed One was the first to inspire me toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and he was also the first to encourage me in the *dāna-pāramitā* up to the *prajñā-pāramitā*, causing me to abide therein.
To speak briefly: in the eastern direction there is the realm Sukhāvatī, where the Buddha is named Akṣobhya;
there is the realm Marakata, where the Buddha is named Sūryagarbha;
and there is the realm Sukheśvara, where the Buddha is named Sukheśvaracandraprabha.
There is a land called Sun-Sunset, where the Buddha is named Wisdom-Sun;
there is a land called Supreme Rest, where the Buddha is named Dragon-Thunder;
there is a land called Equal Forest, where the Buddha is named Vajra-Fame.
There is a land called Self-King, where the Buddha is named Tiger-Light;
there is a land called No-Desire, where the Buddha is named Sun-Treasury;
there is a land called Illuminating Enemies, where the Buddha is named Renowned Sovereign.
There is a land called Meruprabhā, where the Buddha is named Acintyārāja;
there is a land called Saṃrakṣita, where the Buddha is named Candraguṇagarbha;
there is a land called Puṣpaprabhā, where the Buddha is named Ghoṣavijayaprabha.
There is a land called Peaceful Superior, where the Buddha is named Manifest Peaceful Sovereign Meru;
there is a land called Sustaining King, where the Buddha is named Wisdom Image;
there is a land called Variegated Flower, where the Buddha is named Stainless Eye.
"Good son!

With my Buddha-eye, I behold in the eastern direction such immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently preaching the Dharma. Before they had yet resolved upon bodhicitta, I was the first to exhort them toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and cause them to abide therein;
it was I who first exhorted them in the dāna-pāramitā, and so on, until causing them to abide in the prajñā-pāramitā."
These are the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently dwelling in the world whom I previously led to their presence, and from whom I first received the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

When these words were spoken, the seat of the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabhārāja in the world Puṣpasaṃpuṣṭa shook. Thereupon, the bodhisattvas therein, seeing the seat of the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabhārāja shake, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O Lord!...”
"World-Honored One!
For what cause and for what reason does the seat of the Tathāgata shake?
We have never before seen such a thing."
That Buddha addressed them, saying:
"O sons of noble family!

To the west, passing from this buddha-field through eighty-nine hundred thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Sahā. Its Buddha is named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, who currently resides there, preaching the Dharma of past events for the fourfold assembly."

When that Tathāgata was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path and cultivating the conduct of awakening, he first exhorted me toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, causing me to first resolve my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

When that Tathāgata was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path and performing the deeds of enlightenment, he first exhorted me to practice the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), and I came to abide therein.

Furthermore, when that Tathāgata was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path and cultivating the conduct of awakening, he first brought me to the presence of various Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and caused me to receive the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni is my spiritual friend; he currently dwells in the Sahā world, preaching this Dharma of past events to the fourfold assembly.
It is by the power of that Tathāgata’s majestic virtue that my seat has shaken.
"O sons of good family!
Who among you is able to go to that Sahā Buddha-field and speak these words on my behalf:
'I respectfully inquire after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—whether he is free from illness and affliction, and dwelling in peace and happiness?'"
Those bodhisattvas addressed the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabharāja, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in this Puṣpasaṃkusumita world-system are fully endowed with supernormal powers; they have all crossed to the further shore of the merits of all bodhisattvas.”

"At this present mealtime we have seen a great radiance; these various auspicious omens have come from other lands, the earth has trembled many times, and a rain of myriad exquisite flowers has fallen.
Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"We wish to go to that Sahā world to pay homage, revere, and attend upon the Tathāgata Śākyamuni;
furthermore, we wish to hear the dhāraṇī gateway of entering the practice of all-knowledge."
Those many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, wishing to depart for that land by means of their own supernormal powers, said:
"We do not know where the buddha-field of Śākyamuni Tathāgata in the Sahā world is located."

Then, at that moment, the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabhārāja immediately extended his arm, and from the tips of his five fingers, he emitted various kinds of light. Those rays of light thoroughly illuminated eighty-nine thousand buddha-fields, reaching even as far as this Sahā world.
Those bodhisattvas saw this Sahā world everywhere filled with bodhisattvas, and gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras filling the void of space.
Having seen this, those bodhisattvas addressed the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabharāja once more, saying:
"World-Honored One!
We see that the Sahā buddha-field is entirely filled with bodhisattvas, such that there is not even a small space where a staff could be placed."
Furthermore, they saw that Śākyamuni Tathāgata was looking only at them and preaching the Dharma for their sake.
Then, that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejorāja addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of noble family!
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni regards all with universal equanimity.
O son of good family!
Whether beings in the Sahā world dwell upon the earth or in the void, each and every one of them knows thus: "The Tathāgata Śākyamuni is looking at me alone and is preaching the Dharma for my sake."
"Good son!
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni manifests all forms within his single body and preaches the Dharma for them.

In that buddha-field, those sentient beings who serve Brahmā see the Tathāgata Śākyamuni in the form of Brahmā; they hear the Great Brahmā voice as he preaches the Dharma. This extends to those who serve Māra, Śakra, the Sun, the Moon, śramaṇas, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, or Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and those who serve Maheśvara—he sees the Tathāgata Śākyamuni in the form of Maheśvara and hears the voice of Maheśvara as he preaches the Dharma."

Furthermore, among those sentient beings who have eighty-four thousand kinds of objects of devotion, each perceives the Tathāgata Śākyamuni according to their respective objects of devotion, and hears the Dharma in the same manner.
Within that great assembly were two bodhisattvas: the first was named Lambaka, and the second was named Candraprabha.
The Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejorāja addressed those two bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of good family!
"You may go to the Sahā world and speak these words on my behalf:
'I respectfully inquire after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—whether he is free from illness and affliction, and whether he dwells in peace and comfort.'"
Those bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We see that the entire space above the lands of all those Sahā buddha-fields is completely filled, such that there is not even room for a single person. Where shall we dwell?”
At that time, the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabharāja replied,
"Sons of good family! Do not speak in this way,
saying that there is no place of abiding in the Sahā buddha-field."
The realm of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is exceedingly vast, endowed with the inconceivable merits of a Buddha.

By virtue of his original vows, that Tathāgata’s compassionate ritual methods are most extensive; he teaches the three refuges and the three vehicles, proclaims various precepts, and manifests the three gates of liberation.

Having rescued sentient beings from the three evil realms, he went to the palace of the yakṣa Śailendra-akṣi on Mount Śilā to deliver them; there, dwelling in the Brahmā Cave, he sat cross-legged for seven days, free from strife and experiencing the bliss of liberation.
The body of that Tathāgata filled the Brahma Cave such that there was not even a space the size of four fingers where the body of the Tathāgata did not pervade.

When the seven days had passed, twelve nayutas of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas from the ten directions arrived at that Sahā world and stood before the mountain; they all desired to behold, pay homage to, and draw near to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and furthermore, they wished to hear the Dharma.
"Good son!
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni manifested supernatural powers for that great assembly, causing the Sāla Cave to become exceedingly vast and spacious."
Those twelve nayutas of bodhisattvas entered the Śāla cave and yet found it to be spacious and vast.

Each of those bodhisattvas, having made offerings to the Tathāgata with various bodhisattva supernatural powers, addressed the noble son: "The dwelling place of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is exceedingly broad and capacious."
Thus, having heard what was spoken by Śākyamuni Buddha, those bodhisattvas prostrated themselves at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and each returned to their own land.
Not long after those bodhisattvas had departed, that Śāla cave returned to its former state.

Within it was a Śakra of the four continents named Kauśika, who perceived that his life was nearing its end and that he was destined to fall among the animals; overcome by extreme terror, he went together with eighty-four thousand deities of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven to the Śāla cave where the World-Honored One was staying, and stood before the Śāla cave near the palace of the yakṣa Indrāyudha.
Empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, he immediately conceived this thought:
"I should now invite Pañcaśikha, the son of the gandharva, to extol the World-Honored One with his exquisite voice through song, so that the World-Honored One may arise from samādhi."
Then Śakra went to invite Pañcaśikha, the son of the gandharvas.

Pañcaśikha took his lute and arrived; sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, he praised the World-Honored One with five hundred verses in a gentle voice, playing the lute and singing hymns of praise.
“Good son!

Just as Pañcaśikha praised the World-Honored One, at that very moment, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni entered the Samādhi of the Supreme Radiance Beyond Sound, causing all the yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, gandharvas, and all the devas of the desire realm and the form realm throughout this entire Sahā world to assemble together.”
Among them, those who delighted in the sound of chanting felt great joy upon hearing the chanted voices;
those who delighted in recitation felt a sense of wonder, joy, and reverence toward the World-Honored One upon hearing the words of praise;
and those who delighted in the sound of the lute also felt great joy upon hearing the lute music.
Then, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni arose from samādhi and manifested the entrance of the Sāla Cave; Śakra immediately approached and asked the World-Honored One, "Where shall I sit?"
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni said:
"You yakṣas who have come together here, you may now enter this Sāla cave and sit."
At that time, the cave became twelve times as vast as the sands of the Ganges River, and the great assembly entered that cave and sat down.
Then, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni preached this Dharma for that great assembly.
Among the assembly, those who sought the vehicle of the śrāvakas were explained the vehicle of the śrāvakas; ninety billion sentient beings therein attained the fruit of srotāpanna.
Those who sought the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas were explained the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas.
To those who sought the unsurpassed Buddha-vehicle, he purely expounded the unsurpassed Mahāyāna.
Eighteen *nayutas* of beings, including Pañcaśikha the son of a Gandharva and others, attained the stage of non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Among them, those who had not yet given rise to the mind of the three vehicles did so; some gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, some gave rise to the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*, and some gave rise to the mind of the *śrāvaka* vehicle.
That Kausika Śakra immediately became free from fear; his lifespan increased by a thousand years, and he attained the fruit of *srotāpanna*.

"Good son! The tolerance of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is vast and expansive; likewise, the wheel of that Tathāgata’s voice is also vast and expansive. No one is able to calculate the limits of the Tathāgata’s wheel of voice. That Tathāgata employs vast skillful means to exhort and guide sentient beings; no one is able to know the limits of that Tathāgata’s skillful means."
"Good son!
That Tathāgata’s body is exceedingly tall and vast; none are able to see its crown or know the limits of its form.

Suppose all the beings currently gathered like clouds in this Sahā Buddha-field were to enter the belly of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; they would all be fully accommodated, yet the Tathāgata’s belly would neither increase nor decrease."
Those sentient beings cannot find the limit of that Tathāgata’s abdomen.
Furthermore, all those sentient beings simultaneously enter together into a single pore of that Tathāgata, yet they do not emerge again, nor does [the pore] increase or decrease.
One might wish to seek the limit of a single pore of the Tathāgata, yet none can find it; even the divine eye cannot know it.
Such is the vastness and breadth encompassed by the body of that Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
"Furthermore, noble son!
That buddha-field of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is exceedingly vast and expansive.
Noble son!"
Furthermore, suppose the Buddha-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, were filled with sentient beings just as this Sahā Buddha-field is now.
If all those sentient beings were to come and enter the Sahā Buddha-land at this very moment, they would all be accommodated and received within it.
Why is this? It is because that Tathāgata, when he first initially resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, established this vow.
O son of good family!

Setting aside this world system containing as many grains of sand as there are in one Ganges River, even if all the sentient beings within a thousand Ganges-river-sands of Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions were to fill them just as the sentient beings now fill the Sahā Buddha-land—if all those beings were to enter the Sahā world now, it would be able to contain them all.
This was because that Tathāgata, when first generating the mind of enlightenment, sought unsurpassed wisdom and established such a vow.
Son of good family!
The extent of what is known within the Buddha-field of that Śākyamuni Tathāgata is thus vast and expansive.
By virtue of these four dharmas, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni surpasses all other Tathāgatas.
Noble sons!
You, Candra-sukha-vimala-puṣpa, having seen as you have, go to the western buddha-field of Sahā and speak these words on my behalf:
"Please inquire after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni: Are you free from illness and affliction? Do you dwell in peace and happiness?
At that time, the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejorāja gave the Moon-Bliss Stainless Flower to the Bodhisattvas Rāvaṇa and Candraprabha.
Having granted this, he addressed him, saying:
"O son of good family!
By my supernatural power, I shall go to the Sahā world."
Thereupon, twenty thousand sentient beings among them spoke with one voice to the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
We too, relying on the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, shall go to the Sahā world to pay homage, show respect, and draw near to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
Then, that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabhārāja said:
"Sons of good family,
you may go as you please."

Those two bodhisattvas, Rāvaṇa-kuñjara and Candraprabha, together with twenty thousand bodhisattvas, relying on the supernatural power of that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇaprabharāja, departed from the world-system Padmavikāśita and arrived at this Sahā buddha-field in the time of a single thought-moment. They went to Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”
To the east, passing from here through eighty-nine hundred thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world named Flower-Blossom; its Buddha is named King of Stainless Virtue and Radiance Tathāgata.
That Buddha, in the midst of a great assembly of bodhisattvas, extolled the merits of the Tathāgata, speaking these words:
"In the Sahā world-system there is a Buddha named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, who currently exists."

When that Tathāgata was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path and performing the deeds of awakening, he first inspired me toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established me therein; following his words, I gave rise to the mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
When that Tathāgata was formerly a bodhisattva, he first exhorted me to abide in the *dānapāramitā*, and so forth, as previously described.
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni surpasses all other Tathāgatas by means of these four dharmas.
"That Tathāgata has sent these *candraratnavimalapuṣpa* flowers and inquires:
'Are you free from illness and affliction? Are you dwelling in peace and happiness?
Thus, the seat of Akṣobhya Tathāgata in the world-system Sukhāvatī shook, and all the bodhisattvas present in that assembly saw the seat of Akṣobhya Tathāgata shake.
He immediately dispatched messengers with inquiries, as briefly described above;
this was said in the same manner for every location.

At that time, bodhisattvas sent by immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* Tathāgatas from the east each brought *candrarocavimala* flowers to this Sahā Buddha-field to pay their respects, inquire after the health of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, and to offer worship, reverence, and service while listening to the Dharma.

At that time, the World-Honored One, having just finished reciting the names of the Buddhas in the worlds of the eastern direction, again desired to recite those of the southern direction and spoke these words: "Good son!

I see that to the south, passing from this buddha-field across as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a world named Sarvadaurmanasyāpagata; its Buddha is named Anupakramaṇaguṇa Tathāgata, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma.
When I was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, I first exhorted that Buddha toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and so forth, as previously described.
In the Jambūdvīpaprabhāsa realm, there is the Buddha Dharmaiśvaramegha;
in the Merupratiṣṭhita realm, the Buddha Paramaiśvaryadṛḍhendra; in the Guṇavyūhendrarāja realm, the Buddha Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja;
in the Maṇimukuṭavyūha realm, the Buddha Nārāyaṇagarbha; and in the Raśmipramuñcanasamantāvabhāsa realm, the Buddha Ratnasaṃcayaguṇa.
The Buddha Guṇavikrīḍita; the Buddha Jñānagarbha in the realm Sukhāvatī; the Buddha Jyotiṣprabha in the realm Candanāmūla;
the Buddha Puṇyabalasālendrarāja in the realm Gandhābhigandha; the Buddha Mṛdughoṣasvararāja in the realm Suparikīrtita;
the Buddha Sālendrarājanāmadheya in the realm Prāntavihāra; and [the Buddha] Vajraghoṣa in the realm Vajra.
The Buddha Sovereign Radiance; the Buddha Gentle Sound in the Cloud-Thunder Realm;
the Buddha Jewel-Palm Dragon in the Divided-Jewel Realm; and the Buddha Sovereign of the Dharma-Cloud Moon-Light in the Supreme Jewel-Tree Realm—these are briefly as described previously.
In this way, the seats of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya buddhas in the southern direction shook, and those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, all extolled and praised Tathāgata Śākyamuni.

At that time, Tathāgatas from the southern direction, numbering as many as immeasurable asaṃkhyeyas, dispatched bodhisattvas carrying *candrarocavimala* flowers to this Sahā buddha-field, to pay their respects to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and to listen to the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again, saying: "Good son!

I see that to the west, beyond ninety-seven nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields from this land, there is a world named Śānta. Its Buddha is named Ratnagiri Tathāgata, who currently dwells in the world, preaching the Dharma for the sake of the assembly."
"When I was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, I first exhorted that Buddha toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and so forth, as previously described.
To briefly state their names:

the Buddhas were named Wondrous Light Treasury (*Prabhāsa-garbha*), Sound Wisdom Treasury (*Ghoṣajñāna-garbha*), Vast Renown (*Vipula-yaśas*), Universal Treasury Subduer (*Samanta-garbha-vinīta*), Brahma Flower (*Brahma-puṣpa*), Palm Transcendent (*Karatala-vikrāmin*), Dharma Lamp Radiance (*Dharmapradīpa-prabhāsa*), Peerless Eloquence (*Asama-vākya*), Delight in High Sound (*Uccaghoṣa-rata*), Dissemination King (*Saṃprakāśana-rāja*), and Brahma Lord Voice (*Brahmendraghoṣa*). All of these were as previously described.
In this way, the seats of all the immeasurable asaṃkhyeya Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the western quarter—whose names the Tathāgata Śākyamuni has proclaimed—all shook.

At that time, immeasurable asaṃkhyeya buddhas from the western direction dispatched bodhisattvas carrying *candrarati-vimala* flowers to this Sahā buddha-field; having arrived, they each sat down to listen to the Dharma.
To speak briefly:
it is the same for the north, the zenith, the nadir, the southeast, the southwest, and the northwest, as described above.
Then, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, wishing to speak further regarding the northeast, spoke these words:

“Good son! I see that to the northeast, passing from this buddha-field through ninety-eight billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddha-fields, there is a world named Free from Dust. The Buddha there is named Saroruharāja Tathāgata, King of the Śāla Trees, whose fame is vast and who has risen above all sorrow and affliction.”

When I was originally practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva and performing the practices for awakening, I first exhorted that Tathāgata toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and caused him to abide in the six *pāramitās*.
I first brought them to the presence of the Buddhas so that they might receive the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

As their names were proclaimed, their seats all shook; even as I spoke of the eighty-four thousand kinds of deliverance for sentient beings, each heard the sound according to their own circumstances and beheld the Tathāgata Śākyamuni hearing such a Dharma.
Within that assembly were two bodhisattvas: the first was named Mountain Honey, and the second was named Equally Joyful Aspiration.
At that time, the Tathāgata Saroruhavimala-viśālakīrti-śālarāja addressed those two bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of good family!..."
Go to that Sahā world and, in my name, inquire of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni:
"Are you free from illness and affliction? Do you dwell in peace and well-being?"
They addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We see that the land and the space of that Sahā buddha-field are entirely filled, such that there is not even room for a single person; where shall we dwell?”
That Tathāgata said:
"Good son! Do not speak in this way."
"In the Sahā Buddha-field, there is no place to dwell. "Noble son!
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni is vast and spacious in his acceptance [of beings], and is endowed with inconceivable Buddha-merits."

That Tathāgata, by virtue of his original vows, possesses a compassionate manner and a vast capacity for inclusion; he teaches the three refuges and the Dharma of the three vehicles, proclaims the three types of precepts and manifests the three gates of liberation, and delivers sentient beings from the three evil realms, establishing them in the three good paths.
"Good son!

Not long after that Tathāgata Śākyamuni attained Buddhahood, he sat cross-legged for seven days at the Sāla Cave in the palace of the yakṣa Indrākṣa on Mount Madhyamaśilā, dwelling in the joy of liberation without conflict for the sake of sentient beings."
The body of that Tathāgata filled the Śāla cave; within that cave, there was not even a space the size of four fingers that was not filled by the body of the Tathāgata.

When the seven days had passed, twelve nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas from the ten directions arrived at that Sahā world and stood before the mountain to pay homage and revere the Tathāgata Śākyamuni; furthermore, by means of these four dharmas, that Śākyamuni Buddha excels all other Tathāgatas.
"Good sons!

Take these Moon-like Joyful Stainless Flowers and, as you have seen, go to the Sahā Buddha-field in the southwest to respectfully inquire of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni whether he has little illness and little affliction, and whether he dwells in peace and happiness."

At that time, the Tathāgata Saralarāja, Free from Sorrow, Distress, Leaping Upward, and Vast Renown, took a moon-like, joyous, and stainless flower and gave it to the Bodhisattvas Śailamadhura and Ratisamagati, saying:
"Noble sons!..."
"Relying upon my supernatural power, go to the Sahā world-system.
At that time, twenty thousand people spoke with one voice, saying:
"We too, relying upon the Tathāgata’s supernatural power, shall go to the Sahā Buddha-field to pay homage, show respect, and draw near to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
That Tathāgata said:
"O sons of good family!
You may go as you please."

Those two bodhisattvas, together with twenty thousand bodhisattvas, relying on the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, set out from the Vimala world-system and, in the space of a single thought-moment, arrived here at Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain in this Sahā Buddha-field. With palms joined in reverence, they addressed Śākyamuni Tathāgata, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”
In the northeast there is a Buddha, as previously described.
That Buddha has sent these Moon-like Joyful Stainless Flowers to respectfully inquire after the World-Honored One: whether he is free from illness and affliction, and dwelling in peace and happiness?

"In this way, when the seat of the Tathāgata Mārapramardaka shook, the bodhisattvas assembled there saw that the seat of the Tathāgata Mārapramardaka had shaken; they immediately asked the Tathāgata about the cause and conditions for it, as previously described."
In this way, there were the Buddha Śālendrarāja, the Buddha Mahābalaprabha, the Buddha Padmottara, the Buddha Candanamerurāja, the Buddha Sāgarāpāraprabhāsa, and the Buddha Jñānabala.
At that time, from the northeast, these immeasurable asaṃkhyeya Tathāgatas each dispatched two bodhisattvas carrying *candra-sukha-vimala* flowers to this Sahā buddha-field.
They pay their respects and inquire after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, making offerings, honoring, and attending upon him to hear the Dharma.

Chapter Twenty-nine: Entering the Gate of Samādhi *Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, Chapter Twenty-nine: Entering the Gate of Samādhi At that time, regarding all sentient beings who had gathered in this Sahā Buddha-field, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, by means of his supernormal powers, caused each and every sentient being to become as large as a mustard seed.

In this way, sentient beings fill and crowd the land and the space of the Sahā buddha-field until it is so densely populated that there is not even room for a single hair; yet those sentient beings do not see one another, seeing only empty space.

Furthermore, all stone mountains, Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, and the barrier mountains—from the celestial palaces above down to the Golden Wheel below—are entirely without obstruction.
The eyes of sentient beings saw only the Tathāgata Śākyamuni entering the Samādhi of the Uninterrupted Dharma Pervading All Space.

At that time, the Tathāgata drew all the *candra-sukha-vimala-puṣpa* (moon-joy-stainless-flower) hairs from within his pores; all those sentient beings who had gathered in the Sahā world were able to see those [other] sentient beings.
Setting aside contemplation of the Buddha’s physical form and mind, one contemplates every pore of the Tathāgata.

Within each pore, one sees various gardens and ponds, various jewel-trees, and various flowers and fruits with luxuriant branches and leaves; there are various pavilions, various garments, and various banners, canopies, standards, pennants, and *kiyūras*, adorned with pearls and necklaces. These trees are as magnificent as the flourishing groves of the World of Peace and Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
At that time, all sentient beings thought to themselves:
"We should now go to behold the groves.

Then, all sentient beings gathered in this Sahā world entered through the pores of the Tathāgata’s body and sat within them, with the sole exception of those in the hells, the hungry ghosts, the animals, and the formless heavens.
At that time, the World-Honored One withdrew his supernormal powers, and all those sentient beings were able to see one another;
they immediately asked each other, "Where is the Tathāgata Śākyamuni now?"
Then Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the great assembly, saying:
"Ho! You sentient beings!
You should all know that we have now all gathered within the belly of the Tathāgata."
Each of them saw the internal and external physical marks of that Tathāgata’s body, and then they came to know that he was gathered within the Tathāgata’s belly.
They all thought to themselves:
"How did we enter the Tathāgata’s belly?"
"Who has taken us and placed us within the Tathāgata’s belly?
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the great assembly with a loud voice:
"You all should listen: this is not the power of anyone else; it is the supernatural transformation of the Tathāgata, performed for the sake of benefiting us."
“The World-Honored One shall now preach the Dharma; you all should listen with single-minded attention and reflect upon it well.
At that time, the great assembly joined their palms in reverence and gazed up at the World-Honored One.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke the *Sarvadharmanayanirdeśasūtra*.
What is the *Sarvadharmanayanirdeśasūtra*?
It refers to crossing the abyss of birth and death, entering the Eightfold Noble Path, and fulfilling all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Within natural wisdom there are ten matters:
first, to resolve the mind with utmost sincerity and dedicate it toward liberation;
second, to give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings.
Third, to gather all sentient beings with a mind of benefit;
fourth, to deliver those not yet delivered like a great shipmaster;
fifth, to liberate those not yet liberated from their various inversions.
Sixth, they let out the great lion’s roar to startle and move all sentient beings, causing them to contemplate the dharma of non-self;
seventh, they travel through all worlds, awakening to all dharmas as being like illusions, dreams, and reflections;
eighth, they adorn and embellish all worlds with the power of the body of pure precepts.
Ninth, accomplishing the ten powers of a Tathāgata and fulfilling all the pāramitās;
tenth, practicing as taught in order to possess the four fearlessnesses and attain the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.

There are no other bodhisattvas who, having heard the Dharma as it was taught, practice it all in its entirety to eliminate worldly delusion; this is called the "Sutra on the Practice of the Dharma-Gate of All Ten Matters."

Knowing the gate of practice that reaches the signless, one contemplates all phenomena as being without self and without arising or ceasing; this is non-retrogression, non-reversal, non-interruption, non-permanence, non-abandonment, and non-attainment.

When this Dharma was being taught, eighty billion beings, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, immediately attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within the Tathāgata’s belly.
Among them, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas beyond counting attained various samādhis, dhāraṇīs, and patiences.
Then, they all emerged once more from the pores of the Tathāgata’s body, having experienced what was unprecedented within the Tathāgata.
Having prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata, each returned to their own land in the ten directions.

As for the Bodhisattvas of the eastern direction who truly desired to seek out the sound-circle and physical marks of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, those eastern Bodhisattvas proceeded further and further until they had passed through immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* Buddha-lands in the east, yet still had not reached the end.

The sound from the wheel of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s voice was heard there in such a way that its words, phrases, and meanings were all complete and perfect, no different from sitting before the Tathāgata Śākyamuni himself to listen to the Dharma.
They were likewise unable to know any increase or decrease in the body of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.

Wherever they went, they saw the body of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni appearing before them, and they also saw immeasurable asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas and śrāvakas entering and exiting from a single pore of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s body without obstruction.
Each and every pore is likewise; even seeing sentient beings entering and exiting within all the pores is likewise so, and it is explained in the same way for the ten directions.

At that time, the great assembly who had been within the Tathāgata’s belly all emerged from the pores of the Tathāgata’s body. They prostrated with their heads at the feet of the World-Honored One, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and stood before the Tathāgata. With verses of exquisite beauty, complete in both phrasing and meaning, they simultaneously offered praise and eulogy to the Tathāgata.

At that time, the devas of the desire and form realms rained down various exquisite flowers, flower garlands, and fragrant ointments from the midst of the void; they performed celestial music and suspended heavenly silks, banners, canopies, standards, pennants, robes, and head-coverings, as well as pearls and necklaces, to make offerings to the Tathāgata.

Chapter Thirty: Entrustment The Mahāyāna Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Chapter Thirty: Entrustment At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Abhayasamādhi who, with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"What shall this great prophecy be called?
How should it be upheld?
The Buddha said:
"The first is named 'The Dharma Gate of the Dhāraṇī for Entering the Practice of All-Knowledge';
the second is named 'The Treasury of All Buddhas';
the third is named 'The Great Collection'."
The fourth is titled "Bestowing the Prediction upon Bodhisattvas";
the fifth is titled "Entering the Path of Fearlessness";
the sixth is titled "Entering All Samādhis."
The seventh is named "Manifesting All Buddha-lands";
the eighth is named "Like the Great Ocean";
the ninth is named "Beyond Number."
"The tenth is named 'The Great Compassion White Lotus.
He addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"Yes, World-Honored One!"
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family should receive,
uphold, read, recite, and explain this sutra to others— even if only a single four-line verse— how much merit would they obtain?
The Buddha said:
"I have already previously explained the merit of this sutra; now I shall briefly explain it for you.
If there are good sons or good daughters!"

If one upholds this sutra—reciting it, copying it, or explaining it to others, even if only a single four-line verse—the merit obtained by that person exceeds that of a bodhisattva who has practiced the six pāramitās for ten great kalpas.

Why is this so? Because this sutra is able to extinguish and eliminate the malevolent minds of all devas, worldlings, Brahmās, Māras, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, nāgas, gandharvas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, kiṃnaras, asuras, and others.
Furthermore, it can eliminate all diseases, conflicts, enmities, and jealousies;
it can eliminate untimely evil winds, frost, hail, and torrential rains;
and it can eliminate epidemics and famine, bringing about peace and security so that there is constant abundance and joy.
It causes people to become robust and brings joy to assemblies; it reconciles those who are discordant; it bestows the bliss of fearlessness upon those who are terrified;
it can extinguish the fetters and latent tendencies while increasing roots of goodness;
and it enables those in the three evil realms to escape the limits of all suffering.
Furthermore, they are able to manifest the wondrous path of the Three Vehicles;
they can enable people to attain samādhi, dhāraṇī, and patience;
and they are able to benefit all sentient beings.
They are able to sit upon the Vajra-seat and destroy the four Māras;
they are able to awaken to the factors conducive to enlightenment and turn the Wheel of Dharma;
and for those sentient beings who lack the seven noble riches, they are able to cause them to attain abundance through the Bodhisattva teachings.
Desiring to lead many sentient beings into the city of fearlessness, I have expounded this Dharma; to whom now should I entrust this Dharma?

Who is able, in the midst of the evil age to come, to proclaim this Dharma so that non-retrogressive Bodhisattvas in all directions may hear and know it, and so that sentient beings may eliminate their attachment to what is not the Dharma, their craving for fame and profit, and their adherence to views of wrong dharma, thereby completely extinguishing all thoughts of no karmic fruition?
At that time, the entire great assembly knew the mind of the Tathāgata. Among those seated was a yakṣa-ṛṣi named Namirvatsa.
Then Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva took Namirvatsa by the arm and led him to the place where the World-Honored One was.
The Buddha said:

"Great Seer, you shall receive and uphold this Dharma, and even in future evil ages, you shall widely proclaim and disseminate it so that all Bodhisattvas of non-retrogression in every direction may hear and know it; those who hear it shall abide in the mind of non-retrogression."
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!

By virtue of my original vow, I have been a yakṣa-ṛṣi for eighty-four thousand great kalpas while practicing the bodhisattva path; I have exhorted countless sentient beings to dwell in the four Brahma-abodes and abide on the stage of non-retrogression.”
“World-Honored One!

If there are sentient beings who, in the future evil age, are able to receive, uphold, copy, read, and recite this sutra, or even explain a single four-line verse to others, I shall personally protect them, ensuring that no one can cause that Dharma-preacher any affliction.”
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the great assembly—the devas, nāgas, gandharvas, asuras, and human beings—having heard the sutra, rejoiced, paid their respects, and departed.
